definition: is a conditional and partitive and corroborative particle;
sourceDefinition: is a conditional and partitive and corroborative particle; and is sometimes written A^ayomaA , by the change of the first m into Y . (Mughnee, K.) ― -b2- It is used as a conditional particle in the words of the Kur [ii.24], fA^am~aA Al~a*iyna A=manuwA fayaEolamuwna A^an~ahu AloHaq~u mino rab~ihimo waA^am~aA Al~a*iyna kafaruwA fayaquwluwna maA *aA A^araAda All~`hu bih*aA mavalAF [ For as for those who have believed, they know that it is the truth from their Lord; but as for those who have disbelieved, they say, What is it that God meaneth by this as a parable ?]. (Mughnee,* K,* TA.) That it denotes a condition is shown by the necessary occurrence of f after it; for if this f were a conjunction, it would not be prefixed to the enunciative; and if it were redundant, it might be dispensed with; but it may not be dispensed with except in a case of necessity in poetry or in a case of an ellipsis. ― -b3- In most cases, (Mughnee, K,) it is used as a partitive, (S, Mughnee, K,) implying the meaning of a condition; (S; [in which it is mentioned with A^amaA ;]) and thus it is used in the passage of the Kur cited above; (Mughnee;) and in the following exs. [in the Kur xviii. 78 and 79 and 81], A^am~aA Als~afiynapu fakaAnato limasaAkiyna yaEomaluwna fiY AlbaHori and waA^amaA AlogulaAmu fakaAna A^abawaAhu muw^ominiyna and wA^am~aA AlojidaAru fakaAna liglaAmayni yataymayoni [ As for the ship, it belonged to poor men who worked on the sea . . . and as for the boy, his two parents were believers . . . and as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys ]. (Mughnee, * K, * TA.) [It is a partitive also in the phrase A^am~aAbaEodu , which see in art. bEd .] ― -b4- Few have mentioned its use as a corroborative: (Mughnee:) it is thus used in the phrase A^am~aA zayodN fa*aAhibN [ Whatever be the case, or happen what will or what may, or at all events, Zeyd is going away ], when you mean that Zeyd is inevitably going away, and determined, or decided, upon doing so: (Z cited in the Mughnee, and K:) therefore Sb explains it as meaning, in this case, mahomaA yakuno mino $aYo'K [ whatever be the case, &c., as above, or, in some instances, happen what would or what might ]; thereby showing it to be a corroborative, and to have a conditional meaning: (Z cited in the Mughnee: [and the same explanation of it is given, with a similar ex., in the S, in art. Amw :]) the fa , in this case, is transferred from its proper place before the inchoative, and put before the enunciative. (I 'AK p. 306.) Ks says that A^am~aA is used in commanding and forbidding and announcing: you say, A^am~aA All~`ha faAEobudo [ Whatever be the case, or happen what will, &c., God worship thou ]: and A^am~aA Alxamora falaA ta$orabohaA [i. e. A^am~aA Alxamora falaA ta$orabohaA (as is shown in the case of a similar ex. in the Mughnee, though you may say A^am~aA Alxamoru falaA ta$orabohaA , without an ellipsis, like as you say A^m~aA vamuwdu fahadayonaAhumo as well as A^am~aA vamuwda , in the Kur xli. 16, accord. to different readers,) Whatever be the case, &c., wine (drink not), drink not thou it ]: and A^am~aA zayodN faxaraja [ Whatever be the case, &c., with respect to other things, Zeyd has gone forth; or whatever be the case with respect to others, as for Zeyd, he has gone forth ]: whereas A_im~aA [which see in the next paragraph] is used in expressing a condition and in expressing doubt and in giving option and in taking option. (T.) ― -b5- [IHsh says that in his opinion,] in the phrase A^am~aA AlEabiyda fa*uw EabiydK , thus heard, with AlEbyd in the accus. case, the meaning is, mahamA *akarota [&c., i. e. Whenever thou mentionest the slaves, he is a possessor of slaves: but I would rather say that the meaning is, A^am~aA *ikoruka AlEabiyda , &c., i. e. as for thy mentioning the slaves, &c.]: and so in similar phrases which have been heard. (Mughnee.) -A2- Distinct from the foregoing is A^am~aA in the saying in the Kur [xxvii. 86], A^am~aA *Akunotumo taEmaluwna [ Or rather, what is it that ye were doing? ]: for here it is a compound of the unconnected A^amo and the interrogative maA (Mughnee.) -A3- So too in the saying of the poet, A^abaA xuraA$apa A^am~aA A^anota *aA nasfarK faA_n~a quwomiYa lamo taA^kulohumu AlD~abuEu [ O Aboo-Khurásheh, because thou wast possessor of a number of men dost thou boast? Verily, my people, the year of dearth, or of sterility, hath not consumed them ]: for here it is a compound of the A^ano termed maSudariy~ap [which combines with a verb following it to form an equivalent to an inf. n.] and the redundant maA : A^am~aA A^anota is for liA^ano kunota ; the preposition and the verb are suppressed for the sake of abridgment, so that the pronoun [ ta in kunota ] becomes separate; and maA is substituted for the verb [thus deprived of its affixed pronoun], and the n [of An ] is incorporated into the m [of mA ]. (Mughnee.) [See another reading of this verse voce A_im~aA ; and there also, immediately after, another ex. (accord. to the Mughnee) of A^am~aA used in the manner explained above. See also A^ano as a conditional particle, like A_ino .] -A4- Also i. q. A_im~aA , q. v. (Mughnee, K.)

(M, K.) ― -b2- It denotes doubt; (Ks, T, Mughnee, K;) as in maA A^adoriY mano qaAma A_im~aA zayodNwA_im~aA EamorNw [ I know not who stood: either Zeyd or 'Amr ]: (Ks, T:) and jaA='aniY A_im~aA zayodN waA_im~aA EamorNw [ There came to me either Zeyd or 'Amr ], said when one knows not which of them came. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b3- It also denotes vagueness of meaning; as in [the Kur ix. 107,] A_im~aA yuEa*~ibuhum wA^m~aA yatuwbu Ealayohimo [ Either He will punish them or He will turn unto them with forgiveness ]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b4- It also denotes giving option; as in [the Kur xviii. 85,] A_im~aA A^an tuEa*~iba wA_im~aA A^ano tat~axi*a fiyihimo HusonAF [ Either do thou punish, or do thou what is good to them ]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b5- It also denotes the making a thing allowable; as in taEal~amo A_im~aA fiqohFA wA_im~aA naHowFA [ Learn thou either low or syntax; (an ex. given in the T, on the authority of Ks, as an instance of the usage of A_im~aA to denote giving option;)] but its use with this intent is disputed by some, (Mughnee, K,) while they assert it of A^awo . (Mughnee.) ― -b6- It is also used as a partitive; as in [the Kur lxxvi. 3,] A_m~aA $aAkirAF w A_m~aA kafuwrFA [ Either, or whether, being thankful or being unthankful ]; (Mughnee, K;) the two epithets being here in the accus. case as denotatives of state: or, accord. to the Koofees, A_m~aA may be here [a compound of] the conditional A_ino and the redundant maA ; kaAna , accord. to Ibn-EshShejeree, being understood after it: (Mughnee:) and Fr says that the meaning is, A_ino $akara waA_ino kafara [ if he be thankful and if he be unthankful ]. (T.) ― -b7- It also denotes taking option; as in the saying, liY daArN biAlkuwfapi faA^naA xaArijN A_layohaA faA_m~aA A^ano A^asokunahaA wA_im~aA A^ano A^abiyEahaA [ I have a house in El-Koofeh, and I am going forth to it, and either I will inhabit it or I will sell it: but this is similar to the usage first mentioned above]. (Ks, T.) ― -b8- It is a conjunction, (S in art. Amw , and Mughnee,) accord. to most authorities, i. e., the second A_im~aA in the like of the saying, jaA'aniY A_m~aA zayodN wA_im~aA EamorNw [mentioned above]; (Mughnee;) used in the manner of A^awo in all its cases except this one, that in the use of Aw you begin with assurance, and then doubt comes upon you; whereas you begin with A_im~aA in doubt, and must repeat it; as in the saying last mentioned: (S: [and the like is said in the Mughnee, after the explanations of the meanings:]) but some assert that it is like the first A_im~aA , not a conjunction; because it is generally preceded by the conjunction w : and some assert that A_im~aA conjoins the noun with the noun, and the w conjoins A_im~aA with A_im~aA ; but the conjoining of a particle with a particle is strange. (Mughnee.) ― -b9- Sometimes the w is suppressed; as in the following verse, (Mughnee,) of El-Ahwas; (S;) yaA layotamaA A^um~uniA $aAlato naEaAmatuhaA A^ayomaA A_ilaY jan~apK A^ayomaA A_ilaY naAri [ O, would that our mother took her departure, either to Paradise or Hell-fire! ]; (S,* Mughnee, K;) cited by Ks, with AymA for A_im~aA : (T:) and sometimes it is with kesr [i. e. A_iymaA ]: (S:) IB says that it is correctly A_im~aA , with kesr; asserting the original to be A_im~aA , with kesr, only. (TA.) ― -b10- And sometimes the former maA is dispensed with; as in the following verse, (Mughnee,) which shows also that maA is sometimes suppressed; saqatohu Ar~awaAEidu mino Say~ifK waA_ino mino xariyfK falano yaEodamaA [ The thundering clouds of summer-rain watered him, or of autumn-rain; so he will not want sufficient drink]: i. e. A_im~aA mino Say~ifK waA_im~aA mino xariyfK . (Mughnee, K.) Mbr and As say that A_ino is here conditional, and that the f is its complement: but this assertion is of no weight; for the object is the description of a mountain-goat as having sufficient drink in every case: AO says that A_ino in this verse is redundant. (Mughnee.) ― -b11- Sometimes, also, one does not require to mention the second A_im~aA , by mentioning what supplies its place; as in the saying, A_im~aA A^ano tatakal~ama bixayorK waA_il~aA fAsokuto [ Either do thou speak what is good or else be silent ]. (Mughnee.) [See art. AlA , near its end.] -A2- Distinct from the foregoing is A_im~aA in the saying in the Kur [xix. 26], faA_im~aA^itaryin~a mina Aloba$ari A^aHadFAi [ And if thou see, of mankind, any one ]: for this is [a compound of] the conditional A_in and the redundant maA . (S * in art. Amw , and Mughnee.) [In like manner,] you say, in expressing a condition, A_im~aA ta$otiman~a zoydFA faA_in~ahu yaHolumu Eanoka [ If thou revile Zeyd, he will treat thee with forbearance ]. (Ks, T.) And A_im~aA taA^otiniy A^ukoirimoka [ If thou come to me, I will treat thee with honour ]. (S.) ― -b2- In the following saying, A_im~aA A^anota munoTaliqFA AnoTalaqotu [ If thou be going away, I go away ], the maA is not that which restrains the particle to which it is subjoined from governing, but is a substitute for a verb; (K and TA in art. maA ;) as though the speaker said, A_i*aA Sirota munoTaliqFA [or rather A_ino Sirota ]. (TA in that art.) And hence the saying of the poet, [of which a reading different from that here following has been given voce A^am~aA ,] A^abaA xuraA$apa A_im~aA A^anota *aA nasfarK faA_n~a qawomiYa lamo taA_okulohumu AlD~abugu [ O Aboo-Khurásheh, if thou be possessor of a number of men, verily, my people, the year of dearth, or of sterility, hath not consumed them ]; as though he said, A_ino kunotu *aA nafarK . (TA in that art.) [But IHsh states the case differently; saying,] An instance of A^am~aA A^anota munTaliqFA AnoTalaqotu not used to restrain from governing, but as a substitute for a verb, occurs in the saying, A^am~aA A^anota munTaliqFA AinoTalaqotu [ Because thou wast going away, I went away ]; originally, AinoTalaqotu liA^ano kunota munTaliqAF : [for an explanation of which, see what is said of A^am~aA A^anota in a reading of the verse commencing with A^abaA xuraA$ap voce A^am~aA :] but accord. to El-Fárisee and IJ, the government belongs to maA ; not to kaAna [or kunota ]. (Mughnee in art. maA .) ― -b3- So too in the saying, AifoEalo h*aA A_im~aAlaA , meaning A_ino kunota laAtafoEalu gayorahu [i. e. Do thou this if thou wilt not do another thing; or do thou this at least ]; (Mughnee and K, each in art. maA ;) indicating a person's refusal to do [fully] that which he is ordered to do: (TA in that art.:) or A_im~aAlaA faAfoEalo ka*aA , meaning if thou wilt not do that, then do thou this; the three particles [ A_ino and maA and laA ] being made as one word: so says Lth: (T:) [J says,] A_im~aAlaA faAfoEalo ka*aA is pronounced with imáleh, [i. e. “ immá-lè, ”] and is originally A_in laA with maA as a connective; and the meaning is, if that thing will not be, then do thou thus: (S in art. laA :) [but] AHát [disallows this pronunciation, and] says, sometimes the vulgar, in the place of AifoEalo *`lika A_im~aAlaA , say, AifoEalo *`lika baAriY [ Do thou that at least ]; but this is Persian, and is rejected as wrong: and they say also, A^um~aAlaYo , with damm to the A [and with imáleh in the case of the final vowel, and thus it is vulgarly pronounced in the present day]; but this too is wrong; for it is correctly A_im~aAlaA , [with kesr, and] not pronounced with imáleh, for particles [in general] are not thus pronounced: (T:) and the vulgar also convert the hemzeh into h with damm [saying hum~aAlaYo ]. (TA in art. maA .) [Fei says,] laA is a substitute for the verb in the saying, A_im~aAlaA faAfoEalo h`*aA , the meaning being If thou do not that, then [ at least ] do thou this: the origin thereof is this; that certain things are incumbent on a man to do, and he is required to do them, but refuses; and then one is content with his doing some, or a part, of them, and says to him thus: i. e., if thou wilt not do all, then do thou this: then the verb is suppressed, on account of the frequency of the usage of the phrase, and maA is added to give force to the meaning: and some say that it is for this reason that laA is here pronounced with imáleh; because it serves for the verb; like as balaY is, and the vocative yaA : but it is said that it is correctly pronounced without imáleh; because particles [in general] are not pronounced therewith; as Az says. (Msb in art. laA .) [El-Hareeree says that] A_im~aAlaA is properly [a compound of] three particles, which are A_ino and maA and laA , made as one word, and the A at the end thereof is like the A of HubaAraY [in which it is written Y , agreeably with rule]; wherefore it is pronounced with imáleh, like as is the A of this latter word. (Durrat el-Ghowwás, in De Sacy's Anthol. Gr. Ar. p. 57 of the Arabic text.) In the Lubáb it is said that laA is used as a negative of the future, as in lA tafoEalo ; and the verb [in A_im~aAlaA ] is suppressed; so it [ lA ] serves as a substitute in the saying, AifoEalo h`*aA A_im~aAlaA ; therefore they pronounce its A with imáleh: and IAth says that the Arabs sometimes pronounced laA with a slight imáleh; and the vulgar make the imáleh thereof full, so that its A becomes Y ; but this is wrong. (TA.) You say also, xu*o h`*aA A_im~aAlaA , meaning Take thou this if thou take not that. (T.) It is related that the Prophet saw a runaway camel, and said, “ To whom belongeth this camel? ” when, lo, some young men of the Ansár said, “ We have drawn water upon him during twenty years, and yet he has in him fat; so we desired to slaughter him; but he escaped from us. ” He said, “ Will ye sell him? ” They answered, “ No: but he is thine. ” And he said, A_im~aAlaA fA^aHosinuwA A_ilayohi Hat~aY yA^otiyahu A^ajaluhu , meaning If ye will not sell him, act well to him until his term of life come to him. (T.)

[El-Hareeree says that] A_im~aAlaA is properly [a compound of] three particles, which are A_ino and maA and laA , made as one word, and the A at the end thereof is like the A of HubaAraY [in which it is written Y , agreeably with rule]; wherefore it is pronounced with imáleh, like as is the A of this latter word. It is related that the Prophet saw a runaway camel, and said, “ To whom belongeth this camel? ” when, lo, some young men of the Ansár said, “ We have drawn water upon him during twenty years, and yet he has in him fat; so we desired to slaughter him; but he escaped from us. ” He said, “ Will ye sell him? ” They answered, “ No: but he is thine. ” And he said, A_im~aAlaA fA^aHosinuwA A_ilayohi Hat~aY yA^otiyahu A^ajaluhu , meaning If ye will not sell him, act well to him until his term of life come to him. (T.)

sourceDefinition: , meaning Yesterday, or the day before the present day (Msb, K) by one night, (K,) and tropically applied to (tropical:) what is before that, (Msb,) or a short time before, (Bd in x. 25,) [used as a subst. and as an adv.,] is indecl., with any of the three vowels for its termination: (K:) [written A^amosi and A^mosa and A^mosu :] or it is an adv. n., indecl., with kesr for its termination, unless made indeterminate, or made determinate [be the article Al ]; and sometimes indecl. with fet-h: (EzZejjájee, M, TA:) or, accord. to I Hsh, the termination with fet-h is a rejected form; and that with damm is not mentioned by any of the grammarians: (TA:) but mu*o A^amosa [ Since yesterday ] occurs, used by poetic licence: (Sb, S:) A^amos is a noun of which the last letter is made movent to avoid the concurrence of two quiescent letters: and the Arabs differ respecting it: (S:) most of them make it indecl., with kesr for its termination, when it is determinate [without the article Al ]: but some of them make it [imperfectly] decl. when it is determinate [in the same manner]: (S, K: *) [accord. to the most approved usage,] you say, [ raA^ayotuhu A^amosi , and biAlA^amosi , which is more common, and AlA^amosa , I saw him yesterday; and] maA raA^ayotuhu mu*oA^amosi [ I have not seen him since yesterday ]; and if you have not seen him [since the day next] before that, you say, maA raA^ayotuhu mu*o A^aw~alu mino A^amosi [ I have not seen him since the day before yesterday ]; and if you have not seen him [since] two days before that, you say, maA raA^ayotuhu mu*o A^aw~alu mino A^aw~ala mino A^amosi [ I have not seen him since the day before the day before yesterday ]. (ISk, TA.) The phrase raA^ayotuhu A^amosK [ I saw him yesterday ] has also been heard, but it is extr. (K.) The people of El-Hijáz make A^amos indecl., with kesr for its termination; and the Benoo-Temeem do the same when it is in the accus. or gen. case; but these latter make it [imperfectly] decl. when it is in the nom. case, saying, *ahaba A^amosu bimaA fiyhi [ Yesterday has gone with what happened during it ]; whereas the people of El-Hijáz say, *ahaba A^amosi bimaA fiyhi , because it is [held by them to be] indecl. on account of its implying that it has the determinative article Al [understood as prefixed to it], the kesreh being added to avoid the concurrence of two quiescent letters; while the Benoo-Temeem hold it to be, in the nom. case, a deviation from AlA_amosu , and therefore imperfectly decl., because of its being determinate, [and so resembling a proper name,] and its deviation from the original form, like saHaru in the like case: (IB, TA:) all of the Arabs, however, make it decl. when the article Al is prefixed to it, (S, K, *) and when it is made indeterminate, or is prefixed to another noun: (S:) they say, using it indeterminately, kul~u gadK SaAy^irN A^amosKA [ Every morrow becomes a yesterday ]; (S, * IB;) and making it determinate by the article Al , they say, kaAna AlA^amosu Tay~ibFA [ The yesterday was good ], (IB,) and maDay AlA^amosu AlmubaAraku [ The blessed yesterday has past ]; (S;) and prefixing it to another noun, kul~u A^amosinaA kaAna Tay~ibFA [ All of our yesterday was good ], (IB,) and maDaY A^amosunaA [ Our yesterday has past ]: (S:) [therefore,] in the following verse, waA_in~iY waqafotu Alyawoma waAlA^amosi qabolahu bibaAbika Hat~aY kaAdati Al$~amosu tagorubu [ And verily I stood to-day, and yesterday before it, at thy door until the sun was almost setting ], (thus related by IAar in two different ways, AlA^amosi and AlA^amosa ,) if we read AlA^amosi , the Al is redundant, because it is implied in the word A^amosi ; but if we read AlA^amosa , the Al is not implied in A^amosa , and therefore is prefixed to make it determinate. (IJ, M.) The pl. is A=musN and A=maAsN , (Zj, K,) both pls. of pauc., (Zj, TA,) and A^muwsN , (Zj, K, TA, [in the CK, incorrectly, AmuwosN ,]) which is a pl. of mult. (Zj, TA.) There is no dim. form of A^amos ; like as there is none of gadN and AlbaAriHapu and kayofa and A^ayona and mataY and A^aY~u and maA and Einda and the names of the months and those of the days of the week, except AljumoEapu . (Sb, S.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (T, Msb, K,) inf. n. A^amonN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and A_imonN (Zj, M, K) and A^amanN (M, K) and A^amanapN (T, S, M, K) and A_imonapN (T) and A^amaAnN (M, K) [and app. A^amaAnapN , for it is said in the S that this is syn. with A^amaAnN ,] and A=mnN , an instance of an inf. n. of the measure faAEilN , which is strange, (MF,) or this is a subst. like faAlijN , (M,) He was, or became, or felt, secure, safe, or in a state of security or safety; originally, he was, or became, quiet, or tranquil, in heart, or mind; (Msb;) he was, or became, secure, or free from fear; A^amonN signifying the contr. of xawofN , (S, M, K,) and so A^amanapN (S) and A=minN [&c.]: (M, K:) he was, or became, or felt, free from expectation of evil, or of an object of dislike or hatred, in the coming time; originally, he was, or became, easy in mind, and free from fear. (El-Munáwee, TA.) [See A^amonN , below.] You say also, yaA_omanu EalaY nafosihi [ He is secure, or safe, or free from fear, for himself ]. (M.) And A^amina Albaladu , meaning The inhabitants of the country or district, or town, were in a state of security, or confidence, therein. (Msb.) The verb is trans. by itself, and by means of the particle mino ; as in A^amana zayodN AlA^asada and A^amina mina AlA^asadi , meaning Zeyd was, or became, or felt, secure from, safe from, [or free from fear of, ] the lion. (Msb.) You say also, A^amina ka*iba mano A^axobarahu [ He was secure from, or free from fear of, the lying of him who informed him ]. (M.) And laA A=nanu A^ano yakuwna ka*lika [ I am not free from fear of its being so; I am not sure but that it may be so ]. (Mgh in art. nb* ; and other lexicons passim.) And, of a strong-made she camel, A^aminato A^ano takuwna DaEayfapF [ She was secure from, or free from fear of, being weak ]: (M: [in a copy of the S A^uminato :]) and A^aminati AlEivaAra waAlA_aEoyaA='K [ She was secure from, or free from fear of, stumbling, and becoming jaded ]: (M:) and A^umina EivaAruhaA [ Her stumbling was not feared ]. (So in a copy of the S.) And, of a highly-prized camel, A^umina A^ano yunoHara [ It was not feared that he would be slaughtered; or his being slaughtered was not feared ]. (M.) [ A^amnahu sometimes means He was, or became, free from fear, though having cause for fear, of him, or it. i. e. he thought himself secure, or safe, from him or it. (See Kur vii. 97.)] ― -b2- A^minahu (inf. n. A^amonN TK) [and accord. to some copies of the K ↓ A=manahu ] and ↓ A^m~nhu (inf. n. taA^omiynN K) and ↓ Ay^tmnhu ([written with the disjunctive alif Aiytamanahu , and] also written Ait~amanahu , on the authority of Th, which is extr., like Ait~ahala [&c.], M) and ↓ AstA^mnhu all signify the same (M, K, TA) [ He trusted, or confided, in him; (as also A=mn bihi , q. v.;) he intrusted him with, or confided to him, power, authority, control, or a charge; he gave him charge over a thing or person: these meanings are vaguely indicated in the M and K and TA.]. You say, yaA^omanuhu Aln~aAsu walaA yaxaAfuwna gaAy^ilatahu [ Men, or people, trust, or confide, in him, and do not fear his malevolence, or mischievousness ]. (T, M.) And A^aminahu EalaY ka*aA (S, Mgh, * Msb *) and ↓ Ay^tmnhu Ealayohi , (S, Msb, K,) [ He trusted, or confided, in him with respect to such a thing; he intrusted him with, or confided to him, power, authority, control, or a charge, over it; he gave him charge over it; ] he made him, or took him as, A^amiyn over such a thing. (Mgh.) Hence, in a trad., the muw^a*~in is said to be muw^otamanN ; i. e. Aln~aAsu Eala AlA^awoqaAti Al~atiY yuw^a*~anu fiyhaA ↓ yaA^otaminuhu [ Men trust, or confide, in him with respect to the times in which he calls to prayer ], and know, by his calling to prayer, what they are commanded to do, as to praying and fasting and breaking fast. (Mgh.) It is said in the Kur [xii. 11], maA laka laA taA^omanunaA EalaY yuwsufa and [ taA^oman~aA ] with idghám [i. e. What aileth thee that thou dost not trust, or confide, in us with respect to Joseph? or, that thou dost not give us charge over Joseph? ]; (S;) meaning, why dost thou fear us for him? (Bd;) some pronouncing the verb in a manner between those of the former and the latter modes of writing it; but Akh says that the latter is better: (S:) some read tiyman~aA . (Bd.) You say also, ↓ Auwtumina fulaAnN [ Such a one was trusted, or confided, in &c.;] when it begins a sentence, changing the second ' into w ; in like manner as you change it into Y when the first is with kesr, as in Aiytamanahu ; and into A when the first is with fet-h, as in A=mana . (S.) The phrase A^amaAnapF ↓ Auwtumina , in a saying of Mohammad, if it be not correctly EalaY A^amaAnapK , may be explained as implying the meaning of AusotuHofiZa A^amaAnapF [ He was asked to take care of a deposite; or he was intrusted with it ]. (Mgh.) [You also say, A^aminahu bika*aA , meaning He intrusted him with such a thing; as, for instance, money or other property: see two exs. in the Kur iii. 68.] -A2- A^amuna , (M, Mgh, K,) or A^amina , (Msb,) inf. n. A^amaAnapN , (M, Mgh, Msb,) He was, or became, trusted in, or confided in: (M, K:) or he was, or became, trusty, trustworthy, trustful, confidential, or faithful: said of a man. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: is originally A^aA^omana ; the second ' being softened. (S.) You say, A=mnhu , [inf. n. A_iymaAnN ;] (S, M, Msb;) and ↓ A^m~nhu , [inf. n. taA^omiynN ;] (M, TA;) meaning He rendered him secure, or safe; (Msb;) he rendered him secure, or free from fear; (S, M, TA;) contr. of A^axaAfhu : (TA:) so in A=manotuhu minohu I rendered him secure, or safe, from him, or it. (Msb.) And of God you say, A=mana EibAdahu mino A^ano yaZolimahumo [ He hath rendered his servants secure from his wronging them ]. (S.) And yuw^ominu EibaAdahu mino Ea*aAbihi [ He rendereth his servants secure from his punishment ]. (M.) You say also, A=manotu AlA^asiyra , meaning I gave, or granted, AlA^amaAn [i. e. security or safety, or protection or safeguard, or the promise or assurance of security or safety, or indemnity, or quarter, ] to the captive. (Msb.) And A=mana fulaAnN AlaEaduw~a [ Such a one granted security, &c., to the enemy ], inf. n. as above. (T.) It is said in the Kur ch. ix. [verse 12], accord. to one reading, laA A_iymaAna lahumo They have not the attribute of granting protection; meaning that when they grant protection, they do not fulfil their engagement to protect. (T.) -A2- A_iymaAnN also signifies The believing [a thing, or in a thing, and particularly in God]; syn. taSodiyqN ; (T, S, &c.;) by common consent of the lexicologists and other men of science: (T:) its primary meaning is the becoming true to the trust with respect to which God has confided in one, by a firm believing with the heart; not by profession of belief with the tongue only, without the assent of the heart; for he who does not firmly believe with his heart is either a hypocrite or an ignorant person. (T, TA.) Its verb is intrans. and trans. (TA, from a Commentary on the Mutowwal.) You say, A=mana , meaning He believed. (T.) And it is said to be trans. by itself, like Sad~aqa ; and by means of bi , considered as meaning AiEotiraAfN [or acknowledgment ]; and by means of li , considered as meaning A_i*oEaAnN [or submission ]. (TA.) [Thus] you say, [ A=mnhu and] A=mn bihi , (inf. n. A_iymaAnN , T, K,) namely, a thing. (T, M.) And A=mn biAll~`hi He believed in God. (T.) It seems to be meant by what is said in the Ksh [in ii. 2], that A=mn bihi [or A=manahu ] properly signifies A=manahu Alt~ako*iyba [ He rendered him secure from being charged with lying, or falsehood ]; and that the meaning he believed him or in him, is tropical; but this is at variance with what its author says in the A; and Es-Saad says that this latter meaning is proper. (TA.) The phrase in the Kur [ix. 61], wayuw^ominu lilomw^ominiyna , accord. to Th, means And he believeth the believers; giveth credit to them. (M.) ― -b2- Sometimes it is employed to signify The acknowledging with the tongue only; and hence, in the Kur [lxiii. 3], *lika bA^an~ahumo A=manuwA vum~a kafaruwA That is because they acknowledged with the tongue, then disacknowledged with the heart. (TA.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The trusting, or confiding, or having trust or confidence. (M, K.) [You say, A=mn bihi , meaning He trusted, or confided, in him, or it: for] the verb of AymAn in this sense is trans. by means of bi without implication; as Bd says. (TA.) [And it is also trans. by itself: for] you say, maA A=mana A^ano yajida SaHaAbapF , meaning (tropical:) He trusted not that he would find companions; (M, * K, * TA;) said of one who has formed the intention of journeying: or the meaning is maA kaAda [i. e. he hardly, or scarcely, found &c.; or he was not near to finding &c.]. (M, K.) See also A^aminahu . ― -b4- Also The manifesting humility or submission, and the accepting the Law, (Zj, T, * K,) and that which the Prophet has said or done, and the firm believing thereof with the heart; (Zj, T, M;) without which firm belief, the manifesting of humility or submission, and the accepting that which the Prophet has said or done, is termed A_isolaAmN , for which one's blood is to be spared. (T.) [In this sense, it is trans. by means of li , accord. to some, as shown above; or by means of bi , for, accord. to Fei,] you say, A=manotu biAll~`hi , inf. n. as above, meaning I submitted, or resigned, myself to God. (Msb.) [There are numerous other explanations which it is needless to give, differing according to different persuasions. ― -b5- See also A_iymaAn below.]

sourceDefinition: Trusted; trusted in; confided in; (T, * S, * M, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ A^um~aAnN ; (S, M, K;) i. q. ↓ maA^omuwnN (S, M, K) and ↓ muw^otamanN : (ISk, T, K:) [ a person in whom one trusts or confides; a confidant; a person intrusted with, or to whom is confided, power, authority, control, or a charge, EalaY $aYo'K over a thing; a person intrusted with an affair, or with affairs, i. e., with the management, or disposal, thereof; a confidential agent, or superintendent; a commissioner; a commissary; a trustee; a depositary; ] a guardian: (TA:) trusty; trustworthy; trustful; confidential; faithful: (Mgh, Msb: *) pl. A^umanaA='u , and, accord. to some, ↓ A^amanapN , as in a trad. in which it is said, A^aSoHaAbiY A^amanapN liA^um~atiY , meaning My companions are guardians to my people: or, accord. to others, this is pl. of ↓ A=minN [app. in a sense mentioned below in this paragraph, so that the meaning in this trad. is my companions are persons who accord trust, or confidence, to my people ]. (TA.) Hence, A^alamo taEolamiY yaA A^asoma wayoHaki A^an~aniY Halafotu yamiynFA laA A^axuwnu A^amiyniY [ Knowest thou not, O Asmà ( A^asomaA=' , curtailed for the sake of the metre), mercy on thee! or woe to thee! that I have sworn an oath that I will not act treacherously to him in whom I trust? ] i. e. ↓ maA^omuwniY : (S:) or the meaning here is, him who trusts, or confides, in me; (ISk, T;) [i. e.] it is here syn. with ↓ A=miniY . (M.) [Hence also,] AlA^amiynu fiY AlqimaAri , (K voce mujumidN , &c.,) or A^amiynu , AlqimaAri , [ The person who is intrusted, as deputy, with the disposal of the arrows in the game called Almayosir ; or] he who shuffles the arrows; Al~a*iY . yaDoribu biAlqidaAHi . (EM p. 105.) [Hence also,] Alr~uwHu AlA^amiynu [ The Trusted, or Trusty, Spirit ]; (Kur xxvi. 193;) applied to Gabriel, because he is intrusted with the revelation of God. (Bd.) ↓ A^um~aAnN , mentioned above, and occurring in a verse of El-Aashà, applied to a merchant, is said by some to mean Possessed of religion and excellence. (M.) ↓ muw^otamanN is applied, in a trad., to the muw^a*~in , as meaning that men trust, or confide, in him with respect to the times in which he calls to prayer, and know by his call what they are commanded to do as to praying and fasting and breaking fast. (Mgh.) AlmuEaAmalapi ↓ huwa maA^omuwnu means He is [ trusty, or trustworthy, in dealing with others; or] free from exorbitance and deceit or artifice or craft to be feared. (Msb.) ― -b2- An aid, or assistant; syn. EawonN [here app. meaning, as it often does, an armed attendant, or a guard ]; because one trusts in his strength, and is without fear of his being weak. (M.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) The strong; syn. qawiY~N . (K, TA: [in the latter of which is given the same reason for this signification as is given in the M for that of Ewn ; for which qwY may be a mistranscription; but see A^amuwnN .]) ― -b4- One who trusts, or confides, in another; (ISk, T, K;) [as also ↓ A=minN , of which see an ex. voce Ha*irN ;] so accord. to ISk in the verse cited above in this paragraph: (T:) thus it bears two contr. significations. (K.) ― -b5- See also A=minN , in five places. -A2- And see A=miyna .

definition: ― -b2- Trustiness;
sourceDefinition: : see A^amonN , first sentence. ― -b2- Trustiness; trustworthiness; trustfulness; faithfulness; fidelity; (M, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ A^amanapN . (M, K.) A^amaAnapu All~`hi [for A^amaAnapu All~`hi qasamiy or maA A^uqosimu The faithfulness of God is my oath or that by which I swear ] is composed of an inf. n. prefixed to the agent, and the former is in the nom. case as an inchoative; the phrase being like laEamoru All~`hi , as meaning an oath; and the enunciative being suppressed, and meant to be understood: accord. to some, you say, A^amaAnapa All~`hi [app. for na$adotuka A^amaAnapa All~`hi I adjure thee, or conjure thee, by the faithfulness of God, or the like ], making it to be governed in the accus. case by the verb which is to be understood: and some correctly say, waA^amaAnapi All~`hi [ By the faithfulness of God ], with the w which denotes an oath: (Mgh:) or this last is an oath accord. to Aboo-Haneefeh; but Esh-Sháfi'ee does not reckon it as such: and it is forbidden in a trad. to swear by AlA^amaAnap ; app. because it is not one of the names of God. (TA.) [Or these phrases may have been used, in the manner of an oath, agreeably with explanations here following.] -A2- A thing committed to the trust and care of a person; a trust; a deposite; (Mgh, Msb;) and the like: (Msb:) property committed to trust and care: (TA:) pl. A^amaAnaAtN . (Mgh, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [viii. 27], wataxuwnuwA A^amaAnaAtikumo [ Nor be ye unfaithful to the trusts committed to you ]. (Mgh.) And in the same [xxxiii. 72], A_in~aA EaraDonaAAlA^amaAnapa EalaY Als~mwaAti waAloA^aroDiwaAlojibaAli faA^abayona A^ano yaHomilonahaA waA^a$ofaqona minohaA waHamalahaA AloA_inosaAnu [ Verily we proposed, or offered, the trust which we have committed to man to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and (accord. to explanations of Bd and others) they refused to take it upon themselves, or to accept it, and they feared it, but man took it upon himself, or accepted it: or, (accord. to another explanation of Bd, also given in the T, and in the K in art. Hml , &c.,) they refused to be unfaithful to it, and they feared it, but man was unfaithful to it: but in explaining what this trust was, authors greatly differ: accord. to some,] AlAmAnp here means obedience; so called because the rendering thereof is incumbent: or the obedience which includes that which is natural and that which depends upon the will: [for] it is said that when God created these [celestial and terrestrial] bodies, He created in them understanding: or it may here [and in some other instances] mean reason, or intellect: [and the faculty of volition: and app. conscience: these being trusts committed to us by God, to be faithfully employed: (see an ex. voce ja*orN :)] and the imposition of a task or duty or of tasks or duties [app. combined with reason or intellect, which is necessary for the performance thereof ]: (Bd:) or it here means prayers and other duties for the performance of which there is recompense and for the neglect of which there is punishment: (Jel:) or, accord. to I'Ab and Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr, (T,) the obligatory statutes which God has imposed upon his servants: (T, K: *) or, (T, K,) accord. to Ibn-'Omar, [ the choice between ] obedience and disobedience was offered to Adam, and he was informed of the recompense of obedience and the punishment of disobedience: but, in my opinion, he says, (T,) it here means the intention which one holds in the heart, (T, K,) with respect to the belief which he professes with the tongue, and with respect to all the obligatory statutes which he externally fulfils; (K;) because God has confided to him power over it, and not manifested it to any [other] of his creatures, so that he who conceives in his mind, with respect to the acknowledgment of the unity of God, (T, K,) and with respect to belief [in general], (T,) the like of that which he professes, he fulfils the AmAnp [or trust], (T, K,) and he who conceives in his mind disbelief while he professes belief with the tongue is unfaithful thereto, and every one who is unfaithful to that which is confided to him is [termed] HaAmilN , (T,) or HaAmilu AlA^amaAnapi , and muHotamiluhaA : (Bd:) and by AlA_inosaAnu is here meant the doubting disbeliever. (T.) ― -b2- Also, [as being a trust committed to him by God, A man's] family, or household; syn. A^aholN . (TA.)

definition: Secure, safe, or free from fear;
sourceDefinition: Secure, safe, or free from fear; as also ↓ A^amiynN (Lh, T, * S, * M, Msb, K) and ↓ A^aminN . (M, K.) Hence, in the Kur [xcv. 3], ↓ wah*aA Alobaladi AloA^amiyni [ And this secure town ]; (Akh, Lh, T, S, M;) meaning Mekkeh. (M.) baladN A=minN and ↓ A^amiynN means A town, or country, or district, of which the inhabitants are in a state of security, or confidence, therein. (Msb.) It is also said in the Kur [xliv. 51], ↓ A_in~a Alomut~aqiyna fiy maqaAmK A^amiynK , meaning [ Verily the pious shall be in an abode ] wherein they shall be secure from the accidents, or casualties, of fortune. (M.) [And hence,] ↓ AlA^amiynu is one of the epithets applied to God, (Mgh, K,) on the authority of El-Hasan; (Mgh;) an assertion requiring consideration: it may mean He who is secure with respect to the accidents, or casualties, of fortune: but see Almuw^ominu , which is [well known as] an epithet applied to God. (TA.) A=minu AlmaAli means What is secure from being slaughtered, of the camels, because of its being highly prized; by AlmAl being meant AlA_ibil : or, as some say, (tropical:) what is highly esteemed, of property of any kind; as though, if it had intellect, it would feel secure from being exchanged. (M.) You say, A^aEoTayotuhu mino A=mini maAliy , (K, TA, [in the CK A=mani ,]) meaning (tropical:) I gave him of the choice, or best, of my property; of what was highly esteemed thereof; (K, TA;) and maAliY ↓ mino A^amoni which Az explains as meaning of the choice, or best, of my property. (TA: [in which is given a verse cited by ISk showing that A^amon , thus used, is not a mistranscription for A=min .]) And A=minu AlHilomi means Steadfast in forbearance or clemency; of whose becoming disordered in temper, and free from self-restraint, there is no fear. (M.) ― -b2- See also A^amiynN , in three places: ― -b3- and see AaminN . -A2- See also A^amiynN , in two places.

sourceDefinition: [in the CK, erroneously, A=miynu ] and ↓ A^amiyna ; (Th, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) both chaste and well known, (TA,) the latter of the dial. of El-Hijáz, (Msb, TA,) as some say, (TA,) [and this, though the less common, is the original form, for] the medd in the former is only to give fulness of sound to the fet-hah of the A^ , (Th, M, Msb, TA,) as is shown by the fact that there is no word in the Arabic language of the measure faAEiylN ; (Msb, TA;) and some pronounce the former A=m~iyna , (K,) which is said by some of the learned to be a dial. var., (Msb,) but this is a mistake, (S, Msb,) accord. to authorities of good repute, and is one of old date, originating from an assertion of Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, [i. e. Th,] that A=miyna is like EaASiyna , by which he was falsely supposed to mean its having the form of a pl., [and being consequently A=m~iyna ,] (Msb, [and part of this is said in the M,]) whereas he thereby only meant that the m is without teshdeed, like the S in EaASiyna ; (M;) beside that the sense of qaASidiyna [which is that of A=m~iyna , from A^am~a ,] would be inconsistent after the last phrase of the first chapter of the Kur [where A=myna is usually added]; (Msb;) and sometimes it is pronounced with imáleh, [i. e. “émeena,”] as is said by ElWáhidee in the Beseet; (K;) but this is unknown in works on lexicology, and is said to be a mispronunciation of some of the Arabs of the desert of El-Yemen: (MF:) each form is indecl., (S,) with fet-h for its termination, like A^ayona and kayofa , to prevent the occurrence of two quiescent letters together: (T, S, TA:) it is a word used immediately after a prayer, or supplication: (S, * M:) [it is best expressed, when occurring in a translation, by the familiar Hebrew equivalent Amen: ] El-Fárisee says that it is a compound of a verb and a noun; (M;) meaning answer Thou me; [i. e. answer Thou my prayer; ] (M, Mgh;*) or O God, answer Thou: (Zj, T, Msb, K:) or so be it: (AHát, S, Msb, K:) or so do Thou, (K, TA,) O Lord: (TA:) it is strangely asserted by some of the learned, that, after the Fátihah, [or Opening Chapter of the Kur-án,] it is a prayer which implies all that is prayed for in detail in the Fátihah: so in the Towsheeh: (MF:) or it is one of the names of God: (M, Msb, K:) so says El-Hasan (M, Msb) El-Basree: (Msb:) but the assertion that it is for yaA Aall~`hu [ O God ], and that AsotajibN [ answer Thou ] is meant to be understood, is not correct accord. to the lexicologists; for, were it so, it would be with refa, not nasb. (T.)

(TA.)

definition: [ Intuitive knowledge;
sourceDefinition: [ Intuitive knowledge;] such that its origination does not rest upon speculation, and acquisition by study, whether it do, or do not, require some other thing, as conjecture or experience &c.; (KT, Kull;) so that it is [ sometimes] syn. with DaruwriY~N [and opposed to naZariY~N ]: and sometimes it means such as does not require anything whatever after the intellect has directed itself; so that it is more particular than DaruwriY~N : (KT:) as the conception of heat and cold, and the assent of the mind to the position that negation and affirmation cannot be co-existent, nor be simultaneously non-existent, in the same instance. (KT, Kull.) ― -b2- [And hence,] A mere simpleton or fool: but this is post-classical. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, TA,) inf. n. baz~N , (S, K, TA,) He took it away; or seized it, or carried it away, by force; (S, TA;) as also ↓ Abtz~hu , (S, K,) and ↓ bazobazahu : (K:) he took it away unjustly, injuriously, and forcibly; as also ↓ Abtz~hu : (K, * TA:) he gained the mastery over it: (K, * TA:) he pulled it up or out or off; removed it from its place; displaced it; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ Abtz~hu , and ↓ bazobazahu . (TA.) It is said in a prov., mano Eaz~a baz~a He who overcomes takes the spoil. (S, A.) And you say, baz~ahu vawobahu , and ↓ Abtz~hu , He took away from him, or seized or carried away from him by force, his garment. (A.) It is said in a trad., viyaAbiY ↓ fayabotaz~u wamataAEiY And he strips me, or despoils me, of my clothes and my goods; takes them from me by superior force. (TA.) You say also, baz~ahu viyaAbahu He pulled off from him his clothes. (TA.) And Alr~ajulu jaAriyatahu m$no viyaAbihaA ↓ Abtz~ The man stripped his slave-girl of her clothes. (Mgh, * TA.) ― -b2- Also baz~avawobahu , aor. as above, He pulled his garment towards him, or to him: so in a verse of Khálid Ibn-Zuheyr El-Hudhalee [cited in art. ryb , but with this difference, that yajur~u is there put in the place of yabuz~u ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- [ baz~ahu is also explained in the TA by Habasahu ; but without any ex.; and I think it probable that Habasahu is a mistake for ja*abahu ].

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of 1. (S, &c.) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] jiYo'a bihi Eaz~aA baz~FA He was brought without any means of avoiding it; (A, TA;) willingly or against his will: (TA in art. Ez :) [as though originally signifying by being overcome and despoiled. ] -A2- Cloths, or stuffs, or garments; syn. viyaAb : (IAmb, Mgh, K:) [see also biz~apN :] or a kind thereof: (Lth, Mgh, Msb:) or such as are the goods of the baz~aAz , (S, A,) or of the merchant: (Msb:) or the furniture of a house or tent, consisting of cloths or stuffs ( viyaAb , IDrd, Mgh, Msb, K) and the like: (K:) in the dial. of the people of El-Koofeh, cloths, or stuffs, or garments, ( vyAb ,) of linen and of cotton; not of wool nor of xaz~ : (Mgh:) pl. buzuwzN ; (A;) meaning, in conjunction with xuzuwzN , (i. e., xuzuwzN wa buzuwzN ,) good cloths or stuffs or garments. (A.) [Golius explains it as “Chald. בוּץ , Byssus, seu potius pannus lineus, bombacinus, etiam sericus: ” as on the authority of the S and K (though he omits the explanations in both those lexicons) and Meyd and Ibn-Maaroof (who explains it only by the Persian word jaAmaho , meaning cotton or linen cloth, or a garment, ) and the Mirkát el-Loghah. He seems to have judged from its resemblance in sound to the Chaldee and Latin words with which he identifies it. The things which it signifies, however, may perhaps be so called because they are usual spoils: and hence also, perhaps, the application here next following.] -A3- Weapons, or arms; or a weapon; syn. silaAHN ; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ biz~apN , (S, A, Msb, K,) and ↓ bazazN , (K,) and ↓ biz~iyzaY : (TA:) the first of these four words including in its application coats of mail and the migofar and the sword: (TA:) or it signifies a sword: (IDrd, A, TA:) and ↓ bazazN , accord. to AA, complete arms. (TA.) You say, taqal~ada baz~aA HasanFA He hung upon himself a goodly sword, putting its suspensory belt or cord upon his neck. (A.) And kaAmilapK ↓ gazaA fiY biz~apK He went to war in complete arms. (A.)

(A, TA.) -A2- See also baz~N , latter part.

(TA.) [But see A^adamapN .] ― -b2- Hence the saying in a trad., mano A^aHab~a AlquroA=na qaloyabo$uro , accord. to him who recites it thus, with damm to the $ ; meaning (assumed tropical:) Whoso loveth the Kur-án, let him make himself light of flesh, [ by not eating more than will be sufficient, and so prepare himself] for [reading, or reciting,] it, [like as one prepares a horse for running,] because eating much causes one to forget it. (TA.) ― -b3- Hence also, ba$ara AlA^aroDa , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (S, K,) (assumed tropical:) It (a swarm of locusts) stripped the ground; (TA;) ate what was upon the ground, (S, K,) i. e., upon its surface; as though the exterior of the ground were its ba$arap . (TA.) ― -b4- And ba$ara , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He clipped his mustache much, so that the ba$arap (i. e. the exterior of the skin, TA) became apparent. (K, TA.) sourceDefinition: (S, A, Msb, &c.,) the form used by the Arabs in general, (Msb,) inf. n. tabo$iyrN ; (S, Msb, K, &c.;) and ↓ ba$arahu , aor. , (S, Mgh, Msb,) of the dial. of Tihámeh and the adjacent parts, (Msb,) inf. n. ba$orN and bu$uwrN (S, K) and bu$orN , (TA,) or this last is a simple subst.; (Msb;) and ↓ Ab$rhu ; (S, A, Mgh, K;) and ↓ Astb$rhu ; (K, TA;) are syn.; (S, K, &c.;) originally signifying He announced to him an event which produced a change in his ba$arap [or complexion ]: and hence, (El-Fakhr Er-Rázee,) he announced to him an event which rejoiced him: (A, El-Fakhr Er-Rázee:) so in common acceptation [when not restricted by an adjunct that denotes its having a different meaning: see bu$oraY and an ex. below in this paragraph]: (El-Fakhr Er-Rázee:) or he rejoiced him [ by an annunciation ]: (Msb:) and he announced to him an event which grieved him: [or he grieved him by an annunciation: ] both these significations are proper. (El-Fakhr Er-Rázee.) You say, b$~rhu biAlA^amori [generally meaning He rejoiced him by the annunciation of the event ]; and bihi ↓ ba$arahu , aor. and inf. ns. as above; &c. (TA.) And ba$~arotuhu bimawoluwdK [ I rejoiced him by the annunciation of a new-born child ]. (S.) And it is said in the Kur [iii. 20, &c.], ba$~irohumo biEa*aAbK A^aliymK [ Grieve thou them by the annunciation, or denunciation, of a painful punishment ]. (S.) You say also, of a she-camel, ba$~arato biAll~aqaAHi , meaning (assumed tropical:) She made it known that she had begun to be pregnant. (TA. [See also 4.])

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ muba$~irN , (S, Mgh, K,) [and so ↓ ba$uwrN , as will be seen by an ex. in what follows,] One who announces to a people [ or person ] an event, either good or evil; (TA;) but meaning the former oftener than the latter: (Msb:) [ an announcer of a joyful event, or joyful events: one who rejoices another, or others, by an annunciation: ] pl. bu$araA='u (A) and bu$urN , (TA in art. n$r ,) or this is pl. of ↓ ba$uwrN . (TA in the present art.) It is said in the Kur [vii. 55], wa huwa A@l~a*iY yurosilu A@lr~iyaAHa bu$urFA , and bu$orFA , and ↓ bu$oraY , and ba$orFA ; [accord. to different readings, meaning (assumed tropical:) And He it is who sendeth the winds announcing coming rain; ] in which bu$urN is pl. of ↓ ba$uwrN , [syn. with ba$iyrN and muba$~irN , but both masc. and fem.,] (TA,) or of ba$iyrN , (Bd,) or of ba$iyrapN ; (TA in art. n$r ;) and bu$orFA is a contraction of the same; and bu$oraY is syn. with bi$aArapN ; and ba$orFA is the inf. n. of ba$arahu in the sense of ba$~arahu (TA. [But the reading commonly followed in this passage is nu$urFA , with n : another reading is nu$orFA : another, na$orFA : and another, na$arFA .]) And ↓ Almuba$~iraAtu , (A,) or muba$~iraAtu Alr~iyaAHi , (S,) signifies (tropical:) Winds that announce [ coming ] rain: (S, A:) so in the Kur xxx. 45. (TA.) -A2- Also Goodly; beautiful; elegant in form or features; (S, K;) applied to a man, and to a face: (TA:) fem. with p ; (S, K;) applied to a woman, and to a she-camel; (S;) and meaning, when applied to a she-camel, neither emaciated nor fat: or, accord. to Aboo-Hilál, neither of generous nor of ignoble breed: or, as some say, half-fattened: (TA:) pl. of the fem. ba$aAy^iru : (S:) and ↓ mabo$uwrapN signifies beautiful in make and colour; (IAar, K;) applied to a girl. (IAar.)

definition: (T, S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (T, S, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ bakiymN (S, K) i. q. A^axorasu [meaning Dumb, either by natural conformation or from inability to find words to express what he would say ]: (S, Msb, K:) or not having understanding to reply, (IAar, T, Msb, TA,) nor ability to frame speech well, (T, TA,) though possessing the faculty of speech; whereas Axrs signifies speechless, or destitute of the faculty of speech, by natural conformation, (T, Msb, TA,) like the beast that lacks the faculty of articulation; (T, TA;) unable to find words to express what he would say; unable to reply: (AZ, TA:) or dumb by natural conformation: (IAth, TA:) fem. bakomaA='u : (TA:) pl. bukomN (Msb, K) and bukomaAnN , (K,) both pls. of A^abokamu , like as Sum~N and Sum~aAnN are pls. of A^aSam~u ; and the pl. of ↓ bakiymN is A^abokaAmN . (TA.) In the Kur ii. 166, bukomN means persons in the condition of him who has been born dumb: or, as some say, deprived of their intellects: (Zj, TA:) or ignorant and ignoble; because not profiting much by the faculty of speech, so that they are as though they had been deprived of it. (IAth, TA.) The phrase fitonapN Sam~aA='u bakomaA='u EamoyaA='u , occurring in a trad., [lit.] meaning [ A sedition, or the like,] deaf, dumb, blind, applies to a ftnp that does not withdraw, or become removed: or, as some say, to one which, by reason of the confusion attending it, and the perishing of the sound and the sick therein, is likened to the deaf and dumb and blind who does not pursue the right course to a thing, but goes at random like the weak-sighted she-camel. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of balaga ] and A_ibolaAgN [inf. n. of ↓ Ablg , but it seems that AblAg is here a mistranscription for balaAgN , which is, like buluwgN , an inf. n. of balaga , and this observation will be found to be confirmed by a statement immediately following this sentence,] signify The reaching, attaining, arriving at, or coming to, the utmost point of that to which, or towards which, one tends or repairs or betakes himself, to which one directs his course, or which one seeks, pursues, endeavours to reach, desires, intends, or purposes; whether it be a place, or a time, or any affair or state or event that is meditated or intended or determined or appointed: and sometimes, the being at the point thereof: so says Abu-1-Kásim in the Mufradát. (TA: [in which it is said, in the supplement to the present art., that balaAgN signifies The reaching, attaining, arriving at, or coming to, a thing. ]) You say, balaga AlmakaAna , (S, K,) and Almanozila , (Msb,) [aor. ,] inf. n. buluwgN (S, K) [and balaAgN , as shown above], He reached, attained, arrived at, or came to, (S, Msb, K,) the place, (S, K,) and the place of abode: (Msb:) and (so in the S, but in the K “ or, ”) he was, or became, at the point of reaching it, attaining it, &c. (S, K.) fabalagona A^ajalahuna , in the Kur [ii. 232], means And they have fully attained, or ended, their term. (Msb.) But faA_i*aA balagona A^ajalahun~a , in the same [lxv. 2], means And when they are near to attaining, or ending, their term: (S, TA:) or are at the point of accomplishing their term. (Msb, TA.) It has the first of the meanings explained above in the phrase, balaga A^a$ud~ahu [Kur xii. 22 &c., He attained his manly vigour, or full maturity, &c.]. (TA.) And in balagaA^arobaEiyna sanapF [Kur xlvii. 14, He attained the age of forty years ]. (TA.) And in balaga maEahu Als~aEoYa [Kur xxxvii. 100, He attained to working with him ]. (TA.) In the Kur [iii. 35], occurs the phrase, waqado balaganiYa Alkibaru [ When old age hath come to me, or overtaken me ]: and in another place [xix. 9], wa qado balagotu mina Alkibari Eutiy~FA [ And I have reached the extreme degree of old age: so explained in the Expos. of the Jel]: phrases like A^adorakaniYa Aljahodu and A^adorakotuhu . (Er-Rághib, TA.) You say also, maA balaga ↓ lazimahu *`lika baAligFA with the accus. case as a denotative of state; meaning [ That clave to him, or adhered to him, &c.,] rising to its highest degree or point; from balaga Almanozila , explained above. (Msb.) [But maA balaga ↓ baAligFA more frequently means Whatever point, degree, amount, sum, quantity, number, or the like, it may reach, attain, arrive at, come to, or amount to. ] And ↓ balaga fulaAnN mabolagahu and ↓ mabolagatuhu [ Such a one reached, or attained, his utmost point or scope or degree ]. (TA.) And ↓ balaga fiY AlEilomi AlmabaAliga [ He attained, in knowledge, or science, the utmost degrees of proficiency ]. (TA.) And balaga fiY ↓ Aljawodapi mabolagFA [ It reached a consummate degree in goodness ]. (S, K, * TA.) And balaga mina Aljawodapi ↓ mabolagFA [ He attained a consummate degree of goodliness ]: said of a boy that has attained to puberty. (O, TA.) And balaga gaAyatahu fiY AlT~alabi [ He did his utmost, or used his utmost power or ability, in seeking to attain an object ]. (Msb in art. jhd .) And balaga A^aqoSaY majohuwdi baEiyrihi fiY Als~ayori [ He exerted the utmost endeavour, or effort, or power, or strength, of his camel, in journeying ]. (S in art. nkv .) And balaga jahoda daAb~atihi i. q. jahadahaA [ He jaded, harassed, distressed, fatigued, or wearied, his beast ]: (K in art. jhd :) and in like manner, balaga ma$aq~atahu and balaga minohu Alma$aq~apa i. q. jahadahu [and $aq~a Ealayohi , i. e. He, or it, jaded him, harassed him, &c.; ditressed him, afflicted him, oppressed him, overpowered him: thus in each of these instances, as in many similar cases, the verb with the inf. n. that follows is equivalent to the verb of that inf. n.]. (Msb in art. jhd .) [And, elliptically, balaga minohu i. q. balaga minohu Alm$aq~apa , explained above: and often meaning It took, or had, an effect upon him; it affected him: frequently said of wine and the like: and of a saying; as in the Ksh and Bd in iv. 66, where yabolugu minohumo is followed by wayuw^aviru fiyhi as an explicative: see also baliygN .] And balagota min~aA Albulagiyna , (S, K,) and Albilagiyna , and kul~a mabolagK : (K:) see Albulagiyna below. And balagotu mina AlA^amori Alma$aq~apa [ I experienced distress from the affair, or event ]. (TA in art. mD .) [See also an ex. voce A_ibidN . balaganiY also signifies It has come to my knowledge, or been related to me, or been told me; or it came to my knowledge, &c.: and in this case it is generally followed by A^an~a , or by A^ano as a contraction of A^an~a : for exs., see these two particles. And in like manner, balaganiY Eanohu Information has come to me, or information came to me, from him, or concerning him, that such a thing has happened, or had happened.] And balaga said of a letter or writing, inf. n. balaAgN and buluwgN , It reached, arrived, or came. (Msb.) And said of a plant, or of herbage, It attained its full growth: (TA:) and of a tree, such as a palm-tree &c., its fruit became ripe: (AHn, TA:) and of fruit, it became ripe. (Msb.) Also, said of a boy, (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. buluwgN , or, as IKoot says, balaAgN , (Msb,) He attained to puberty, virility, ripeness, or maturity; syn. A^adoraka , (T, S, Msb, K,) and AiHotalama ; (M, Msb;) and attained a consummate degree of goodliness ( balaga mina Aljawodapi mabolagFA ): (O, TA:) as though he attained the time of the writing of his marriage-contract, and of his having duties or obligations imposed upon him: (TA:) and in like manner one says of a girl, balaga , (T, TA,) or balagato . (TA.) ― -b2- balaga A@ll~`hu bihi [ God caused him to reach, attain, arrive at, or come to, his appointed end, or term of life; A^ajalahu , or the like, being understood]. (TA.) You say, balaga A@ll~`hu bika A^akolaA^a AlEumuri , i. e. [ May God cause thee to reach, or attain, ] the extreme, or most distant, period of life! (S and TA in art. klA^ .) And faEalotu bihi maA balaga bihi AlA^a*aY wa Almakoruwho [ I did with him that which caused him to come to what was annoying, or hurtful, and evil ]. (TA.) And balaga bihi Albilagiyna : see the last word of this phrase below. ― -b3- buliga , like EuniYa , He (a man) was, or became, jaded, harasssed, distressed, fatigued, or wearied. (K.) -A2- baluga , [aor. ,] (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. balaAgapN , (S, Msb,) He was, or became baliyg , i. e. faSiyH [more properly signifying chaste, or perspicuous, in speech, but here meaning eloquent ]; (S, * Msb, K;) and sharp, or penetrating, or effective, in tongue; (Msb;) attaining, by his speech, or diction, the utmost scope of his mind and desire. (K, * TA.) The difference between balaAgapN and faSaAHapN is this: that the latter is an attribute of a single word and of speech and of the speaker; but the former is an attribute only of speech and the speaker: (Kull:) blAgp in the speaker is A faculty whereby one is enabled to compose language suitable to the exigency of the case, i. e., to the occasion of speaking [ or writing ], with chasteness, or perspicuity, or eloquence, thereof: in language, it is suitableness to the exigency of the case, i. e., to the occasion of speaking [or writing ], with chasteness or perspicuity, or eloquence, thereof. (KT.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A_ibolaAgN [inf. ns. of bl~g and Ablg ] signify The causing to reach, attain, arrive, or come; bringing, conveying, or delivering: (S, K, TA:) the former is the more common. (Er-Rághib, TA.) [You say, bl~ghu AlmakaAna He caused him, or it, to reach, attain, arrive at, or come to, the place. And bl~ghu maqoSuwdahu He caused him to attain his object of aim or endeavour &c.] And bal~agotu Alr~isaAlapa [ I brought, conveyed, or delivered, the message ]. (S.) And bl~ghu Als~alaAma , (Msb,) and Alxabara , (TA,) as also ↓ Ablghu , (Msb, TA,) He brought, conveyed, delivered, or communicated, to him the salutation, (Msb,) and he brought, &c., or told, to him the news, or information. (TA.) [And bal~aganiY Eano fulaAnK He told me from such a one, or on the part of such a one, some piece of information, or that some event had happened, &c.] -A2- bl~g AlfaArisu , (S, A, K,) inf. n. taboliygN , (K,) The horseman stretched forth, or extended, his hand, or arm, with the rein of his horse, [or gave the rein to his horse, ] in order that he might increase in his running. (S, A, K.) -A3- bl~g Al$~ayobu fiY raA^osihi Hoariness began to appear on his head; accord. to IAar; as also bl~E , with the unpointed E : the Basrees assert that the former is a mistranscription; but it is related as heard from Th, by Aboo-Bekr Es-Soolee. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. mubaAlagapN (JK, K, &c.) and bilaAgN , (K.) He exceeded the usual, or ordinary, or the just, or proper, bounds, or degree, in a thing; acted egregiously, or immoderately, or extravagantly, therein: (KL:) he strove, or laboured; exerted himself, or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; employed himself vigorously, strenuously, laboriously, sedulously, earnestly, with energy or effectiveness; took pains, or extraordinary pains: (K, TA:) he did not fall short of doing what was requisite, or what he ought; did not flag, or was not remiss: (S, K, TA:) he exerted unsparingly his power or ability, or effort or endeavour, or the utmost thereof: (Msb:) he accomplished, or did, or attained, the utmost of his power or ability, or effort or endeavour; he did his utmost: (JK:) fiY A^amorK [ in an affair ]: (S, K, TA:) or fiY ka*aA , meaning in the pursuit of such a thing. (Msb.) [ bAlg fiY ka*aA may be rendered as above, or He did such a thing much, exceedingly, egregiously, extraordinarily, immoderately, extravagantly, excessively, vehemently, energetically, superlatively, excellently, consummately, thoroughly. Hence mubaAlagapN in explanations of words; meaning Intensiveness; muchness; extraordinariness; excessiveness; vehemence; energy; emphasis; hyperbole; &c.; and sometimes, frequentative signification. Thus, A_isomu mubaAlagapK means A noun of intensiveness; or an intensive epithet: as $akuwrN “ very thankful, ” or “ very grateful; ” and Ham~aAdN “ a great praiser, ” or “ a frequent praiser. ”]

definition: , (S,) or Albilagiyna , (JK,) or both, (K,) Calamity, misfortune, or disaster: (S, K:) or distress, or affliction.
sourceDefinition: , (S,) or Albilagiyna , (JK,) or both, (K,) Calamity, misfortune, or disaster: (S, K:) or distress, or affliction. (JK.) Hence the saying of 'Áïsheh to 'Alee, (S, K,) when she was taken prisoner [by him], (S,) balagota min~aA Albulagiyna , (S, K,) and Albilagiyna , (K,) i. e., Ald~aAhiyapa ; meaning balagota ↓ min~aA kul~a mabolagK [ Thou hast distressed us, or afflicted us, in the utmost degree ]: (K:) it is said to mean that the war harassed her, and distressed her in the utmost degree. (TA.) It is like AlburaHiyna [and AlbiraHiyna ] and AlA^aTowariyna ; all meaning calamities, misfortunes, or disasters: (A'Obeyd, TA:) and is as though they said xaTobN bilagN [and bulagN ], meaning baliygN , and then formed the pl. thus because they considered calamities [as personified, i. e.,] as rational beings having purpose, or design. (IAth, TA.) It is invariably thus, terminating with Y and n : or one may say in the nom. case Albulaguwna , and in the accus. and gen. Albulagiyna . (O, K. *) You say also, balaga bihi Albilagiyna [lit. He caused him to come, i. e. he brought him, to calamity, misfortune, or disaster, or to distress, or affliction ]; meaning he went to the utmost point in reviling him, and annoying him, or molesting him. (IAar, TA.)

definition: Reaching, attaining, arriving at, or coming to, a place [or time, or an affair or a state or an event that is meditated or intended or determined or appointed;
sourceDefinition: Reaching, attaining, arriving at, or coming to, a place [or time, or an affair or a state or an event that is meditated or intended or determined or appointed; reaching, &c., to the utmost point or degree: and sometimes, being at the point of reaching &c.: see 1, first sentence]. (TA.) You say also, ↓ jayo$N balogN , meaning baAligN [ An army reaching, or arriving at, its appointed place ]. (K, TA.) And ↓ A^amoru A@ll~`hi balogN , i. e. baAligN , (S, K,) meaning [ The decree of God ] reacheth, or attaineth, its intended object: (K:) from the saying in the Kur [lxv. 3], A_in~a A@ll~`ha baAligN A^amorahu (S) Verily God attaineth his purpose. (Bd, Jel.) And baAligN fiY AlHumoqi Reaching the utmost point, or degree, in stupidity, or foolishness. (TA.) definition: The third letter of the alphabet: called taA='N and taA [respecting which latter see the letter b ]: the pl.
sourceDefinition: The third letter of the alphabet: called taA='N and taA [respecting which latter see the letter b ]: the pl. [of the former is taA='aAtN ; and of the latter,] A^atowaA='u . (TA in bAb AlAlf Allyin~p .) It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap [or non-vocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice], and of those termed niTaEiy~ap [and niToEiy~ap and naTaEiy~ap and naToEiy~ap pronounced by pressing the tip of the tongue against the upper gums and suddenly withdrawing it with an emission of the breath]: these latter are T and d and t , three letters that are among those which are changed into other letters. (TA at the commencement of bAb AltA=' .) -A2- It is one of the augmentative letters: (S:) and is movent when added at the beginning of a noun, and at the end of a noun, [and at the beginning of a verb,] and at the end of a verb, and is also quiescent at the end of a verb. (Mughnee, K.) -A3- Added at the beginning of a noun, it is a preposition, or particle governing the gen. case, significant of swearing, (S, * Mughnee, K,) and denoting wonder; (Mughnee, K;) and [accord. to general usage] it is peculiarly prefixed to the name All~`h ; (S, Mughnee, K;) as in taA@ll~`hi laqado kaAna ka*aA [ By God, verily it was thus, or verily such a thing was ]; (S;) and taA@ll~`hi laA^afoEalan~a ka*aA [ By God, I will assuredly do such a thing ]: (TA:) but sometimes they said, tarab~iY [ By my Lord ], and tarab~i AlkaEobapi [ By the Lord of the Kaabeh ], and taA@lr~aHomaAni [ By the Compassionate ], (Mughnee, K,) as is related on the authority of Akh; deviating from common usage. (TA.) Thus used, it is a substitute for w , (S, Mughnee,) as it is also in tatoraY and turaAvN and tujaAha and tuxamapN [&c.]; (S;) and the w is a substitute for b ; (S, Mughnee;) but the t has the additional meaning of denoting wonder: so says Z. (Mughnee.) -A4- Added at the end of a noun, it is a particle of allocution: (Mughnee, K:) it is thus added in A^anota [ Thou ], (S, Mughnee, K,) addressed to a male, (TA,) and A^anoti [ Thou ], (Mughnee, K,) addressed to a female; (TA;) uniting with the noun, as though the two became one; not being an affixed noun governed in the gen. case. (S. [See A^ano .]) -A5- It is added in [the beginning of] the second person of the future, (S,) [i. e.,] in the beginning of the aor., (TA,) [as a particle of allocution,] as in A^anota tafoEalu [ Thou dost, or wilt do ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- It is also added, as a sign of the fem. gender, in the beginning of the future, [or aor.,] as in hiYa tafoEalu [ She does, or will do ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- It is also added in the beginning of the third person [fem.] of the [aor. used as an] imperative, [as a sign of the fem. gender,] as in litaqumo hinodu [ Let Hind stand ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And sometimes it is added in the beginning of the second person of the [aor. used as an] imperative, [as a particle of allocution,] as in the phrase in the Kur [x. 59, accord. to one reading], fabi*`lika falotaforaHuwA [ Therefore therein rejoice ye ]: and in the saying of the rájiz, tiy^o*ano faA_in~iY Hamow^uhaA wajaAruhaA qulotu libaw~aAbK ladayohi daAruhaA [explained in art. A*n ]: and [thus] it is added in the beginning of [the second person of] the [aor. used as an] imperative of a verb of which the agent is not named, as in lituzoha yaA rajulu [ Be thou proud, vain, boastful, or self-conceited, O man ], from zuhiYa : but Akh says that the adding of the l in the beginning of the second person of the [aor. used as an] imperative [except in the case of a pass. verb or a verb of which the agent is not named] is a bad idiom, because the l is not needed. (S, TA.) -A6- The movent t added at the end of a verb is a pronoun, as in qumotu [ I stood ], (Mughnee, K,) and qumota [ Thou stoodest, addressed to a male], and qumoti [ Thou stoodest, addressed to a female ]: (Mughnee:) thus added in the first and second persons of the pret., it is a pronoun denoting the agent. (S.) ― -b2- The quiescent t added at the end of a verb is a sign of the fem. gender, (Mughnee, K,) i. e., a particle applied to denote the fem. gender, (Mughnee,) as in qaAmato [ She stood ]. (Mughnee, K.) J says [in the S] that, when thus added at the end of the pret., it is a pronoun: but IB says [correctly] that it is a particle. (TA.) -A7- It is also, sometimes, affixed to vum~a and rub~a ; and in these cases it is most commonly movent with fet-h, (Mughnee, K,) so that one says vum~ata and rub~ata . (TA.) [See arts. vm and rb .] -A8- ti is an imperative of A^ataY . (M in art. AtY .) -A9- [As a numeral, t denotes Four hundred. ]

definition: A twin; one of two young, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and of more, (M, K,) brought forth at one birth, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) of any animals; whether a male or a female, or a male [ brought forth ] with a...
sourceDefinition: A twin; one of two young, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and of more, (M, K,) brought forth at one birth, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) of any animals; whether a male or a female, or a male [ brought forth ] with a female; (M, K;) and tawo'amapN is [also] applied to a female: (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) it occurs in poetry contracted into tawamN : (M:) the pl. is tawaAy^imu and tuw^aAmN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter of which is of a rare form, not without parallels, (M,) said by some to be a quasi-pl. n., and by some to be originally [ tiy^aAmN ,] with kesr, but the assertion of these last is condemned by AHei; (MF;) and tawo'amuwna is allowable as applied to human beings: (S, TA:) you say, huwa tawo'amuhu [in the TA, erroneously, tuw^omuhu , with damm,] and ↓ tiy^omuhu and ↓ tay^iymuhu [in the CK tayoy^muhu ] (AZ, M, K) [meaning He is his twin-brother ]: and humaA tawo'amaAni (S, * M, Mgh, Msb * K) and tawo'amN (M, K) [ They two are twin-brothers ]: or tawo'amN applies only to one of the two; (Msb;) it is a mistake to say humaA tawo'amN and humaA zawojN : (Mgh:) [but see zawojN :] Lth says that tawo'amN applies to two sons, or young ones, [ born ] together; and that one should not say humaA tawo'amaAni , but humaA tawo'amN : this, however, is a mistake: correctly, as ISk and Fr say, tawo'amN applies to one, and tawo'amaAni to two. (T, TA.) It is of the measure fawoEalN , (Kh, S, IB, Msb,) in the opinion of some, (IB,) and originally wawo'amN , (Kh, T, S, IB,) like as tawolajN is originally wawolajN ; (Kh, T, S;) from Alwiy^aAmu , (T, IB,) “ the being mutually near, ” (T,) “ mutually agreeing, ” (T, IB,) “ being mutually conformable; ” (IB;) so that it means one that agrees with, or matches, another, (IB.) ― -b2- It is metaphorically used in relation to all things resembling one another [so that it means (tropical:) One of a pair ]. (M.) A poet says, qaAlato lanaA wadamoEuhaA tuw^aAmu kaA@ld~ur~i A_i*o A^asolamahu A@ln~iZaAmu EalaY A@l~a*iyna A@rotaHaluwA A@ls~alaAmu (assumed tropical:) [ She said to us, while her tears fell in pairs, or in close succession, like large pearls when the string lets them drop off, Upon those who have departed be peace ]. (S.) [This citation, and what immediately follows it in the S, mentioning the pl. tawo'amuwna , not tuw^aAmuwna , have been misunderstood by Golius; and Freytag has followed him in this case.] ― -b3- Alt~awo'amu is also [a name of] (assumed tropical:) A certain Mansion [ of the Moon; namely, the Sixth; more commonly called AlhanoEapu ;] pertaining to AljawozaA=' [here meaning Gemini ]; (M, K;) one of two [ asterisms ] called tawo'amaAni : (M:) Alt~awo'amaAni is (assumed tropical:) The Sign of Gemini. (Kzw.) ― -b4- [The pl.] tawaAy^imu also signifies (assumed tropical:) Clusters, or what are clustered together, ( maA ta$aAbaka ,) of stars, and of pearls. (M, K.) ― -b5- And tawo'amaAni , (assumed tropical:) A pair of pearls, or large pearls, for the ear: each of them is termed a tawo'amap to the other. (TA.) ― -b6- Alt~awo'amaAni , [in the CK Alt~awo'amAnu ,] (assumed tropical:) A certain small herb, (AHn, M, K,) having a fruit like cumin-seed, (AHn, M, and K in art. wA^m ,) and many leaves, growing in the plains, spreading long and wide, and having a yellow flower. (AHn, TA.) ― -b7- Alt~awo'amu also signifies (assumed tropical:) The arrow of the kind used in the game called Almayosir : (M:) or a certain arrow of those used in that game: (K:) or the second of those arrows; (S, M, K;) said by Lh to have two notches, and to entitle to two portions [ of the slaughtered camel ] if successful, and to subject to the payment for two portions if unsuccessful. (M.) ― -b8- And tawo'amaAtN , (assumed tropical:) A kind of women's vehicles [ borne by camels ], (T, K,) like the ma$aAjir , (T, TA,) erroneously said in the copies of the K to be like the ma$aAjib , (TA,) having no coverings, or canopies: the sing. is tawo'amapN . (T, K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. tafavN , He left off, or abstained from, anointing himself, and shaving his pubes, and in consequence became dirty: (Msb:) or tafavN signifies the state of being dirty; (Mgh;) the state of having matted and dusty hair, or a dusty head, long left unanointed: (T, Mgh, K:) so in relation to the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage: (T, K:) thus explained by ISh; but not by any [other] of the lexicologists: he says that it is one of the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; (T;) which is a conventional term of the professors, or lecturers, of the colleges: (Mgh:) accord. to I'Ab, it signifies the shaving, and shortening, or clipping, of the beard and mustache and [ the hair of ] the armpit, and slaughtering [ of the victims ], and casting [ of the pebbles ]: accord. to Fr, the slaughtering of the [ victims termed ] budon , and other victims, namely, kine, and sheep or goats, and shaving the head, and paring the nails, and the like: (T:) AO says that no poem is adduced as presenting an ex. of it: (Msb, TA:) and Zj says that it is not known by the lexicologists except from the expositors of the Kur-án; (T, M;) who say that it is the clipping the mustache, and paring the nails, and plucking out the hair of the armpit, and shaving the pubes, and clipping the hair [ of the head ]: (T:) or the plucking out the hair, and paring of the nails, and deviating from all that is prohibited to the muHorim : (M:) as though it were a passing from the state of A_iHoraAm to the state of A_iHolaAl : (T, M:) or, in the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage, the doing such things as paring the nails, and clipping the mustache, and shaving the pubes (S, K) and the head, and casting the pebbles, and slaughtering the budon , (S,) &c.: (S, K: [but in two copies of the S, this art. is omitted:]) or the doing away with the matted and dusty state of the hair, and pollution and dirt, absolutely. (TA.) Accord. to ISh, qaDaA='u Alt~afavi means The doing away with the matted and dusty state of the hair by shaving, and paring the nails, and the like: (T:) or it means the doing away with the state of tafav , by clipping the mustache, and paring the nails, and plucking out the hair of the armpit, and shaving the pubes. (Mgh.) Accord. to IAar, vum~a liyaqoDuwA tafavahumo [in the Kur xxii. 30] means Then let them accomplish their needful acts of shaving and cleansing: (T:) or it means then let them do away with their dirtiness, by clipping the mustache, and paring the nails, and plucking out the hair of the armpit, and shaving the pubes, on the occasion of A_iHolaAl : (Bd:) it is an allowance, after entering the state of A_iHolaAl , of that which was forbidden them in the state of A_iHoraAm . (Msb.) ― -b2- fatafavati AldimaA='u makaAnahu occurs in a trad., meaning And the blood (lit. bloods ) contaminated the place thereof. (TA.)

Ait~iqaA='N (Msb) and [quasi-inf. n.] taqiy~apN and tuqaApN ; (S, art. wqY ;) He feared God: (S and TA in art. tqY : all else that follows is from art. wqY except where reference is made to another art.:) or he was cautious of a thing; guarded, or was on his guard, against it; prepared, prepared himself, or was in a state of preparation, against it; or feared it: (K:) or he looked forward to a thing, and guarded against it, sought to avoid it, or was cautious of it. (T, TA.) [For other explanations of the latter verb, which apply also to the former, see art. wqY .] ↓ Ait~aqaY is originally AiwotaqaY ; (T, S;) then AiytaqaY ; then Ait~aqaY ; and when this came to be much in use, they imagined the t to be a radical part of the word, and made the word AitaqaY , aor. yataqiY , with fet-h to the t in each case, and without teshdeed; and not finding any analogue to it in their language, they said taqaY , aor. yatoqiY , like qaDaY , aor. yaqoDiY : (S:) or, as is said in the T, they suppressed the t , and the Ait~aqaY changed into t , in Ait~aqaY , and said taqaY , aor. yatoqiY . (TA.) A poet says, (namely, Khufáf Ibn-Nudbeh, TA,) jalaAhaA AlS~ayoqaluwna faA^axolaSuwhaA xifaAfFA kul~uhaA yatoqiY biA^avori or, as some read it, yataqiY , with the t movent, but without teshdeed; (S;) and this latter, accord. to IB, is the right reading. (TA.) [See this verse explained in art. Avr .] IB adds that Aboo-Sa'eed [app. meaning As] disallowed taqaY , aor. yatoqiY , inf. n. taqoYN ; saying that it would require the imperative to be Aitoqi , which is not said; and this, he states, is right: [for] J says that the imperative used is taqi [ Fear thou, or beware thou, &c.], as in taqi A@ll~`hi [ Fear thou God ]; and to a woman, taqiY ; formed from the verb AitaqaY , without tesh-deed, by the suppression of the A . (TA.)
