definition: , or taqowFY , accord.
sourceDefinition: , or taqowFY , accord. to different readings in the Kur ix. 110, (Bd,) [of which readings the former is the more common,] is originally taqoyaA , (K,) [or taqoyFA ,] or [rather waqoyaA , or waqoyFA , and then] waqowaY , of the measure faEolaY , from waqayotu , (ISd, TA,) or, accord. to MF, the right opinion is that it is [ waqowFY ,] of the measure faEowalN , (TA,) and is thus transformed in order to make a distinction between the subst. and the epithet such as xazoyaA and SadoyaA : (K:) it is a subst. from Ait~aqaY or waqaY ; (Msb, K;) [and signifies Fear; caution; &c.: (see 1:) and particularly reverential, or pious, fear of God: or simply piety: or the preservation, or guarding, of oneself, accord. to some, exceedingly, or extraordinarily, from sin, either of commission or of omission: or the preservation, or guarding, of oneself from punishment in the world to come, and from acts of disobedience, by righteous conduct: or righteousness, virtue, justice, or honesty: (see taqiY~N :) its explanations in relation to religion are many and various, but are all resolvable into fear of God, or of sin; or the preservation, or guarding, of oneself from sin: ] and ↓ taqiy~apN and ↓ tuqaApN are syn. with each other (S) and with taqoway , (Msb,) and are used as inf. ns. of Ait~aqaY : (S:) and ↓ tuqFY [also] is syn. with taqoway ; (S;) or it is pl. of ↓ tuqaApN , or a coll. n., (Kzz, IB, Msb,) like as TulFY is of TulaApN , (Kzz, IB,) and as ruTabN is of ruTabapN . (Msb.) waA=taAhumo taqowaAhumo , in the Kur xlvii. 19, means And hath explained to them, (Bd,) or suggested to them, (Jel, TA,) what they should fear, or that from which they should preserve themselves: (Bd, Jel, TA:) or hath aided them to practise their taqowaY : (Bd:) or hath given them the recompense of their tqwY . definition: ― -b2- Alv~uray~aA [ The Pleiades;
sourceDefinition: : see variY~N . ― -b2- Alv~uray~aA [ The Pleiades; the Third Mansion of the Moon: it is believed to be the most beneficial, in its influences on the weather, of all the Mansions of the Moon, on account of the period of its auroral setting, which, in central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, began on the 12th of Nov., O. S.: (see manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl ; and see also nawo'N :) hence what is said of it in Job xxxviii. 31; and hence, as being the most excellent of all asterisms, it is called by the Arabs] Aln~ajomu [ the Asterism ]: (S, K:) the former appellation is given to it because it comprises, in appearance, many stars in a small space; (M, K; *) for it is said that amid its conspicuous stars are many obscure stars; (IAth, TA;) the number altogether being said to be four and twenty, agreeably with an assertion of the Prophet: some say that it is so called because of the abundance [of the rain] of its nawN' [here meaning auroral setting]: (TA:) the word is thus applied only in the dim. form, which is used in this instance to denote magnification. (M, TA.) ― -b3- [ vuray~aA also signifies (tropical:) A cluster of lamps, generally resting in holes in the bottom of a lantern: see an engraving in my “Modern Egyptians,” ch. vi.] The vuray~aA of lamps is so called as being likened to the asterism above mentioned. (M.)

definition: The price of a thing;
sourceDefinition: The price of a thing; i. e. the thing that the seller receives in return for the thing sold, whether money or a commodity; (Er-Rághib, TA;) the vaman of a thing sold: (S:) and also (Er-Rághib, TA) a compensation, or substitute, (Mgh, Msb, Er-Rághib, TA,) whatever it be, for a thing, (Er-Rághib, TA,) i. e., for a thing that is sold; but in the sense commonly known, such as it is incumbent upon one to pay, of pieces of silver, and of gold [ or other money ]; not commodities and the like: (Mgh:) or the value, or worth, of a thing; (K;) its qiymap : (T:) or the estimated value, or worth, of a thing, by mutual consent, even though it be really excessive or deficient; whereas the qiymap is its real value or worth, its equivalent: (MF:) pl. A^avomaAnN (T, Mgh, Msb, K) and A^avomunN , (S, Msb, K,) the latter used only as a pl. of pauc., (Msb,) and [so] A^avominapN . (CK: not in the TA.) definition: a noun of number, well known;
sourceDefinition: a noun of number, well known; [meaning Eight; ] as also ↓ vamaAnK , (M, TA,) which is like yamaAnK , (M, K,) in form: (M:) the former is the masc. form: the latter, the fem.: (Msb:) this is not a rel. n. [though likened above to yamaAnK ]: (M, K:) or it is originally a rel. n. from Alv~umunu , because it is the part, or portion, that makes seven to be eight, so that it is its eighth: they make the first letter to be pronounced with fet-h, because they make changes [in some other cases] in the rel. n., (S, K,) as when they say suholiY~N and duhoriY~N , [which are rel. ns. of saholN and dahorN ,] (S,) and they suppress one of the two Y which are characteristic of the rel. n., and compensate it by the insertion of A , as they do in the rel. n. of Alyamanu [when they say yamaAnK , originally yamaAniYN , for yamaniY~N ]: (S, K: [and the like is said in the Mgh:]) El-Fárisee says that the A of vamaAnK is the characteristic of the rel. n., because this word is not a broken pl. like SaHaArK ; and IF assents to this, and says that were it not so, the p would be inseparable, as it is in EabaAqiyapN &c. (M.) You say vamaAniyapu rijaAlK [ Eight men ], (T, S, Mgh,) and vamaAniyapu A^ay~aAmK [ eight days ]. (Msb.) And when vmAn is prefixed to another noun, its Y is retained, like the Y in AlqaADiY : (S, Msb, K:) and it is decl. in the same manner as words of the class to which this last belongs: (Msb:) you say vamaAniY nisowapK [ Eight women ], (T, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and vamaAniY miAy^apK [ eight hundred ], (S, Msb, K,) [in the nom. and gen. cases;] and raA^ayotu vamaAniYa nisowapK [ I saw eight women ], pronouncing the fet-hah [at the end, in this case]. (Msb.) When it is with tenween, the Y is dropped in the nom. and gen. cases, but it is retained in the accus. case: (S, K:) [i. e.,] when the fem. form is not prefixed to another noun, you say, EinodiY mina Aln~isaA='i vamaAnK [ I have with me, of women, eight ], and mararotu minohun~a bivamaAnK [ I passed by, of them, eight ], and raA^ayotu vamaAniyFA [ I saw eight ]. (Msb.) It sometimes occurs, in poetry, indecl.: (S, M:) this is because it is fancied to be a pl.; (S;) or because it is likened, as to the letter, but not as to the meaning, to jawaAriYa . (M.) The people of El-Hijáz pronounce the masc. and the fem. with nasb in every case, in phrases like A^atawoniY valaAvatahumo and A^atayonaniY valaAvahun~a ; and so on to ten [inclusive]. (S voce valaAvapN , q. v.) Th mentions ↓ vamaAnN ; (TA;) and some instances of its occurrence are cited; but As disallows it. (T, Mgh, TA.) kisaA='N *uw vamaAnK means A [ garment of the kind called ] ksA' made of eight fleeces. (T.) tuqobilu biA^arobaEK watudobiru bivamaAnK [ She advances with four and goes back with eight ] is a saying of one of the muxan~avuwn of El-Medeeneh; meaning, with four creases ( Eukan ) of the belly, and with eight extremities thereof; each crease having two extremities, towards the two sides of the woman spoken of. (Mgh in art. hyt .) The saying Alv~awobu saboEN fiY vamaAnK should properly be fiY vamaAniyapK , (S,) which means, The garment, or piece of cloth, is seven cubits in length by eight spans in breadth; (Msb;) because the length is measured by the *iraAE , which is fem., and the breadth by the $ibor , which is masc.; but they use the fem. when they do not mention things; as when they say, SumonaA mina Al$~ahori xamosFA [We fasted, of the month, five], though meaning days: (S:) or because *rAE is fem. in most instances, and $br is masc. (Msb.) [But it is said that when vmAnyp means the things numbered, not the amount of the number, it is imperfectly decl., being regarded as a proper name: thus] you say, tisoEapu A^akovaru mino vamaAniyapa [ Nine things are more than eight things ]. (TA voce tisoEapN , q. v.) [See also sit~apN .] ― -b2- When you make it a compound [with the number ten], you say, EinodaY vamaAniyapa Ea$ara rajulFA [ I have with me eighteen men ]: and in the case of the fem., you may either make the Y to be with fet-h or make it quiescent, saying, EinodiY mina Aln~isaA='i vamaAniYa Ea$orapa A@moraA^apF or vamaAniYoEa$orapa [ I have with me, of women, eighteen women ]; but the former is the more chaste; and in one dial., the Y is elided, on the condition of [saying vamaAna Ea$orapa ,] making the n to be with fet-h; (Msb;) or in this case you say vamaAni Ea$orapa , with kesr. (T.) A poet says, (T, S,) namely, El-Aashà, (K,) falaA^a$oraban~a vamaAniyFA wavamaAniyFA wavamaAni Ea$orapa waA@vonatayoni waA^arobaEaA [ And I will assuredly drink eight cups of wine, (a pl. of kaA^os , which is fem., being understood,) and eight more, and eighteen, and two, and four ]: (T, S, K: but in the S and K, walaqado $aribotu ; and in the K, and in one copy of the S, wavamaAna :) he should properly have said vamaAniYa Ea$orapa or vamaAniYo Ea$orapa , (accord. to different copies of the T and S and K,) but he elides the Y after the dial. of him who says TiwaAlu AlA^ayodi [for AlA^ayodiY ], (S, K,) and he makes the n to be with kesr in order to indicate the Y . (T.) ― -b3- The dim. of vamaAniyapN may be formed either by suppressing the A , which is the preferable way, so that you say ↓ vumayoniyapN , or by suppressing the Y , saying ↓ vumay~inapN , changing the A into Y and incorporating into it the Y that is the characteristic of the dim.; and you may compensate for both [of these suppressed letters by saying ↓ vumayoniy~apN and ↓ vumay~iynapN ]. (S.) ― -b4- Alv~amaAniY is also the name of A certain plant. (As, T, K.)

definition: a well-known noun of number;
sourceDefinition: a well-known noun of number; [meaning Eighty; ] sometimes used as an epithet: ElAashà says, lay^ino kunota fiY jub~K vamaAniyna qaAmapF waruq~iyta A^asobaAba Als~imaA='i bisul~ami [ Assuredly if thou wert in a well eighty fathoms deep, and wert made to ascend the tracts of heaven by a ladder ]: he uses it thus as meaning deep. (TA. [But in this verse, as cited in the present art in the TA, A^abowaAba is put in the place of AsbAb , which is the reading commonly known, and given in the S and TA in art. sb , and in the TA in art rqY -]) A^aHomaqu mino SaAHabi DaA^onK vamaAniyna [ More stupid than an owner of eighty sheep ], (S, K,) or mino raAEiY DaA^onK vamaAniyna [ than a pastor of eighty sheep ], as in some of the copies of the S, or, as in the Proverbs of Aboo-'Obeyd, mino TaAlibi DaA^onK vamaAniyna [ than a demander of eighty sheep ], (TA,) is a saying that originated from the fact that an Arab of the desert announced to Kisrà an event that rejoiced him, whereupon he said, “ Ask of me what thou wilt; ” and he asked of him eighty sheep. (S, K.) ― -b2- [It also signifies Eightieth. ]

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. jad~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He cut it, or cut it off. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) This is the primary signification. (Mgh.) You say of a weaver, jad~a vawobFA He cut off a piece of cloth [sufficient for a garment or the like, from the web]. (S, K.) And jad~a Aln~axola , (S, Mgh, L,) aor, , (S, L,) inf. n. jad~N (S, L, K) and jadaAdN (Lh, Mgh, L) and jidaAdN ; (Lh, L; [in the L, the last two forms are mentioned as inf. ns., and the former of them is mentioned as inf. n. in the Mgh; but in the K, they are only mentioned as syn. with jad~N ; and in the S, it seems to be implied that they are simple substs., or quasiinf. ns.;]) i. q. Saramahu ; (Lh, S, Mgh, K; *) [like ja*~ahu and jaz~ahu ;] i.e., He cut off the fruit of the palm-trees. (Mgh, L. [See also jadaAdN .]) And jud~ato A^axolaAfu Aln~aAqapi The she-camel's teats were cut off by some accident that befell her: (As, TA:) or, in consequence of injury occasioned to her by the SiraAr [q. v.]. (S.) And tajodiydN [inf. n. of ↓ jd~d ] signifies The cutting off the teat of a camel. (KL.) You say also, jud~a vadoyaA A^um~ika May thy mother's breasts be cut off: a form of imprecation against a man; and implying a wish for his separation. (As, L, from a trad.) ― -b2- See also 5. -A2- jad~a , aor. , inf. n. jid~apN , It (a garment, TA, or a thing, S, Msb, TA) was new; (S, L, Msb, K;) [as though newly cut off from the web; ] from jad~a as signifying “ he cut, ” or “ cut off. ” (L.) [See also 5.] -A3- jad~a , like taEiba , (Msb,) see. pers. jadidNta , [like its syn. HaZiZota ,] (L, Msb,) aor. yajad~u ; (Msb;) or jud~a , with damm, (Mgh,) see. pers. judidota , (S,) [aor. yujad~u ;] inf. n. jad~N ; (S, * Mgh, L, Msb;) He was, or became, fortunate, or possessed of good fortune, (S, Mgh, L, Msb,) or of good worldly fortune; (TA;) he advanced in the world, or in worldly circumstances; (Mgh;) biAlA^amori by the affair, or event, whether good or evil; (L;) or biAl$~aYo'i by the thing. (Msb.) And humo yujad~uwna bihimo , as also yuHaZ~uwna bhm , They become possessed of good fortune, and riches, or competence, or sufficiency. (Ibn-Buzurj, L.) [You say also, jad~a jad~uhu (tropical:) : so in a copy of the A: probably a mistranscription for jad~a jid~uhu , which see below: if not, meaning His fortune became good; or his good fortune increased in goodness: or, perhaps, his dignity became great; from what next follows]. -A4- jad~ fiY EayoniY , (S, A,) or fiY Euyuwni Aln~aAsi , and Suduwrihimo , (Mgh,) aor. , inf. n. jad~N , (S,) He was, or became, great, or of great dignity or estimation, in my eye, or in the eyes of men, and their minds. (S, A, Mgh.) It is said in a trad. of Anas, kaAna Alr~ajulu min~aA A_i*aA qaraA^a Albaqarapa waA=la EimoraAna jad~a fiynaA , i. e., [ A man of us, when he recited the chapter of the Cow and that of the Family of 'Imrán (the second and third chapters of the Kur-án),] used to be great in our eyes. (S.) -A5- jad~a fiY AlA^amori , (S, A, K,) or fiY A^amorihi , (L,) or fiY kalaAmihi , (Msb,) aor. (S, L, Msb, K) and , (L, K,) inf. n. jid~N , (S, K,) or jad~N , (L, Msb,) jid~N being a simple subst.; (Msb;) and fiyhi ↓ Ajd~ ; (L, K;) He was serious, or in earnest, (S, A, L, Msb, K,) in the affair, (S, A, K,) or in his affair, (L,) or in his speech; (Msb;) syn. Haq~aqa ; (L;) contr. of hazala . (L, Msb. [In the S and A and K, the inf. n. is said to signify the contr. of hazolN ; and in the K, it is also said to be syn. with taHoqiyqN .]) ― -b2- And jad~a fiY AlA^amori , (As, S, L, Msb, K,) aor. and , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. jid~N , (S, * K, * TA,) or this is a simple subst., and the inf. n. is jad~N ; (Msb;) and fyh ↓ Ajd~ ; (As, S, L, K;) signify also He strove, laboured, or toiled; exerted himself or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; employed himself vigorously, strenuously, laboriously, diligently, studiously, sedulously, earnestly, or with energy; was diligent, or studious; took pains, or extraordinary pains; in the affair. (As, S, L, Msb, K.) And jad~afiY Als~ayori He strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, in going, or journeying, or in his course, or pace; (tropical:) he hastened therein: and in like manner, Als~ayora ↓ Ajd~ (assumed tropical:) he hastened his course, or pace. (L.) And jad~a jid~uhu , [meaning His labour, or exertion, or energy, was, or became, great, or extraordinary: or] meaning AizodaAda jid~uhu jid~FA [ his labour, &c., increased in labour, &c.]: or it may mean what was not [ his ] jid~ , became jid~ ; wherefore, i. e. because it would be so eventually, it is here so called. (Ham p. 33. [See also jad~a jad~uhu , above.] ― -b3- jad~a bihi AlA^amoru (A, L) (tropical:) The affair, or event, distressed, or afflicted, him. (L.) So in the saying of Aboo-Sahm, A^axaAlidu laA yaroDaY Eani AlEabodi rab~uhu A_i*aA jad~a biAl$~ayoxi AlEuquwqu AlmuSam~imu [ O Khálid, his Lord will not approve of the servant, or man, (meaning the son,) when cutting, or biting, disobedience to a parent distresses the old man ]. (L.) -A6- jad~a , aor, inf. n. jad~N and jid~N , It (a house, or tent, bayot ) dripped, or let fall drops. (K.)

definition: Fortune, or particularly good fortune, syn.
sourceDefinition: Fortune, or particularly good fortune, syn. HaZ~N , (S, A, Mgh, L, K,) and baxotN , (S, A, L, K,) in the world, or in wordly circumstances; (TA;) advance in the world, or in worldly circumstances: (Mgh:) pl. [of mult.] juduwdN (S) and [of pauc.] A^ajodaAdN and A^ajud~N . (TA.) You say, fulaAnN *uw jad~K fiY ka*aA Such a one is possessed of good fortune in such a thing. (L.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the day of resurrection, waA_i*aA A^aSoHaAbu Aljad~i maHobuwsuwna And lo, the people who were possessed of good fortune and riches in the world were imprisoned. (L.) And in a prayer, (L,) laA yanofaEu *aA Aljad~i minoka Aljad~u The good worldly fortune of him who is possessed of such fortune will not profit him, (Mgh, L,) in the world to come, (L,) in lieu of Thee; (Mgh, L; *) i. e., of obedience to Thee: (Mgh, and Mughnee in art. mino :) or in lieu of the good fortune that cometh from Thee: or, as some say, will not defend him from Thee. (Mughnee ubi suprà. [See also another explanation below.]) Hence, A^ajad~aka laA tafoEalo [or A^ajad~ika ]; and, accord. to some, wajad~ika : see jid~N . ― -b2- One's lot in life; and the means of subsistence that one receives from the bounty of God. (L, K.) One says, lifulaAnK fiY h`*aA AlA^amori jad~N Such a one has in this thing, or state of affairs, means of subsistence. (A'Obeyd, L.) ― -b3- Richness; competence, or sufficiency; or the state of being in no need, or of having no wants, or of having few wants. (S, L, Msb.) lA ynfE *A Aljd~ mnk Aljd~ , [explained above, is said to mean] Riches, &c., will not profit the possessor thereof with Thee; for nothing will profit him but acting in obedience to Thee: mnk here signifies Einodaka . (S, Msb.) ― -b4- Greatness, or majesty; (Mujáhid, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) accord. to some, specially of God: (TA:) so in the Kur lxxii. 3: (S, TA:) or his freedom from all wants or the like; syn. ginFY . (S.) Hence, taEaAlaY jad~uka , (Mgh, TA,) in a trad. respecting prayer, (TA,) Exalted be thy greatness, or majesty. (Mgh, * TA.) ― -b5- See also A^ajad~aka , as an interrogative phrase, voce jid~N . -A2- Also, (S, K,) and ↓ majoduwdN , (S, A, Mgh, K,) and ↓ jadiydN , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ jad~iy~N , (S,) and ↓ jud~N , and ↓ jud~iy~N , the last two with damm, (K,) applied to a man, Fortunate; or possessed of good fortune; (S, A, Mgh, Msb;) or possessed of good worldly fortune: (TA:) or possessing great fortune, or great good fortune: (K:) [the words here given from the S are there coupled with synonyms of the same form, thus; ↓ jadiydN HaZiyZN , and maHoZuwZN ↓ majoduwdq , and jad~N HaZ~u , and HaZ~iY~N ↓ jad~iy~N ; on the authority of ISk:] ↓ jud~N , with damm, as an epithet applied to a man, is said by Sb to be syn. with majoduwdN ; and its pl. is jud~Nwna only. (L.) -A3- Also jad~u , A grandfather; the father's father, and the mother's father: (S, Msb, K:) and (assumed tropical:) a higher ascendant; an ancestor: (Msb:) and ↓ jad~apN a grandmother; the father's mother, and the mother's mother: (K:) [and (assumed tropical:) a female ancestor: ] pl. of the former, A^ajodaAdN [a pl. of pauc.] and juduwdN and juduwdapN : (K:) and of the latter, jad~aAtN . (TA.) Hence, accord. to some, wajad~ika laA tafoEalo : see jid~N . -A4- See also jud~apN : ― -b2- and see jadiydN .

definition: [accord. to some an inf. n., but accord. to others a simple subst., (see jad~a ,)] Seriousness, or earnestness, contr. of hazolN , (S, A, Msb, K,) in speech. (Msb.) Hence, valaAvN jid~uhun~a jid~N...
sourceDefinition: [accord. to some an inf. n., but accord. to others a simple subst., (see jad~a ,)] Seriousness, or earnestness, contr. of hazolN , (S, A, Msb, K,) in speech. (Msb.) Hence, valaAvN jid~uhun~a jid~N wahazoluhun~a jid~N [There are three things in relation to which what is serious is serious and what is jesting is serious ]: a saying of Mohammad, whereby he forbade a man's divorcing and emancipating and marrying and then retracting, saying “ I was jesting; ” as was customary in the time of paganism. (Msb.) A^ajid~aka and ↓ A^ajad~aka signify the same; (S;) but the former is the more chaste; (TA;) jid~ and jad~ being thus used only as prefixed nouns: (S, K:) As says that the meaning is, A^abijid~K minoka h`*aA [ Does this proceed from thee in seriousness, or in earnest? ]; and that jid~ is put in the accus. case because of the rejection of the [prep.] b : AA says that the meaning is, maA laka A^ajid~FA minoka [ What aileth thee? Doth it proceed from thee in seriousness, or in earnest? ]; and that jd~ is put in the accus. case as an inf. n.: Th says that the phrase as it occurs in poetry is A^ajid~aka , with kesr: (S:) but when it occurs with wa [in the place of A^a , or with A^a in the sense of wa , as a particle denoting an oath,] it is ↓ wajad~ika [or A^ajad~ika ], with fet-h: (S, K:) yon say, wajad~ika laA tafoEalo , (K, in the CK wajad~aka ,) meaning, By thy grandfather, do not [such a thing]: or by thy fortune, or good fortune, do not: (TA:) also, when you say, A^ajid~aka laA tafoEalo , [or A^ajid~ika , for A^a (q. v.) is substituted for a particle of swearing, as in A^all~`hi laA^afoEalan~a ,] the meaning is, I adjure thee by thy truth, (Lth, K,) and by thy seriousness, or earnestness, (Lth, TA,) do not: and when you say, laA tafoEalo ↓ A^ajad~aka , [or A^ajad~ika ,] the meaning is, I adjure thee by thy fortune, or good fortune, do not: (Lth, K:) Aboo- 'Alee Esh-Shalowbeenee asserts that it implies the signification of an oath. (MF.) In the phrase Ajd~k lA tafoEalu , AAF says, we may consider lA tfEl as put in the place of a denotative of state; or the phrase may be originally Ajd~k A^ano laA tafoEala , An being suppressed, and its government annulled: [therefore it may be rendered, in the former case, Is it with seriousness on thy part, thou doing such a thing? and in the latter case, Is it with seriousness on thy part that thou will not do such a thing? i. e. dost thou mean seriously that thou will not do it? or in this case, Ajd~k may be used as a form of adjuration in one of the senses explained above, and laA tafoEalu may mean, that thou do not such a thing; or Ajd~k may mean wajad~aka , (explained above, and so in the three exs. below,) and laA tafoEalu , thou wilt not do it:] and, as AHei says, there is here a nice point, which is this; that the noun [meaning the pronoun] to which jd~ is prefixed should agree in person with the verb which follows it; so that one should say, Ajd~iY laA A^ukorimuka , and Ajd~ka laA tafoEalu , and Ajd~hu laA yazuwrunaA ; because jd~ is an inf. n. corroborating the proposition that follows it. (MF.) ― -b2- Also, [and in this case, likewise, accord. to some an inf. n., but accord. to others a simple subst., (see, again, jad~a ,)] A striving, labour, or toil; exertion of one's self, or of one's power or efforts or endeavours or ability; vigorousness, strenuousness, laboriousness, diligence, studiousness, sedulousness, earnestness, or energy; painstaking, or extraordinary painstaking; (S, L, Msb, K;) in affairs, (S,) or in an affair. (Msb, K.) Hence, jid~FA [meaning In a great, or an extraordinary, degree; greatly, much, exceedingly, or extraordinarily; very; very greatly, or very much; extremely ]; as in the phrase, (Msb,) fulaAnN muHosinN jid~FA [ Such a one is beneficent in a great, or an extraordinary, degree; very, exceedingly, or extremely, beneficent ]: you should not say jad~FA . definition: The bank, or side, or a river;
sourceDefinition: The bank, or side, or a river; as also jid~apN and ↓ jid~N (IAth, L, K) and ↓ jud~N (IAth, Mgh, L) and ↓ jad~N , (Mgh, L, K,) accord. to some, but correctly jud~N ; so called because cut off from the river, or because cut by the water, in like manner as it is called saAHilN because it is abraded by the water: (Mgh:) or the part of a river that is near the land; as also ↓ jid~apN : (L:) and the shore of the sea: (MF:) accord. to As, jd~p is an arabicized word from the Nabathean kd~ . (L.) ― -b2- The stripe, or streak, that is on the back of the ass, differing from his general colour. (S, A, * K.) And (tropical:) A streak (Fr, S, K, TA) in anything, (TA,) as in a mountain, (Fr, S,) differing in colour from the rest of the mountain, (S,) white and black and red; (Fr, TA;) as also in the sky: (A, TA:) pl. judadN , (Fr, S,) occurring in the Kur xxxv. 25; (S;) where some read jududN , pl. of ↓ jdydp [app. jadiydapN ], which is syn. with jud~apN ; and some, jadadN [q. v.]. (Bd.) ― -b3- A sign, or mark, syn. EalaAmapN , (Th, K,) of, or in, anything. (Th, TA.) ― -b4- A beaten way, marked with lines [ cut by the feet of the men and beasts that have travelled along it ]: (Az, L:) or a road, or way: pl. judadN : (Msb:) and juduwdN , also, [app. another pl. of jud~apN ,] signifies paths, or tracks, forming lines upon the ground. (Az, L.) See also jaAd~apN . ― -b5- [Hence, app., but accord. to the S from the same word as signifying “a streak,”] rakiba jud~apF mina AlA^amori , (S, A, TA,) or jud~apa AlA^amori , (K,) (tropical:) He set upon a way, or manner, of performing the affair: (A:) or he formed an opinion respecting the affair, or case. (Zj, S, A, K.) ― -b6- See also jid~apN .

sourceDefinition: Hard ground: (S:) or hard level ground: (Har p. 522:) [see also jadojadN :] or rough level ground: (K:) or rough ground: or level ground: (TA:) or a level and spacious tract of land; a tract such as is called SaHoraA=' , and such as is called faDaA=' , containing no soft place in which the feet sink, nor any mountain, nor any [ hill such as is called ] A^akamap ; sometimes wide, and sometimes of little width: (ISh:) [and] a conspicuous road: (Bd in xxxv. 25:) pl. definition: and ↓ jidaAdN The cutting off of the fruit of palm-trees.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ jidaAdN The cutting off of the fruit of palm-trees. (S, * A, * L, Msb, * K. *) You say, h`*aA zamanu AljadaAdi and AljidaAdi [ This is the time, or season, of the cutting off of the fruit of the palmtrees ]. (S, A, Msb. *) Some say that jdAd signifies particularly [as above,] the cutting off [of the fruit] of palm-trees; and j*A* , the cutting off of all fruits, in a general sense: others say that they signify the same. (S.)

(TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (L,) applied to a garment, (L, TA,) or a thing, (S, Msb,) New; contr. of qadiymN , (Msb,) or contr. of xalaqN ; (S, L;) from jid~apN as contr. of bilFY : (K:) pl. definition: The kind of pad, or stuffed thing, ( rifaAdapN ,) and the felt, stuck, or attached, beneath the two boards of a horse's saddle: there are two such things, called jadiydataAni : (S:) or the jdydtAn...
sourceDefinition: The kind of pad, or stuffed thing, ( rifaAdapN ,) and the felt, stuck, or attached, beneath the two boards of a horse's saddle: there are two such things, called jadiydataAni : (S:) or the jdydtAn consist of the felt that is stuck, or attached, in the inner side of a horse's and of a camel's saddle: (L:) but jdydp thus applied is a post-classical word: the [classical] Arabs say jadoyapN , (S,) or, as in J's own handwriting, jadiy~apN . (So in the margin of a copy of the S.) -A2- See also jud~apN .

sourceDefinition: [The cricket; ] i. q. sourceDefinition: act. part. n. of jad~a ; (Mgh, L;) Cutting, or cutting off. (Mgh.) -A2- A^ajaAd~u A^anota A^amo haAzilN Art thou serious or jesting? (A.) It is said in a trad., laA yaA^oxu*an~a A^aHadukumo mataAEa A^axiyhi laAEibFA jaAd~FA [ By no means shall any one of you take the property of his brother in play and in earnest ]; by which is meant taking a thing without meaning to steal it, but meaning to vex and anger the owner, so that the taker is in play with respect to theft, but in earnest in annoying. (TA in art. lEb .) ― -b2- fulaAnN jaAd~N Such a one is striving, labouring, or toiling; exerting himself or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; &c. (TA.) And ↓ fulaAnN jaAd~N mujid~N , thus with the two similar words together, (As, S, L,) signifies the same [in an intensive degree]. (L, TA.) -A3- jaAd~u miAy^api wasoqK Land, or palm-trees, of which the produce, cut therefrom, is a hundred camel-loads: jaAd~N being here used in the sense of ↓ majoduwdN . (L.) It is said in a trad. of Aboo-Bekr, Ei$oriyna wasoqFA ↓ nahala EaAy^i$apa jidaAda , meaning He gave to 'Áïsheh palm-trees of which the quantity of the dates cut therefrom was a hundred camel-loads; but the phrase heard from the Arabs is jaAd~a Ei$oriyna : the former is like the saying h`*ihi Ald~araAhimu Darobu AlA^amiyri ; and the latter, like Eiy$apN raADiyapN . (Mgh.)

definition: The main part of a road;
sourceDefinition: The main part of a road; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) its middle: (Mgh, Msb, and M voce jarajap :) or its even part: or the beaten track, or part along which one walks, or travels; the conspicuous part thereof: or a main road that comprises other roads, or tracks, and upon which one must pass: (TA:) or a road, or way, absolutely; as also ↓ jud~apN : (Zj, MF:) or a road leading to water: (AHn, TA:) it is so called because it is marked with tracks, forming lines: (T, TA:) pl. jawaAd~N , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) occurring in poetry without teshdeed, but disapproved by As. (L.) fulaAnN EalaY AljaAd~api means (assumed tropical:) Such a one is following the right course of action or the like. (Mgh.) You say also, huwa EalaY jaAd~api AlHaq~i (assumed tropical:) [ He is on the road, or main road, of truth ]: not, however, EalaY jaAd~api AlbaATili , but ElY mazal~api AlbaATili , and mazolaqatihi , and maholakatihi . (MF.)

(TA in art. d$ .)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yajil~u , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. jalaAlapN , (S,) or jalaAlN , (K, [in the CK, erroneously, julAlFA is put for jalaAlFA ,]) or both, (TA, [but see what follows,]) and jul~aY , (Ham p. 218, see this word below, under jalalN ,) [in its primary sense, It was, or became, thick, gross, coarse, rough, rugged, rude, big, or bulky: (see jaliylN :) and then,] it, (a thing, Msb,) or he (a man, S) was, or became, great; (S, Msb, K, TA;) [said of a thing, meaning in size; and] said of a man, meaning in estimation, rank, or dignity: (S, TA:) or jalaAlapN signifies greatness of estimation or rank or dignity: but jalaAlN , supreme greatness thereof: (Er-Rághib, TA:) the latter is an attribute of God only; (As in Ham p. 607, Er-Rághib, TA;) except in few instances: (As ubi suprà:) or it means the greatness, or majesty, of God: (S, Msb:) or his absolute independence. (Bd in lv. 27.) sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tajoliylN , said of a thing, i. q. Eam~a [as meaning It included persons, or things, &c., in common, or generally, or universally, within the compass of its influence, or effects ]. (S, TA.) So in the phrase saHaAbN yujal~ilu AlA^aroDa biAlmaTari [ Clouds that include the land in common, or generally, or universally, within the compass of their rain; i. e., that rain upon the land throughout its general, or universal, extent ]: (S, TA:) or, as in the A, thundering clouds, covering the land with rain. (TA.) And so in the phrase, jal~ala AlmaTaru AlA^aroDa The rain included the general, or universal, extent of the land within the compass of its fall; and covered the land so as not to leave anything uncovered. (IF, Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, [in a general sense,] He covered a thing. (Msb.) It [or he ] ascended, rose, mounted, got, was, or became, upon, or over, a thing; (Ham p. 45;) as also ↓ tajl~l . (S, K.) ― -b3- He clad a horse (S, K) or beast (K) with a jul~ [or covering for protection from the cold ]; (S, K;) as also ↓ jal~a . (K.)

definition: The greater, main, principal, or chief, part of a thing;

You say, A^axa*a jul~ahu (K, TA) and ↓ julaAlahu (S, Sgh, K) [ He took the greater part of it ]. -A2- A horse-cloth, or covering (Msb, K,) of a horse or similar beast, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) for protection (Msb, K) from the cold; (Msb;) as also ↓ jal~N : (K:) [in Persian jalo :] pl. definition: A great, momentous, or formidable, thing, affair, matter, case, or event;
sourceDefinition: A great, momentous, or formidable, thing, affair, matter, case, or event; as also ↓ jul~aY (S, K, TA) and ↓ jul~aA='u : (TA:) or ↓ julaY [as also jalalN and ↓ jul~aA='u ] signifies a hard, difficult, severe, or distressing, and a great, momentous, or formidable, thing, or affair, &c.: (Msb:) pl. [of jalalN ,] A^ajolaAlN ; (TA;) and of ↓ julalN jul~aY ; (S, K.) El-Hárith Ibn-Waaleh says, qawomiY humu qataluwA A^umayoma A^axiY faA_i*aA ramayotu yuSiybuniY sahomiY falay^ino Eafawotu laA^aEofuwano jalalFA walay^ino saTwotu laA^uwohinano EaZomiY [ My people, they have slain, O Umeymeh, ( A^umayoma being apocopated, for A^umayomapu ,) my brother; so, if I shoot, my arrow will strike me; and verily, if I forgive, I shall indeed forgive a great thing; but verily, if I assault, I shall indeed weaken my bone: see Ham p. 97]. (S.) And Beshámeh Ibn-Hazn says, wamakorumapF ↓ waA_ino daEawota A_ilaY jul~aY yawomFA saraApF kiraAma Aln~aAsi faA@doEiynaA [ And if thou invite to a great affair, and a generous act, any day, manly and noble persons, the generous of mankind, invite us ]: (TA:) or jul~aY is here an inf. n. in the place of jalaAlN and jalaAlapN , like rujoEaY , &c. (Ham p. 218.) ― -b2- Also, i. e., jalalN , A small, (K,) an easy, or a mean, paltry, or contemptible, thing, affair, matter, case, or event: (S, K, TA:) thus bearing two contr. significations. (S, K.) Imra-el-Keys says, on the occasion of his father's having been slain, A^alaA kul~u $aYo'K siwaAhu jalalo bi qatoli baniY A^asadK rab~ahumN meaning [ By Benoo-Asad's slaying their lord: now surely everything beside it is ] a mean, paltry, or small, matter. (S, * TA.) ― -b3- faEalotu *`lika mino jalalika I did that on account of thee, for thy sake, or because of thee; syn. mino A^ajolika ; (S, K *) as also ↓ mn jul~ika , (K,) and ↓ mn jalaAlika , (S, K,) and ↓ mn tajil~atika , and ↓ mn A_ijolaAlika , and mn A^ajoli ↓ A_ijolaAlika . (K.) Jemeel says, rasomu daArK waqafotu fiY Talaliho kidotu A^aqoDiY AlgidApa mino jalalipo meaning [ The remains marking the site of a house, I paused at the relic thereof that was still standing: I almost died, in the early morning, ] on account of it ( mino A^ajolihi ), or, as some say, because of its greatness in my eye. (S.) -A2- Accord. to Zj, jalalo is a particle syn. with naEamo . (Mughnee.)

definition: , in its primary acceptation, signifies Thick, gross, coarse, rough, rugged, rude, big, or bulky;
sourceDefinition: , in its primary acceptation, signifies Thick, gross, coarse, rough, rugged, rude, big, or bulky; applied to a material substance; (Er-Rághib, TA;) opposed to daqiyqN ; (S, Er-Rághib, TA;) as also ↓ jil~N , (S,) opposed to diq~N : (S, K:) [and then,] great; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ jil~N and ↓ jal~N (K) and ↓ julaAlN , (S, K,) which is also explained as signifying large, big, bulky, or large in body, (K,) and ↓ jul~aAlN : fem. jaliylapN and ↓ julaAlapN : (K:) [also] great in respect of estimation, rank, or dignity: (S, TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^ajil~apN and jil~apN and [of mult.] A^ajil~aA='u . (TA.) You say, ↓ maA lahu diq~N y^alaA jil~N , i. e., daqiyqN walaA jaliylN [ He has neither slender, or fine, or small, nor thick, or gross, or coarse, &c., or great ]. (S.) And ↓ $ajarN jil~N [ Large trees; or trees as ] opposed to $ajarN diq~N [or shrubs, or bushes ]. (Lth, Mgh in art. bql .) And ↓ Hulalu jil~K Thick, or coarse, [ garments, or dresses, of the kind called ] Hulal ; opposed to Hulalu diq~N : (Mgh in art. dq :) or the things termed jil~N , of commodities, are carpets, and [the garments called ] A^akosiyap [pl. of kisaA=' ], and the like; (K;) contr. of diq~N ; such as the [ cloth called ] Hilos , and the mat, and the like. (TA.) And ↓ julaAlapN signifies A great she-camel; (S, K;) big-bodied. (TA.) You say also, TaHatapu TaHonFA jaliylFA [ He ground it coarsely ]. (S in art. j$ .) Aljaliylu , meaning The great in dignity, is not applied peculiarly to God: when it is applied to Him, it is because of his creating the great things that are indicative of Him, or because He is too great to be comprehended within limits or to be perceived by the senses. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And qawomN jil~apN means A great people; lords, chiefs, or people of rank or quality; (K;) a good people; (TA;) a people of eminence, nobility, dignity, or high rank. (K.) ― -b2- Also Old, or advanced in age, and firm, or sound, in judgment: pl. jil~apN : (K:) which pl., as meaning old, or advanced in age, is applied to camels, (S, Sgh, K,) as well as to men. (K.) Hence, in a trad., faA@EotaraDa lahumo A_iboliysu fiY Suwarpi $ayoxK jaliylK [ And Iblees presented himself to them in the form of an old man advanced in age ]. (TA.) ↓ jil~apN in the sense last explained above, is also used as a sing., and is applied to the male and the female [of camels]: or signifies such as is termed vaniy~ap , [i. e., a she-camel that has entered her sixth year, ] until she has become a baAzil [ in her ninth year ]: or a male camel that has become a vaniY~ : or it is applied to a she-camel, and ↓ jil~N to a he-camel. (K.) And [the fem.] ↓ jaliylapN [used as a subst.] signifies A she-camel that has brought forth once: (S, O, K:) and [simply] a she-camel; as in the saying, maA lahu jaliylapN walaA daqiyqapN He has neither a she-camel nor a ewe, or she-goat: (S:) or camels. (JK and TA in art. dq [q. v., voce daqiyqN ].) Also (i. e. ↓ jlylp ) A great palm-tree having much fruit: pl. jaliylN ; (K;) [or rather this is a coll. gen. n.;] or, accord. to some copies of the K, the pl. is jilaAlN . (TA.) -A2- Also i. q. vumaAmN [ Panicum, or panic grass ]; (S, K;) a weak plant, with which the interstices of houses are stopped up: n. un. with p : (S:) or ↓ jaliylapN signifies a species of vumaAm : (TA in art. vm :) pl. jalaAy^ilu . (S, K.)

definition: [ A little bell, consisting of a hollow ball of copper or brass or other metal, perforated, and containing a loose solid ball;
sourceDefinition: [ A little bell, consisting of a hollow ball of copper or brass or other metal, perforated, and containing a loose solid ball; ] a small jaras [or bell ]; (Msb, K;) a thing that is hung to the neck of a horse or similar beast, or to the leg of a hawk: (Mgh:) pl. jalaAjilu . (S, Mgh, Msb.) You say, fulaAnN yuEal~iqu Aljulojula fiY Eunuqihi [ Such a one hangs the little bell upon his neck; ] meaning, (tropical:) such a one imperils, or endangers, himself. (TA.) (TA.) ― -b2- See also julaAjilN .

HujazN (Msb, TA) and HujuzaAtN and HujazaAtN : (TA:) and hence HujozapN is applied to the garment called A_izaAr itself; as also ↓ HijozN ; of which latter the pl. is HujuzN , with two dammehs, [app. contracted into HujozN ,] and pl. pl. HujuwzN : Z says that ↓ HijozN and HujozN signify the same. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, $id~apN AlHujozapi (tropical:) Patience, (K, TA,) and hardiness. (TA.) One says, hawa $adydu AlHujozapi (tropical:) He is patient in difficulty. (TA.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Alee, when he was asked respecting the BenooUmeiyeh, humo A^a$ad~unaA HujazFA , or HajozapF , accord. to different relations, (tropical:) They are the most patient of us in difficulty. (TA.) ― -b3- You say also rajulN T~y~ibu AlHujozapi , (A, TA,) and kariymu AlHujozapi , and kariymu AlHujozi , [app. a contraction of AlHujuzi ,] (TA,) (tropical:) He is one who abstains from what is unlawful and indecorous [especially with respect to women ]; like Tay~ibu AlA_izaAri . (TA.) ― -b4- And huwa naAtiY'u AlHujozapi (tropical:) He is full in the flanks: the being so is a fault. (K, TA.) ― -b5- You also say, A^axa*a biHujozatihi ,, meaning (tropical:) He sought aid of him: (A, TA:) or he had recourse to him for refuge and protection. (TA.) And A^axa*a biHujozapi A@ll~`hi , i. e., bisababK minohu [meaning, (assumed tropical:) He laid hold of a means of obtaining access, or nearness, to God ]: said of Mohammad, in a trad. (TA.) And h`*aA kalaAmN A=xi*N baEoDuhu biHujazi baEoDK (tropical:) This is language disposed in regular order, consecutively. (A, TA.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a Alr~aHima A^axa*ato biHujozapi Alr~aHm`ni [ Verily Alr~aHimu is connected with Alr~aHom`n ]: said to mean, that the name of AlrHm is derived from AlrHmn ; so that it is as though it attached itself thereto, and laid hold of the middle thereof. (IAth, TA.)

definition: A thing intervening, as a separation, a partition, a fence, a barrier, or an obstacle, or obstruction, between two other things, (TA,) or between two things facing, or opposite to, each other;
sourceDefinition: A thing intervening, as a separation, a partition, a fence, a barrier, or an obstacle, or obstruction, between two other things, (TA,) or between two things facing, or opposite to, each other; (Az, A, TA;) as also ↓ HijaAzN . (Az, A, TA.) Hence the province called El-Hijáz is thus named, because it forms a separation between Nejd and the Ghowr, or Ghór; (S, Mgh, TA;) or between Nejd and the Saráh; (Msb, K;) or between the Ghowr, or Ghór, and Syria (Mgh, Msb, TA) and the Bádiyeh; (Mgh, TA;) or between Nejd and Tihámeh; (K;) or because the Hirár [or certain stony tracts] separate it from the high part of Nejd; (Az, TA;) or because it is encompassed by the Hirár and the mountains, (Mgh, Msb, *) or by the five Hirár, namely, the Harrah of Benoo-Suleym and that of Wákim and that of Leylà and that of Showrán and that of En-Nár. (As, K.) ― -b2- Also sing. of HajazapN , (K,) which latter signifies Wrongers, or wrongdoers, who prevent one from obtaining his right: (S:) or persons who defend men, one from another, and decide between them justly. (Az, TA.) In the K, the signification of “wrongers, or wrongdoers,” is combined with the contrary explanation given by Az. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of Keyleh, A^ayoEujizu A@bonu h`*ihi A^ano yanotaSifa mino waraA='i AlHajazapi [ Is the son of this woman unable to obtain his right in the absence of the wrongdoers who prevent his doing so? ]: (S:) or [according to one relation] A^ayulaAmu A@bonu *iho A^ano yafSila AlxuT~apa mino waraA='i AlHajazap [ Is the son of this woman to be blamed for deciding the affair in the absence of those who defend men, one from another, and decide between them justly? ]: by “the son of this woman” she means her own son: she says, if he suffer a wrong, and allege for himself that which repels from him the wrong, [without having recourse to the judge,] he is not to be blamed. (TA.) [See also xuT~apN .]

definition: [ A burning by means of fire;
sourceDefinition: [ A burning by means of fire;] a subst. (Mgh, Msb) from AlA_iHoraAqu , (Mgh,) [i. e.] from A_iHoraAqu Aln~aAri : (Msb:) or fire, (S, Msb, K,) itself; (Msb;) [the fire of a burning house &c.; ] as also ↓ HariyqN (Mgh) and ↓ HaAriqapN : (K:) or the flame of fire. (IAar, Th, Mgh, K.) The first is meant in the saying, DaAl~apu Almuw^omini Haraqu Aln~aAri [ The straybeast of the believer is a cause of the burning of fire ]: (Mgh:) or it here signifies the flame of fire: a trad., meaning that if any one takes the stray-beast of a believer to possess it, his doing so will bring him to the flame of the fire [of Hell]. (Az, Mgh, TA.) And hence, (Mgh,) AlHaraqu $ahaAdapN , (Mgh, TA,) i. e. [ Burning, or] fire, [or flame, is a cause of one's receiving the reward of martyrdom: ] occurring in another trad. (TA.) You say also fiY Haraqi A@ll~`hi In the fire of God. (S.) And ↓ A^aloqaY A@ll~`hu AlkaAfira fiY HaAriqatihi , i. e. [ May God cast the unbeliever ] into his fire. (TA.) ― -b2- A burn, (S,) or a mark of burning, (K,) in a garment, or piece of cloth, from the beating (S, K) of the washer, and whitener, and the like; (K;) and so, sometimes, ↓ HaroqN : (S:) or the former, a hole thus caused in a garment, or piece of cloth; (IAar, Mgh, TA;) and so, sometimes, ↓ the latter; which also signifies a hole caused by fire, in a garment, or piece of cloth. (Mgh.)

definition: -A2- AlHaAriqataAni The heads [ of the bones ] of the two thighs, in the two hips: or two sinews in the two hips: (S, K:) when these are severed, the man walks upon the extremities of his toes, and...
sourceDefinition: : see HaraqN , in two places. -A2- AlHaAriqataAni The heads [ of the bones ] of the two thighs, in the two hips: or two sinews in the two hips: (S, K:) when these are severed, the man walks upon the extremities of his toes, and cannot do otherwise: when one so walks by choice, you say that he is mukotaAmN , part. n. of AikotaAma : (IAar, TA:) the HArqp is also explained as being the sinew that connects the thigh and the hip: or the sinew that connects the head [ of the bone ] of the thigh and that [ of the bone ] of the upper arm, which turn in the Sadafap [or socket ] of the hip and of the shoulderblade: when it is severed, it never unites: or a sinew in the xurobap [or socket of the hip ], that suspends [ the bone of ] the thigh to the hip, and by means of which the man walks: it is said that when the HArqp is displaced, the man becomes lame. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, the sing., The side of the body. (AHeyth, TA.)

definition: -A2- Having his HaAriqap [q.
sourceDefinition: : see HariyqN . -A2- Having his HaAriqap [q. v.] severed; (S, TA;) as also ↓ HariqN ; which latter is [said to be] the more common: (TA:) [but this I doubt:] or, as some say, (S,) having his kip dislocated: (S, K:) [pl. of the latter, deviating from rule, ↓ Hur~aAqN , occurring in a verse below.] The ràjiz says, (S,) namely, Aboo-Mohammad El-Hadhlamee, (TA,) describing a pastor, (S,) yaZal~u taHota Alfanani Alwariyqi ya$uwlu biAlmiHojani kaAlmaHoruwqi [ He continues, or continues during the day, beneath the leafy branch, raising the crookedheaded stick, like the mHrwq ]: i. e. he stands upon one leg, stretching himself up towards the branches, and drawing them to him with the mHjn , and shaking off their leaves for the camels: (S, TA:) or he stands upon the extremities of his toes, [see HaAriqapN ,] in order to reach the branch and bend it to his camels. (ISd, TA. But see another meaning of the last word, below.) And another says, humu AlgirobaAnu fiY HurumaAti jaArK Alwuruwki ↓ wafiY AlA^adonayona Hur~aAqu [ They are like the crows in respect of the sacred rights of a neighbour; and in respect of inferiors, like those who are dislocated in the hips, or who have the sinews of the hip-joints severed ]: i. e., when a neighbour having a sacred right to respect alights among them, they are like the crow, which loaths not the gall on the back nor that which is unclean; and in wrongful treatment of their inferiors, like the mHrwq , who walks with an inclining of the body ( yamo$iY mutajaAnifFA ); and they abstain from aiding and defending them. (S, TA.) -A3- Accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, in the saying of the rájiz cited above, it means (TA) The iron instrument with which one roasts meat; syn. saf~uwd . (K, TA.)

definition: [an imperative verbal n.
sourceDefinition: [an imperative verbal n.] Be thou present. (A.) -A2- Also A certain star, (S, K,) upon the right hoof of Centaurus: upon his other fore leg is Alwazonu . (Kzw.) It is said, HaDaAri waAlwazonu muHolifaAni [ Hadári and El-Wezn are two causes of swearing ]: they are two stars that rise before Canopus (Suheyl); and when either of them rises, it is thought to be Canopus, because of their resemblance to it: (AA, S: *) they are termed mHlfAn because of the disagreement of their beholders when they rise; one swearing that the one rising is Canopus, and another swearing that it is not. (AA, TA.) Th says that it is a dim, distant, star; and cites this verse: A^aray naAra layolaY baAlEaqiyqi kaA^an~ahaA HaDaAri A_i*aA maA A^aEoraDato wafuruwduhaA I see the fire of Leylà, in El-'Akeek, dim in the distance, as though it were Hadári, when it appears, with its Furood, which are dim stars around Hadári. (TA.) -A3- HaDaArN : see what next follows.

definition: A man present: (A, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A man present: (A, K:) pl. [ HaADiruwna and] HuD~arN and [more commonly] HuDuwrN , (S, K,) which last is originally an inf. n. (S.) You say, faEalotuhu wafulaAnN HaADirN I did it such a one being present. (A.) And hawa mino HaADiriY Almaliki [ He is of those who are in the presence of the king ]. (A.) ― -b2- So, too, applied to a time: and you say, AlS~alaApu HaADirapN , for waqotuhaA HaADirN , (tropical:) The time of prayer is come. (Msb.) ― -b3- [Also (assumed tropical:) Ready, or prepared: often used in this sense in the lexicons &c., as in modern Arabic. See 4.] You say, quwluwA maA huwa HaADirN Einodakumo (assumed tropical:) Say ye what is ready with you [or in your minds ]. (TA.) And huwa HaADirN biAljawaAbi (tropical:) [ He is ready with the answer, or reply ]; and biAln~awaAdiri (tropical:) [ with rare words or expressions ]; (A;) as also ↓ HaDurN : (TA:) which latter word, alone, signifies a man having the quality of perspicuity of speech, and intelligence; syn. *uw AlbayaAni waAlfiqohi . (K.) ― -b4- A visiting angel: and ↓ HaADirapN is applied to a class or company [ of visiting angels ]. (TA.) ― -b5- One coming to a region, district, or tract, of cities, towns, or villages, and of cultivated land; contr. of baAdK ; (S, K;) as also ↓ muHotaDirN . (S.) ― -b6- A man staying, residing, dwelling, or abiding, bamawoDiEK in a place. (S.) ― -b7- [A man, or people,] staying, or dwelling, by water; (S, * TA;) contr. of baAdK : (K:) pl. HuDuwrN (TA) and HuD~aArN and HaDarapN : (S:) one says, maA EalaY AlmaA='i HaADirN [ There is not any one staying, or dwelling, by the water ]: and h`w^ulaA='i qawomN HuD~aArN and maHaADiru [which is pl. of ↓ maHoDarN , a syn. of xaADirN in this sense; i. e. These are a people staying, or dwelling, by water ]: (S:) or HaADirN signifies any people that have alighted and taken up their abode by a constant source of water, and do not remove from it in winter nor in summer, whether they have alighted and taken up their abode in towns or villages, and cultivated land, and houses of clay, or pitched their tents by the water, and remained there, and sustained their beasts with the water and herbage around them: (TA:) or HaY~N HaADirN , without p , signifies a tribe that has alighted and is abiding by a constant source of water: (T, TA:) and ↓ HaADirapN and HaADiruwna , a people staying, or dwelling, by waters; alighting there in the hottest time of summer: when the weather becomes cool, they migrate from the constant sources of water, and go into the desert, seeking the vicinity of herbage; and then they are termed baAdiyapN and baAduwna . definition: A place where people are present, or assembled.

(Kull p. 352.) This is thought by MF to be a recent conventional term; but it has been heard from the Arabs [of the classical times], and is mentioned by ISd and others. (MF, TA.) -A4- fulaAnN Hasanu AlmaHoDari (assumed tropical:) Such a one is a person who speaks well of the absent. (S.)

HamoHamapN ,] He (a horse) uttered his cry, [or neighed, ] when desiring fodder; as also ↓ taHamoHama : (S:) accord. to Az, HamoHamapN is app. a word imitative of the cry of the horse when he desires fodder; or when he sees his master to whom he has been accustomed, and behaves familiarly towards him: (TA:) or it signifies a horse's uttering a cry with a kind of yearning sound, in order that his master may feel tenderness for him; as also ↓ taHamoHumN : (EM p. 250:) or, of a biro*awon [or hack, or the like,] the uttering of a cry [or neighing ] such as is not loud; and of a horse [of good breed], the uttering of a cry not so loud as the Sahiyl [or usual neighing ]: (Lth, TA:) or, of the br*wn , the uttering of a cry when desiring the barley: (K, * TA:) and the Eir~ , or Eiz~ , [accord. to different copies of the K, but each is app. a mistranscription, for EiY~ as meaning faltering of the voice or cry. ] of the horse, when falling, or stopping, short in neighing, and seeking self-help [ to finish it ]; as also ↓ taHamoHumN : (K:) and the bull's uttering a cry with the desire of leaping the cow. (Az, K.)

definition: [The pigeon, both wild and domestic, but more properly the former;
sourceDefinition: [The pigeon, both wild and domestic, but more properly the former; and sometimes not strictly confined to denote the pigeon-kind:] a certain wild bird, that does not keep to the houses; well-known: (ISd, K:) or any collared, or ringed, bird; (S, Msb, K;) so with the Arabs; such as the fawaAxit and the qamaAriY~ and saAqu Hur~ and the qaTaA and the waraA$iyn and the like, (S, Msb,) and the domestic [ pigeons ] ( Ald~awaAjin ), also, (El-Umawee, S, Msb,) that are taken into houses for the purpose of producing their young ones; (El-Umawee, S;) to which last alone the term is applied by the vulgar: accord. to Ks, it is the wild [ species ]; and the yamaAm is that which keeps to the houses: accord. to As, the latter is the HamaAm waHo$iY~ [or wild pigeon ]; a species of the birds of the desert: (S, Msb:) or, accord. to Esh-Sháfi'ee, HamaAmN signifies any kind of bird that drinks in the manner denoted by the verb Eab~a , [i. e. continuously, ] and cooes; including the qamaAriY~ and waraA$iyn and fawaAxit ; whether it be, or be not, collared, or ringed; domestic or wild: (Az, TA:) the flesh thereof strengthens the venereal faculty, and increases the seminal fluid and the blood; the putting it, cut open while alive, upon the place stung by a scorpion, is a proved cure; and the blood stops bleeding from the nose: (K:) the n. un. is with p ; (S, Msb;) which is applied to the male and the female: (S Msb, K:) and in like manner, HamaAmN , because the p is added to restrict to unity, not to make fem.: (S:) but to distinguish the masc., you may say, raA^ayotu HamaAmFA EalaY HamaAmapK , i. e. I saw a male [ pigeon ] upon a female [ pigeon ]: (Zj, Msb:) accord. to ISd and the K, however, HamaAmN should not be applied to the [single] male: (TA:) in a verse of Homeyd Ibn-Thowr, cited voce Hur~N , by the n. un. is meant a qumoriy~ap : the pl. of HmAmp is HamaAmN , (S,) [or rather this is the coll. gen. n.,] and HamaAy^imu (S, K) and HamaAmaAtN : (S:) and sometimes HamaAmN is used as a sing.: [so in an ex. above: and] Jirán-el-'Owd says, wa*ak~araniY AlS~ibaA baEoda Alt~anaAy^iY HamaAmapu A^ayokapK tadoEuw HamaAmaA [ And a female pigeon of a thicket, calling a male pigeon, reminded me of youth, after estrangement ]: a poet also says, HamaAmaA qaqorapK waqaEaA faTaAraA [ Two pigeons of a desert tract alighted and flew away ]: and El-Umawee cites, as an ex. of HamaAm applied to the domestic [pigeons], qawaATinFA mak~apa mino wuroqi AlHamaY [ Inhabiting Mekkeh, of the pigeons of a white colour inclining to black ]; by AlHmY [or rather it should be written AlHamaA ] meaning AlHamaAm . (S.)

definition: The fever ( Hum~aY ) of camels;
sourceDefinition: The fever ( Hum~aY ) of camels; (S;) as also ↓ Hum~aA='u : (TA:) or of all beasts, (K, TA,) including camels: (TA:) accord. to ISh, when camels eat date-stones, [which are often given to them as food,] they are [sometimes] affected with HumaAm and qumaAH ; the former of which is a heat affecting the skin, until the body is smeared with mud, or clay, in consequence of which they forsake the abundant herbage, and their fat goes away; and it continues in them a month, and then passes away. definition: The qayoZ [or summer: or the most vehement heat of summer, from the auroral rising of the Pleiades ( at the epoch of the Flight about the 13th of May O.
sourceDefinition: The qayoZ [or summer: or the most vehement heat of summer, from the auroral rising of the Pleiades ( at the epoch of the Flight about the 13th of May O. S. ) to the auroral rising of Canopus ( at the same period about the 4th of August O. S. ): or vehemence of heat ]: (S, K:) or a period of about twenty nights, commencing at the [ auroral ] rising of Ald~abaraAn [ at the epoch of the Flight about the 26th of May O. S. ]. (AZ, T voce nawo'N .) ― -b2- Live coals with which one fumigates. (IAar, Sh.) ― -b3- Hot water; (T, S, ISd, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ HamiymapN : (S, ISd, K:) or so maA='N HamiymN : (Msb:) pl. HamaAy^imu ; (K;) i. e. pl. of HamiymN , accord. to IAar; but accord. to ISd, of HamiymapN . (TA.) ― -b4- And Cold water: (K:) or cold, applied to water: so, accord. to IAar, in the saying of a poet, wasaAga liYa Al$~araAbu wakunotu qidomFA A^akaAdu A^agaS~u biAlmaA='i AlHamiymi [ And wine has become easy to swallow to me, whereas I used, in old time, nearly to be choked with cold water ]: (Az, TA:) thus bearing two contr. significations. (Az, K.) ― -b5- The rain that comes in the time of vehement heat; (S;) or after the heat has become vehement, (M, K,) because it is hot; (M;) or in the Sayof [or summer ], when the ground is hot. (TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) Sweat; (Az, S, A, K;) as also ↓ Him~apN : (Az, A, K:) and ↓ HumaAmN is said to signify the sweat of horses. (Ham p. 92.) One says, (to a person who has been in the bath, A, TA,) TaAba Hamiymuka and ↓ TaAbato Him~atuka , meaning May thy sweat be good, or pleasant; (Az, A, K;) and consequently, may God make thy body sound, or healthy: (A, TA:) or the former may mean as above, or may thy bathing be good, or pleasant: (IB:) one should not say, ↓ TaAba Ham~aAmuka , (K, TA,) though MF defends it. (TA.) -A2- A relation, (Lth, S, K,) for whose case one is anxious or solicitous, (S,) or whom one loves and by whom one is beloved: (Lth, K:) or an affectionate, or a compassionate, relation, who is sharp, or hasty, to protect his kinsfolk: or an object of love; a person beloved: (TA:) or a man's brother; his friend, or true friend; because anxious, or solicitous, for him: (Ham p. 90:) and ↓ muHim~N signifies the same: the pl. [of Hmym ] is A^aHim~aA='u : and sometimes HamiymN is used as a pl., and as fem.; (K;) as well as sing. and masc. (TA.) ― -b2- AlHamiymu biAlHaAjapi He who devotes himself to obtain the object of want; who is solicitous for it. (TA.) A poet says, walaA yudoriku AlHaAjaAti A_il~aA HamiymuhaA [ And none will attain the objects of want but he who devotes himself to obtain them; who is solicitous for them ]. (IAar, TA.)

sourceDefinition: and *awaAtu HaAmiyma , (K,) or ↓ A=lu H`m= and *awaAtu H`m= , (S,) A=l being prefixed in this case in like manner as in A=lu fulaAnK , (Fr, S,) Certain chapters of the Kur-án (S, K) commencing with HAmym [or H`m= ], (K,) [namely, the fortieth and six following chapters, ] called by Ibn-Mes'ood diybaAju AlquroA=ni : (S:) one should not say HawaAmiym : (K:) this is vulgar: (S:) but it occurs in poetry. (Az, TA.) It is imperfectly decl. because determinate and of the fem. gender; or because it is of a foreign measure, like qaAbiylu and haAbiylu , (Ksh, Bd,) and determinate. (Ksh.)

definition: , originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: , originally an inf. n., (Msb,) Dates mixed with clarified butter and [ the preparation of dried curd called ] A^aqiT , (S, A, Mgh, K,) and kneaded (A, K) vehemently, (A,) or rubbed and pressed with the hand until they mingle together, (Mgh,) whereupon their stones come forth; (K;) and sometimes sawiyq [or meal of parched barley or wheat ] is put into it; (A, K;) and a little crumbled bread instead of the AqT : (TA:) or dates, of the kind called baroniY~ , and AqT , bruised together, and kneaded vehemently with clarified butter until the stones come forth from it one by one, and then made like variyd : it is the same as waTobapN , except that Hys sometimes has swyq put in it, but wTbp has not: (L:) or dates of which the stones have been taken out, bruised with AqT , and then kneaded, and rubbed and pressed with the hand until the whole becomes like vryd ; and sometimes swyq is put with it: (Msb:) accord. to Ibn-Waddáh El-Andalusee, dates of which the stones have been taken out, mixed with swyq ; but this is not known, (MF, TA,) because of the deficiency of the ingredients: (TA:) Hr is related to have described it as a variydap composed of A^axolaAT [or various mixtures ]. (TA.) A rájiz says, Aalt~amoru waAls~amonu maEFAv~m~a AlA^aqiTo AaloHayosu A_il~aA A^an~ahu lamo yaxotaliTo [ Dates and clarified butter together, then AqT , are Hys , except that it is not yet mixed ]: (S, MF, TA:) from which it might be understood, that these components, when mixed, are not Hys : but this is the contrary of what is meant: (MF:) the meaning seems to be, that these three things, when brought, are virtually Hys , as being the materials thereof, though not mixed. (TA.)

definition: She (a girl) kept herself behind, or within, the curtain;
sourceDefinition: She (a girl) kept herself behind, or within, the curtain; (Es-Sarakustee, Msb;) as also ↓ txd~rt , (A, TA,) and ↓ Axtdrt , and fiY xidorihaA ↓ xadarato . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] ↓ txd~r [in the CK ↓ xd~r (app. a mistranscription)] and ↓ Axtdr (assumed tropical:) He concealed, or hid, himself; (K, TA;) as also ↓ xadira , like fariHa [in measure]: (TA:) whence the saying, AlqaArapu biAls~araAbi ↓ Aixotadarati , i. e. [ The small isolated mountain, or the like, ] became concealed by the mirage. (TA.) [Hence also,] Axdr (tropical:) He (a lion) kept himself in his lurking-place; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ xadira and ↓ xadara , (TA,) or xadara fiY Eariynihi . (A, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) It (a bird) remained in its nest. (S.) And (assumed tropical:) He (a man) remained, stayed, or abode; (S, K;) bimakaAnK in a place; as also ↓ xadara , inf. n. xadorN ; (K;) and fiY A^aholihi among his family. (S.) And ↓ xadara , (S,) inf. n. xadorN (K,) (assumed tropical:) He (a gazelle) remained behind the herd; not going with it: (S, K:) and he (a beast) remained behind; not overtaking, or coming up with, the others. (TA.) And AxdrwA (assumed tropical:) They entered upon night [ and so became concealed from view ]. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) They entered upon a day of rain, and of clouds or mist, and of wind: (K:) or rain came upon them. (S.) -A2- Axdr as a trans. v.: see 2, in four places.

sourceDefinition: The extreme, or most remote, [meaning innermost, ] part of the nose: (S, Msb:) or the interior of the nose: (MA:) or the upper part of the interior of the nose: and the bone of the nose: (KL:) or the part that is above the nuxorap [which here seems to mean the end, or tip, or flexible part, ] of the nose, of the bone thereof: and what is beneath this [is] of [the thin cartilages called] the xa$aArim of the head: (M, K:) and the nose [altogether] (Msb, KL) is so called by some: (Msb:) the word is of the measure fayoEuwlN : (Msb, TA:) and its pl. is xayaA$iym : (Msb:) which [also] signifies certain cartilages in the extreme [or inmost ] part of the nose, between it and the brain: or certain ducts, ( Euruwq , [meaning, or including, the air-passages, see ju$~apN , and naxara , &c.,]) in the interior ( baATin M, or baTon K) of the nose. (M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] the pl. signifies also (tropical:) Prominences, or projecting parts, of mountains. (JK, S, TA.) ― -b3- And the sing., [as a coll. gen. n.,] Small, thin, black things, resembling flesh; and morbose nodes; upon a bone. (TA.)

definition: A plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, state of life.
sourceDefinition: A plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, state of life. (K, TA. definition: , inf. n. muxaAlaTapN (S, Mgh, K) and xilaATN , (S, K,) It mixed, mingled, commingled, intermixed, or intermingled, with it; it became incorporated, or blended, with it; syn. maAzajahu ; (Mgh, K;)...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. muxaAlaTapN (S, Mgh, K) and xilaATN , (S, K,) It mixed, mingled, commingled, intermixed, or intermingled, with it; it became incorporated, or blended, with it; syn. maAzajahu ; (Mgh, K;) and xaAmarahu ; (S, A, K, all in art. xmr ;) [as, for instance,] water with milk. (A in art. xmr , and Mgh in the present art.) xilaATN in relation to camels, and men, and beasts, also signifies Their being mixed together. (K.) A poet says, yaxorujona mino buEokuwkapi AlxilaATi [ They come forth from the crowding and dust (of the beasts) occasioned by the being mixed together ]. (Th, TA.) And it is said in a trad., laA xilaATa walaA wiraATa (S, Mgh,) There shall be no putting together what is separate, nor separating what is put together, from fear of the poor-rate: (S:) for the Prophet made it incumbent on a person having possessed forty sheep or goats a whole year to give one sheep or goat; and so on one having possessed more thereof to the number of a hundred and twenty, to give one sheep or goat; but if they exceeded a hundred and twenty by one, two sheep or goats were to be given of them: (Az, TA:) i. e. there shall be no putting together what is separate; as, for instance, when three persons possess a hundred and twenty sheep or goats, every one of them having forty, they not having been partners for a whole year, and it being incumbent on every one of them to give a sheep or goat; and when the collector of the poorrate comes to them, they put them together, assigning them to one pastor, in order that they may not be obliged to give for them more than one sheep or goat: (K, * TA:) accord. to IAth, this is termed A_ixolaATN [app. a mistake for xilaATN ]: nor shall there be any separating of what is put together; i. e., when there are two partners, each of them having a hundred and one sheep or goats, for which together they are bound to give three sheep or goats; and when the collector of the poorrate comes to them, they separate their sheep or goats, so that each of them shall not have to give more than one sheep or goat: [see also art. wrT :] (TA:) or xlAT signifies a man's mixing his sheep or goats when they are eighty in number with those of another which are forty in number, both together being bound to give two sheep or goats while they are separate, in order that one [ only ] may be taken: and wrAT , a man's giving to another the half of his sheep or goats when they are forty in number, in order that the collector of the poor-rate may not take anything: (Mgh:) or xlAT is, when there are, between two partners, a hundred and twenty sheep or goats, one of them having eighty and the other forty, and the collector of the poor-rate has taken two of these sheep or goats, the former partner's restoring to the latter the third of a sheep or goat; so that the former has had to give a sheep or goat and a third; and the latter, two thirds of one: and if the collector have taken, from the hundred and twenty, one sheep or goat, the former partner's restoring to the latter one third [in some copies of the K, erroneously, two thirds] of a sheep or goat; so that the former has had to give two thirds of a sheep or goat; and the latter, one third of one: (ISd, K, * TA:) and wrAT is deceiving, and acting dishonestly: (ISd, L, TA:) in the place of wrAT , we find, accord. to one relation, $inaAq , followed by fiY AlS~adaqapi . (TA.) ― -b2- El- 'Ajjáj contended with Homeyd El-Arkat in two poems of the metre termed rajaz ending with T , and Homeyd said, AlxilaATa yaA A^abaA Al$~aEovaA='i , i. e. [ Beware thou of mixing; or] do not thou mix my A^urojuwzap with thine [ O father of her with the shaggy hair ]; to which El-'Ajjáj replied, AlfijaAju A^awosaEu mino *`lika yaA A@bona A^axiY [ The roads are wider than to require my doing that, O son of my brother ]. (AO, S.) ― -b3- xAlT Al*~iy^obu Alganama [lit. signifying The wolf mixed with the sheep, or goats, ] means (tropical:) the wolf fell upon the sheep, or goats: (K, TA:) the inf. n. is xilaATN . (TA.) ― -b4- xAlThA , (Az, Msb, K,) inf. n. xilaATN and muxaAlaTapN , (Az, Msb,) (tropical:) He had carnal intercourse with her; (Az, Mgh, * Msb, K;) i. e., a man with his wife, (Az, Msb,) or with a woman: (K:) the lawyers say, xAlThA muxaAlaTapa AlAizodiwaAji : (Msb:) Th explains the inf. n. xilaATN by rafavN , q. v. (TA.) Also, in like manner, with the same inf. ns., (tropical:) a stallion-camel with the female. (Lth, K, TA.) [See also 4.] IAar explains xilaATN in relation to camels as signifying (assumed tropical:) A man's coming to the nightly resting-place of another's camels, and taking thence a male camel, and making him to cover his she-camel without his owner's knowledge. (TA.) ― -b5- xAlThu Als~ahomu (assumed tropical:) [ The arrow penetrated into him ]. (TA.) ― -b6- xAlThu Al$~ayobu [ Hoariness, or whiteness, became intermixed in his hair ]. (S and K in art. wxT ; &c.) ― -b7- xAlThu Ald~aA='u (tropical:) The disease infected, or pervaded, him; [ as though commingling with him; ] syn. xaAmarahu : (Sh, K:) or infected, or pervaded, his inside. (Lth, S.) ― -b8- xaAlaTa qalobahu ham~N EaZiymN (tropical:) [ Great anxiety, or disquietude of mind, infected, or pervaded, his heart ]. (TA.) It is said in a trad., warajaEa Al$~ayoTaAnu yalotamisu AlxilaATa (tropical:) And the devil returned seeking to infect ( yuxaAliT ) the heart of the man praying by suggesting what was vain. (TA.) ― -b9- Alxamoru tuxaAliTu AlEaqola (tropical:) [ Wine infects the intellect ]. (S and K in art. xmr .) And xuwliTa fiY Eaqolihi , inf. n. xilaATN , (tropical:) [ He became infected, corrupted, disordered, or confused, in his intellect. ] (S, K.) And xuwliTa Eaqoluhu , and Eaqoluhu ↓ AixotalaTa , (tropical:) His intellect became corrupted, or disordered; (TA; [in which only the latter phrase is thus explained, though both are mentioned;]) and so ↓ AixotalaTa alone: (S, K:) and nafosuhu ↓ AixotalaTato (assumed tropical:) [ His soul, or stomach, became disordered ]: (S and K in art. xvr :) and ↓ A^axolaTa , said of a man, signifies the same as AxtlT . (TA.) ― -b10- xAlT Alqawoma (assumed tropical:) He mixed with the people, or company of men, in familiar, or social, inter- course; conversed with them; or became intimate with them; or mixed with them in, or entered with them into, their affairs; syn. daAxalahumo ; as also ↓ xalaTahumo , inf. n. xaloTN ; (TA;) and ↓ xaliTa , like fariHa , is used in a similar manner, in the sense of xaAlaTa : (IAar, TA:) and you say also ↓ AxtlT biAln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) [ he mixed, or associated, or conversed, with men ]. (TA.) And xaAlaTotu fulaAnFA (assumed tropical:) I mixed with such a one in familiar, or social, intercourse; conversed with him; or became intimate with him; syn. xaAmarotuhu , (A in art. xmr ,) and EaA$arotuhu . (S, Msb, K, all in art. E$r .) And xAlThu fiY A^amori (assumed tropical:) [ He mixed, or joined, with him in an affair ]. (Mgh.) And hence xAlThu signifies (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, copartner with him; he shared with him. (Mgh.) xaAlaTahumo also signifies xaAlafahumo [evidently a mistranscription, for HaAlafahumo (assumed tropical:) He entered into a confederacy, league, compact, or covenant, with them ]. (TA.) And you say also xAlT AlA^umuwra (assumed tropical:) [ He mixed in, engaged in, or entered into, affairs ]. (S, K.)

rawSourceText: , inf. n. muxaAlaTapN (S, Mgh, K) and xilaATN , (S, K,) It mixed, mingled, commingled, intermixed, or intermingled, with it; it became incorporated, or blended, with it; syn. maAzajahu ; (Mgh, K;) and xaAmarahu ; (S, A, K, all in art. xmr ;) [as, for instance,] water with milk. (A in art. xmr , and Mgh in the present art.) xilaATN in relation to camels, and men, and beasts, also signifies Their being mixed together. (K.) A poet says, yaxorujona mino buEokuwkapi AlxilaATi [ They come forth from the crowding and dust (of the beasts) occasioned by the being mixed together ]. (Th, TA.) And it is said in a trad., laA xilaATa walaA wiraATa (S, Mgh,) There shall be no putting together what is separate, nor separating what is put together, from fear of the poor-rate: (S:) for the Prophet made it incumbent on a person having possessed forty sheep or goats a whole year to give one sheep or goat; and so on one having possessed more thereof to the number of a hundred and twenty, to give one sheep or goat; but if they exceeded a hundred and twenty by one, two sheep or goats were to be given of them: (Az, TA:) i. e. there shall be no putting together what is separate; as, for instance, when three persons possess a hundred and twenty sheep or goats, every one of them having forty, they not having been partners for a whole year, and it being incumbent on every one of them to give a sheep or goat; and when the collector of the poorrate comes to them, they put them together, assigning them to one pastor, in order that they may not be obliged to give for them more than one sheep or goat: (K, * TA:) accord. to IAth, this is termed A_ixolaATN [app. a mistake for xilaATN ]: nor shall there be any separating of what is put together; i. e., when there are two partners, each of them having a hundred and one sheep or goats, for which together they are bound to give three sheep or goats; and when the collector of the poorrate comes to them, they separate their sheep or goats, so that each of them shall not have to give more than one sheep or goat: [see also art. wrT :] (TA:) or xlAT signifies a man's mixing his sheep or goats when they are eighty in number with those of another which are forty in number, both together being bound to give two sheep or goats while they are separate, in order that one [ only ] may be taken: and wrAT , a man's giving to another the half of his sheep or goats when they are forty in number, in order that the collector of the poor-rate may not take anything: (Mgh:) or xlAT is, when there are, between two partners, a hundred and twenty sheep or goats, one of them having eighty and the other forty, and the collector of the poor-rate has taken two of these sheep or goats, the former partner's restoring to the latter the third of a sheep or goat; so that the former has had to give a sheep or goat and a third; and the latter, two thirds of one: and if the collector have taken, from the hundred and twenty, one sheep or goat, the former partner's restoring to the latter one third [in some copies of the K, erroneously, two thirds] of a sheep or goat; so that the former has had to give two thirds of a sheep or goat; and the latter, one third of one: (ISd, K, * TA:) and wrAT is deceiving, and acting dishonestly: (ISd, L, TA:) in the place of wrAT , we find, accord. to one relation, $inaAq , followed by fiY AlS~adaqapi . (TA.) ― -b2- El- 'Ajjáj contended with Homeyd El-Arkat in two poems of the metre termed rajaz ending with T , and Homeyd said, AlxilaATa yaA A^abaA Al$~aEovaA='i , i. e.
