sourceDefinition: [ Mixed; mingled; incorporated, or blended: of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; like qatiylN &c. And hence,] (K,) or EalafN xaliyTN , (S, TA,) [ The kind of trefoil called ] qat~ and cut straw (S, TA) mixed together: (TA:) or clay mixed with cut straw: (K, TA:) or with qat~ . (K.) Also, (K,) or labanN xaliyTN , (TA,) Sweet milk mixed with sour or such as bites the tongue. (K, TA.) Also, (K,) or samonN xaliyTN , (TA,) Clarified butter in which are fat and flesh-meat. (K, TA.) [Hence also,] it is said in a trad. respecting [the beverage called] nabiy* , (TA,) nuhiYa Eani AlxaliyTayoni (S, K) fiY AlA^anobi*api (S) or A^ano yunoba*aA (K) [ Two sorts of things mixed together are forbidden in the beverages of the kind called nby* , or that nby* should be made of them ]; i. e. it is forbidden to mix together [for making nby* ] two sorts of things; (S, TA;) meaning dried dates and raisins; (S, Mgh, K;) or fresh grapes and fresh ripe dates; (S;) or dried dates and full-grown unripe dates, (T, Mgh, K,) thoroughly cooked by fire; (Mgh;) or fresh grapes and raisins; (T, K;) and the like; because such nby* quickly alters, and becomes intoxicating: (K:) and some hold that nby* so made is forbidden even if it do not intoxicate. (TA.) ― -b2- See also A^axolaATN mina Aln~aAsi , voce xiloTN . ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) One who mixes much with men: (Msb, TA:) [see also mixolaATN :] (assumed tropical:) one who mixes with others in familiar, or social, intercourse; or becomes intimate with them; or mixes with them in, or enters with them into, their affairs; syn. with ↓ muxaAliTN ; (S, K;) like as nadiymN is syn. with munaAdimN , and jaliysN with mujaAlisN : (S:) pl. xulaTaA='u (S, Msb, K) and xuluTN : (S, K:) it sometimes has these pls., but is itself both sing. and pl.: (S, TA:) and as a pl. signifies (assumed tropical:) a people, or company of men, whose affair, or case, or state, is one: (K, TA:) it occurs frequently in the poems of the Arabs because they used to assemble in the days of the fresh herbage, sundry tribes of them congregating in one place, and familiar intercourse took place between them, and when they separated and returned to their homes, it grieved them: (S, TA:) or, accord. to some, it relates only to partnership: (TA:) it signifies (assumed tropical:) a partner, copartner, or sharer; (Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) as, for instance, in merchandise, and sheep or goats: (Mgh:) or (assumed tropical:) one who has mixed his property with that of his copartner: (Bd in xxxviii. 23:) or (assumed tropical:) one who shares in merchandise, or in a debt, or in commerce, or in neighbourship: (Ibn- 'Arafeh, TA:) and (assumed tropical:) a sharer in the rights of possession, or property; such as water, and a road: (K:) the pl. is xulaTaA='u ; (Mgh, TA;) occurring in the Kur xxxviii. 23: (TA:) and the sing. also signifies (assumed tropical:) a neighbour; syn. jaArN [which has also other significations here assigned to xaliyTN ]; (TA;) and mujaAwirN : (Msb:) and (assumed tropical:) a husband: and (assumed tropical:) the son of a paternal uncle: (K:) and [the pl.] xuluTN is also explained by IAar as (assumed tropical:) i. q. mawaAlK [pl. of mawolFY , which has several of the significations here assigned to xaliyTN ]: and as signifying also (assumed tropical:) neighbours of sincere friendly conduct. (TA.) It is said in a trad. (K, TA) respecting [the right termed] Al$~ufoEap , (TA,) Al$~ariyku A^awolaY mina AlxaliyTu A^awolaY mina AljaAri (assumed tropical:) The sharer in what is not divided is more deserving than the sharer in the rights of possession, or property; [ and the sharer in the rights of possession, or property, is more deserving than the neighbour: ] (K, TA:) [or the trad. is as follows:] AlxaliyTu mina Al$~ariyki waAl$~ariyku A^aHaq~u mina AljaAri A^aHaq~u mino gayorihi (assumed tropical:) the sharer in the thing itself that is sold has more right than the sharer in the rights thereof; and the sharer in the rights thereof has more right than the adjoining neighbour; and the adjoining neighbour has more right than another: or the meaning here is, he between whom and thyself are acts of receiving and giving, and affairs of debt and credit; not the sharer, or partner. (Mgh.) And in another trad., maA kaAna mino xaliyTayoni faA_A_in~ahumaA yataraAjaEaAni bayonahumaA biAls~awiy~api (assumed tropical:) Whatever two copartners there be that have not divided the beasts [ belonging to them ], they shall make claim for restitution, one of the other, with equality; i. e., if they be copartners in camels for which it is incumbent to give sheep or goats, and the camels be found in the possession of one of them, and the poor-rate for them be taken from him, he shall make a claim for restitution [ of what he has given above his own share ] upon his copartner, with equality: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, K, TA:) the two persons are not xaliyTaAni unless they be such as drive back their beasts to the nightly resting-place, and drive them forth in the morning to the pasturage, and water them, together, and have their stallions mixed together, and have been copartners for a year; and if so, they give the poor-rate as one: otherwise, they are not xlyTAn ; and they give the poor-rate as two: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, TA:) the trad. applies, for instance, to the case of two copartners who have mixed their property together; one of them having forty bulls or cows or of both kinds; and the other, thirty; and the collector of the poor-rates takes from the forty a musin~ap [q. v.], and from the thirty a tabiyE [q. v.]; then the giver of the msn~p makes a claim for restitution of three sevenths thereof upon his copartner; and the giver of the tbyE , of four sevenths thereof upon his copartner; for it is incumbent to give the beasts of these two ages [the msn~p and the tbyE ] when the property is not divided, as though it were the property of one: and the saying bAls~wyp shows that if the collector of the poor-rate wrong one of them, and take from him more than the law imposes upon him, he cannot make a claim for restitution thereof upon his copartner, who is only responsible to him for the value of what falls upon him in particular, of what is incumbent by the law: and the making claim for [just] restitution, by one upon the other, shows that the partnership holds good notwithstanding the distinction of the things which compose the possessions, with such as hold this to be the case. (IAth, TA.)

definition: A maternal uncle;
sourceDefinition: A maternal uncle; one's mother's brother: (JK, S, K:) pl. A^axowaAlN (S, Msb, K) and A^axowilapN , (K,) [both pls. of pauc.,] the latter anomalous, (TA,) and (of mult., TA) xuw~alN and xuw^uwlN (K) and xuw^uwlapN : (Msb, K:) the fem. is xaAla , (JK, S, K,) a maternal aunt; one's mother's sister: (JK, S:) and the pl. of this is xaAlaAtN . (Msb.) One says, humaAA@bonaA xaAlapK [meaning Each of them two is a son of a maternal aunt of the other ]; but one cannot say, A@bonaA Eam~apK : (K:) and in like manner one says, A@bonaA Eam~F ; but one cannot say, A@bonaA xaAlK . (TA.) -A2- An owner of a horse: you say, A^anaA xaAlu h`*aA Alfarasi I am the owner of this horse. (K.) [See also xaAlN in art. xyl .] ― -b2- huwa xaAlu maAlK and maAlK ↓ xaAy^ilu He is a manager, or tender, of cattle, or camels &c.; (K;) or a good manager or tender thereof; (S, K; *) and so maAlK ↓ xawoliY~u : (S:) ↓ xaAy^ilN signifies also a keeper, or guardian, of a thing; (T, S;) or a pastor; (Fr, TA;) a people's pastor, who milks and waters and pastures for them; and one who pays frequent attention to a thing, puts it into a good or right state, or restores it to such a state, and undertakes the management of it: (T, TA:) xuw~alN [is a pl. of xaAy^ilN , like as nuw~amN is of naAy^imN , &c., and] signifies pastors who take care of cattle, or camels &c.: (TA:) and ↓ xawoliY~N , (K,) or, accord. to the M, ↓ xawaliY~N , (TA,) signifies a pastor who is a good manager of cattle, or camels, and sheep or goats; (M, K, * TA;) or a good manager and orderer of the affairs of men; (TA;) and its pl. [or quasi-pl. n. or n. un.] is ↓ xawalN ; (M, K;) accord. to the M, like as EarabN is of EarabiY~N . (TA.) [See also xaAlN in art. xyl .] -A3- An indication, or a symptom, sign, mark, or token, of good (S, * K, TA) in a person. (S, TA.) See 4. -A4- A mole; i. e. [ a thing resembling ] a pimple in the face, inclining to blackness: dim. ↓ xuwayolN and xuyayolN : and pl. xiylaAnN . (JK. [See also art. xyl .]) -A5- The [ kind of banner called ] liwaA=' , of an army or a military force. (S, K. [See also art. xyl .]) ― -b2- A kind of soft garment, or cloth, of the fabric of El-Yemen: (JK:) a kind of burod , (S, K,) well known, (K,) having a red [or brown ] ground, with black lines or stripes. (TA. [Mentioned also in art. xyl .]) -A6- A black stallion-camel. (IAar, K. [See also art. xyl .])

definition: Badness, corruptness, or unsoundness;
sourceDefinition: Badness, corruptness, or unsoundness; or a bad, a corrupt, or an unsound, state or quality; (S, and Mgh in art. ngl ;) [in an affair, &c.;] like daxalN ; (S;) and a thing that induces doubt, or suspicion, or evil opinion; [in an affair; or] in a man: (Mgh ubi suprà:) or a cause of badness, corruption, or unsoundness, in an affair. (JK, T, K, TA.) Hence the saying of El-Hasan, Ait~axuwA kitaAba A@ll~`hi dagalFA [ They made the Book of God to be a cause of corruption: or perhaps they made the Book of God corrupt; i. e. they corrupted it ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Confusedness, or entanglement, and abundance, of plants or herbage; (M, K;) most commonly known in plants of the kind termed HamoD , when amid gryl [i. e. giroyal , app. here meaning silt, or alluvial deposit, left upon the ground by a torrent]. (M, TA.) ― -b3- Tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, trees; (S, K;) as also daxalN . (TA.) ― -b4- Any place in which a wile, machination, or plot, is practised; (JK;) a place in which one fears being taken unawares: (K:) and ↓ dagiylapN signifies the same as dagalN [app. meaning such a place as is here described]: (JK, K:) the pl. of the former is A^adogaAlN [a pl. of pauc.] and digaAlN . (K.) ― -b5- Accord. to En-Nadr, An elevated [ tract of ground such as is termed ] quf~ : and i. q. A^akamapN [ a hill, or mound, &c.]: and a valley: and a level, or smooth, wide, depressed tract of land: and A^adogaAlN signifies mountains: and A^adogaAlu AlA^aroDi , [ tracts of ] land from which water has sunk into the earth, or receded: and low, or depressed, tracts of land: and level, or smooth, tracts thereof. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. dam~N , (T, M, Msb,) He smeared, or did over, (S, M, Msb, K,) a thing, (S, M, K, *) or the face, (Msb,) with any kind of dye [or the like ]: (S, Msb:) and a house, or chamber, with [ plaster of ] gypsum, (T, M, K,) or with mud or clay, (T,) and with [ a wash of ] quick lime: (TA:) and a ship with tar: (M, K:) and an eye, externally, (Lth, T, K,) or a pained eye, externally, (M,) with a dimaAm , (Lth, T, M, K,) i. e. any medicinal liniment, (Lth, T,) such as aloes, and saffron; (TA;) as also ↓ dm~m : (Kr, M, K:) [or this latter, probably, has an intensive signification: see also R. Q. 1:] and dam~ato , aor. and inf. n. as above, said of a woman, she smeared the parts around her eye with aloes or saffron: (M:) or dam~ati AlEayona she applied a collyrium to the eye; or smeared it with a dimaAm . (Msb.) You say also, dam~a Alqidori , aor. and inf. n. as above, He smeared, or did over, the [ stone ] cooking-pot with blood or spleen, [or with liver, (see damiymN ,]) after repairing it: (Lh, M:) and dum~at it (the [stone] cooking-pot) was smeared, or done over, with blood or spleen [or liver ], after it had been repaired: (T:) or was plastered with mud or clay, and with gypsum. (TA.) And dam~a AlS~adoEi , aor. and inf. n. as above, He smeared over the crack with blood and burnt hair mixed together; as also ↓ dam~amahu . (M.) ― -b2- [Hence,] dum~a biAl$~aHomi , said of a camel &c., (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, loaded [or overspread ] with fat; syn. A^awoqara or A^uwoqira . (So accord. to different copies of the S.) And dum~a [alone], inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He (a camel) had much fat and flesh, so that one could not feel in him the prominence of a bone. (T, TA.) And dum~a wajohuhu HusonFA (assumed tropical:) His face was [ flushed, ] as though it were overspread, with beauty. (M.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] bima dam~ato EayonaAhaA , [so I find it written, but I think it should be dum~ato ,] meaning (tropical:) What did she bring forth? or what has she brought forth? a male or a female? and dm~t fulaAnapu bigulaAmK [the verb (here written without any vowel-sign) being app. dum~ato , meaning dum~ato EayonaAhaA , because offspring, and especially boys, are among the things by which the eye is said to be refreshed, as it is by the application of a dimaAm ,] (tropical:) Such a woman brought forth a boy. (TA.) ― -b4- dam~a AlA^aroDa , (M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) He made the earth, or ground, even, (M, K,) as is done after turning it over for sowing. (M.) And dam~a juHorahu , said of the Jerboa, (T, S, M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (T,) It stopped up the mouth of its hole with its nabiy$ap [or earth which it had extracted ]: (T:) or it filled up its hole with earth: (S:) or it covered over its hole and made it even. (M, K.) And dam~a AlkamoA^apa He made the earth, or dust, even over the truffles. (K.) And damamotu EalaY Al$~aYo'i I covered over the thing; (T, TA;) as also damamotu Al$~aYo'a : (Ham p. 461: [see also R. Q. 1:]) and in like manner, damamotu Ealayohi Alqabora [ I covered up the grave over him ]: and ↓ damodamotu EalaY Al$~aYo'i I buried the thing, making the ground even over it. (T, TA. *) ― -b5- dam~ahu , (K,) or dam~a raA^osahu , (T, M,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) (assumed tropical:) He broke his head: (M, K:) or he struck, or beat, and broke, his head: (T:) or it signifies, accord. to Lh, (M,) or signifies also, (K,) he struck, or beat, his head, (M, K,) whether he broke it or not. (M.) And dam~a Zahorahu , aor. and inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He struck, or beat, his back with a brick, (M, TA,) and with a staff or stick, or with a stone: a tropical meaning, as is said in the A. (TA.) ― -b6- dam~ahumo , (Lh, T, M, K,) aor. as above, (Lh, T, M,) and so the inf. n., (M,) (assumed tropical:) He crushed them ( TaHanahumo ), and destroyed them; (Lh, T, M, K;) as also ↓ damodamahumo , and EalayohimN ↓ damodama : (M, K:) or this last ( dmdm Elyhm ) signifies He (God) destroyed them: and Al$~aYo'a ↓ damodamotu , I made the thing to cleave to the ground, and scattered it, or broke it, destroying it. (S.) ↓ fadamodama EalayohimN rab~uhumo , (M, TA,) in the Kur [xci. 14], (TA,) means And their Lord crushed them ( TaHanahumo ), and destroyed them: (M, TA:) or made punishment to fall, or come, upon them in common, or universally; expl. by A^aTobaqa Ealayohimu AlEa*aAba : (Zj, T, Bd, Jel, TA:) or made the earth to quake with them: (Fr, T, TA:) or was angry with them: (IAmb, T:) or spoke to them in anger: (TA:) for [the inf. n.] damodamapN signifies the being angry: (M, K:) and the speaking so as to disquiet, or agitate, a man: (T, TA:) and damodama Ealayohi he spoke to him in anger. (M, K.) You say also, dam~a fulaAnFA , meaning He (a man, IAar, T) punished such a one fully, or completely; (IAar, T, K;) as also ↓ damodamahu : (TA:) [or perhaps damodama Ealayohi ; for Az says, in another place, at the close of this art.,] IAar says that damodama signifies he punished fully, or completely; or inflicted a full, or complete, punishment. (T.) ― -b7- dam~a AlHijora , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) said of a stallion horse, He leaped the mare. (K.) ― -b8- dam~a , (M, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) also signifies He hastened; syn. A^asoraEa [app. in a trans. sense; for otherwise, accord. to rule, the aor. should be yadim~u , with kesr]. (M, K, TA. In the CK, [erroneously,] AaSoraEa .) -A2- dam~a ; (T, Msb;) sec. pers. damamota , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. (Ks, Lh, T, S, M, Msb, K) and ; (S, M, K;) and damimota , (M, Msb, K,) aor. ; (AZ, T, Msb;) and damumota , (T, M, Msb, K) aor. ; (T, Msb;) inf. n. (of the last, TA, or of all, M) damaAmapN ; (S, M, K;) the last of these verbs mentioned by IKtt on the authority of Kh; (TA;) and [said to be] the only instance of its kind, among reduplicative verbs, (T, Msb, TA,) except labubota and $arurota (Msb, TA) and fakukota , mentioned in the K, and Eazuzati Al$~aApu , mentioned by IKh; (TA;) He (a man, T, S, Msb) was, or became, such as is termed damiym [q. v.]: (Ks, Lh, T, S, Msb:) or he did evil; syn. A^asaA='a . (M, K. [See also 4.])

(TA.) ― -b4- Also, The splitting ( ta$aq~uq [which is intrans., but I think it is a mistake for ta$oqiyq , which is trans.,]) of a thing into several oblong pieces of the measure of the cubit in length. sourceDefinition: , in its primary acceptation, has the signification explained in the first sentence of this article. (S, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, it is used in the sense of] (tropical:) Power, or ability; as also ↓ *iraAEN ; (TA;) or a man's reach, or extent of power or ability. (Msb.) And hence the phrases, DaAqa biAlA^amori *aroEuhu , and ↓ *iraAEuhu , (K,) and DaAqa biAlA^amori *aroEFA , (S, Msb, K,) in which the last word is in the accus. case as an explicative, for the original form of the phrase is that first mentioned, (TA,) and sometimes they said ↓ *iraAEFA , (S, TA,) (tropical:) He was unable to do, or accomplish, the thing, or affair; as though meaning, he stretched forth his arm to it and it did not reach it; (S, TA; *) or these phrases are thus used because he who is short in the fore arm will not reach that which he who is long therein reaches, nor will the power of the former equal that of the latter; therefore they are proverbially applied to him whose power falls short of the attainment, or accomplishment, of an affair: (TA:) or he lacked strength, or power, or ability, to do, or accomplish, the thing, or affair, and found not any way of escape from what was disagreeable therein: (K:) or he was unable to bear, or endure, or undertake, the thing, or affair. (Msb.) You say also, maA liY bihi *aroEN , and ↓ *iraAEN , (tropical:) I have not power, or ability, to do it. (TA.) And kasara *`lika mino *aroEiY (tropical:) That disabled, hindered, prevented, or withheld, me from doing that which I desired. (TA.) And AiqoSido bi*aroEika (tropical:) Deal thou gently with thyself; moderate thyself restrain thyself; i. q. AirobaEo EalaY nafosika ; (S, TA;) and let not thy soul, or mind, carry thee beyond thy measure or extent [ of power or ability ]. (TA.) And A^aboTarotu fulaAnFA *aroEhu (tropical:) I imposed upon such a one more than he was able to do: (S, TA:) but *aroEN also signifies (assumed tropical:) the body: and [accord. to IAar] A^abaTaraniY *aroEiY means (tropical:) He wasted my body, and cut off my means of subsistence. (TA.) [See also art. bTr .] You likewise say, rajulN ↓ raHobu Al*~iraAEi [and Al*~aroEi ] (tropical:) A man having ample strength, and power, and might in war or fight, courage, valour, or prowess. (TA. [See also raHobN .]) And DaEiyfu Al*~aroEi (tropical:) Impotent. (KL.) ― -b3- And hence, fulaAnN xaAliY Al*~aroEi (tropical:) Such a one has his heart devoid of anxieties, or solicitudes, and griefs; because the heart is sometimes one of the seats of power: or it may mean, agreeably with the original signification of *aroEN , such a one is free from the causes of occupation which require the stretching forth of the fore arm and extending of the hand. (Har p. 131.) And rajulN waAsiEN Al*~aroEi , and ↓ Al*~iraAEi , (tropical:) A man large, or liberal, in disposition. (K.) And kabura fiY *aroEiY (assumed tropical:) Its occurrence, or befalling, was of great moment, momentous, grievous, or distressing, to me. (TA.) ― -b4- *aroEN also signifies The measure of anything: and naxolapN *aroEu rajalK , A palm-tree of the measure of the stature of a man. (TA.)

definition: , of a man, (Msb,) [The part ] from the elbow to the extremities of the fingers;
sourceDefinition: , of a man, (Msb,) [The part ] from the elbow to the extremities of the fingers; (Mgh, Msb;) the fore arm; syn. saAEidN [q. v.; thus corresponding to the saAq of the leg]: (Lth, K:) and (tropical:) [the space ] from the extremity of the elbow to the extremity of the middle finger: (M, Mgh, * K: [in the last of which, the space is plainly shown to be meant, like as the part is shown in the Msb to be meant in the explanation cited above from that work and the Mgh: see also jariybN :]) in both these senses, sometimes masc., (K,) accord. to Kh: (TA:) J says, (TA,) as relating to the arm, it is masc. and fem.; but Sb says that it is fem.: (S, TA:) [Mtr says,] it is fem.: (Mgh:) [Fei says,] the measure so called is in most instances fem.: accord. to ISk, it is fem.; but some of the Arabs make it masc.: Fr says that it is fem.; but that some of [the tribe named] 'Okl make it masc.: As did not know an instance of its being masc.: and Zj says that such an instance is extr.; not choice: (Msb:) the measure thus called, [i. e. the cubit, ] (Msb,) the *iraAEN mukas~arap [or cubit which is divided into fractions ], (Mgh,) is six qabaDaAt [or fists ] (Mgh, Msb) of middling measure; (Msb;) and this is called *iraAEu AlEamaAm~api [ the cubit of the common people, or the common cubit ], because it wants one qaboDap [or fist ] of what is called *iraAEu Almaliki [ the cubit of the king ], namely one of the Kisràs, (Mgh, Msb,) not the last of them, whose *rAE was seven qabaDaAt : (Mgh:) [see also miylN : it is also an astronomical measure; and as such, it seems, from several instances in which it is mentioned by Kzw and other writers, to be, probably, by rule, two degrees; nearly the half, or quarter, of the length assigned in different instances to the measure termed rumoHN ; but, like the latter, not precise nor uniform in every instance:] the dim. is ↓ *uriy~aEapN , with p because it is fem.; (TA;) or ↓ *urayoEN [or ↓ *uray~iEN , without p , accord. to those who make it masc.]: (L voce HarobN :) the pl. is A^a*oruEN and *uroEaAnN ; (O, Msb, K;) or, accord. to Sb, the former only; (S, Msb;) and Sb adds, they have given it this form of pl. because it is fem.; meaning, that fiEaAlN and fuEaAlN and faEiylN , when fem., have the pl. of the measure A^afoEulN . (TA.) In the phrase Alv~awobu saboEN fiY vamaAniyapK [ The garment, or piece of cloth, is seven cubits by eight spans], they say sbE because A^a*oruE is fem., and vmAnyp because A^a$obaAr is masc.; (S; [and the like is said in the Mgh;]) and because the length is measured by the *rAE , and the breadth by the $ibor . (S in art. vmn .) *iraAEN is also used as an epithet, applied to a masc. n.: thus they say, h`*aA vawobN *iraAEN [ This is a garment, or piece of cloth, a cubit in length ]. (Kh.) You say also, huwa min~iY EalaY Haboli Al*~iraAEi It is prepared, or made ready, on my part: (S:) and huwa laka EalaY Haboli Al*~iraAEi I will pay it to thee in ready money: or it is prepared, or made ready, for thee: the Hbl being a certain vein in the *rAE . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence several tropical significations:] see *aroEN , in six places: and see also *araAEN . ― -b3- Hence also, (Z, TA,) (tropical:) The instrument with which one measures the length of the *rAE [or cubit ], (S, Z, O, Mgh, K,) made of a piece of wood, (Mgh,) or whether it be iron or a rod of wood. (O, K.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) A sleeve: as in the phrase vawobN muwa$~aY Al*~iraAEi (assumed tropical:) [ a garment, or piece of cloth, variegated, or figured, in the sleeve ]: pl. ↓ ma*aAriEu , a pl. not agreeing with its sing., like malaAmiHu and maHaAsinu . (TA.) ― -b5- Of the fore legs of bulls or cows, and of sheep or goats, [The arm; i. e.] the part above the kuraAE : and of the fore legs of camels and horses and mules and asses, [likewise the arm; i. e.] the part above the waZiyf : (K:) [also the arm-bone of any of the animals here mentioned:] accord. to Lth, (TA,) of any animal, [but this is by synecdoche, (assumed tropical:) the fore leg; ] i. q. yadN ; (Msb, TA;) applying to the whole of whatever is called thus: (TA:) [thus, again, corresponding to saAqN ; this latter term, in like manner, having a proper and a synecdochical acceptation. sourceDefinition: A she-camel by which the archer, or the like, conceals himself from the game, (S, K, TA,) walking by her side, and shooting, or casting, when the object puts itself in his power, having first left the she-camel to roam at pleasure with the wild animals in order that they may become familiar with her; (TA;) like dariyoy^apN ; (S;) as also ↓ *araEN : (K:) pl. *uruEN . (IAar.) ― -b2- Hence, (tropical:) Anything that brings one near to a thing; (IAar;) a means of access, nearness, intimacy, ingratiation, attachment, or connexion; syn. wasiylapN ; (S, Msb, K, TA;) and sababN ; and wuSolapN ; (TA;) as also ↓ *uroEapN : (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) pl. *araAy^iEu . (S, Msb.) You say, fulaAnN *ariyEatiY A_ilayoka (tropical:) Such a one is my means of access to thee, and of attachment to thee, or connexion with thee. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, [like dariyoy^apN ,] A ring by aiming at which one learns the art of shooting, or casting [ the lance &c. ]. (TA.)

definition: [ He prepared the A^arobaAq , pl.
sourceDefinition: [ He prepared the A^arobaAq , pl. of riboqN ]. One says, ram~aditi AlD~aA^onu farab~qo rab~qo , i.e. [ The ewes have secreted milk in their udders: therefore ] prepare thou the A^arobaAq : prepare thou the ArbAq : for they will bring forth soon: (S, K:) because they [begin to] secrete milk in their udders EalaY raA^osi Alwaladi [i. e. at the time of bringing forth, or when about to produce the young]. (S.) It is not thus in the case of she-goats: therefore, (S,) in the case of these, one says ran~qo , with n , (S, K,) meaning “ wait thou: ” because they show sings of pregnancy in the state of their udders, and bring forth after some length of time: and [in the case of these] one says also ram~iqo , with m . (K. [See arts. rmq and rnq .]) ― -b2- One also says, rab~aqa A^avonaA='a AlHaboli , meaning He made loops in the middle of the rope to put upon the necks of the young lambs or kids. (T in art. vnY .) ― -b3- See also 1. ― -b4- rab~aqotu AlkalaAma I interlarded, or embel-lished, the speech, or discourse, with falsehood; as also ram~aqotuhu ; syn. laf~aqotu bayonahu ; (JK;) [or laf~aqotuhu ; for] tarobiyqu AlkalaAmi signifies talofiyquhu ; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) as also taromiyquhu . (Ibn-'Abbád.)

definition: A cord having in it a number of loops wherewith lambs, or kids, are tied, or made fast;
sourceDefinition: A cord having in it a number of loops wherewith lambs, or kids, are tied, or made fast; any one of which loops is termed ↓ riboqapN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ raboqapN : (K:) or a cord which is doubled in the form of a ring, into which is put the head of a sheep or goat, and which is then tied, or made fast: so, says Az, I have heard from the Arabs of the desert of Benoo-Temeem: (TA:) pl. [of mult.] ribaAqN (S, Msb, K) and ribaqN and [of pauc.] A^arobaAqN . (S, K.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) xalaEa AlA_isolaAmi mino Eunuqihi ↓ riboqapa , (S, Msb, TA,) occurring in a trad., (S,) (tropical:) He cast off the tie of El-Islám, (Msb, TA,) with which he had bound himself, (TA,) [ from his neck. ] (Msb, TA. [See also xalaEa .]) And lakumu AlEahodu maA lamo taA^okuluwA Alr~ibaAqa , also occurring in a trad., (S,) meaning (tropical:) [ The covenant is yours ] as long as ye sever not the tie with which ye are bound; this tie being likened to the riboq upon the necks of lambs or kids; and the severing thereof, to the beast's eating its riboq , and severing it; for thereby the beast becomes free from the tie. (TA.) And in a trad. of 'Omar, Huj~uwA biAl*~ur~iy~api laA taA^okuluwA A^arozaAqahaA wata*aruwA A^arobaAqahaA fiY A^aEonaAqihaA [ Perform ye the pilgrimage with the women: devour not their means of subsistence, while ye leave their ties upon their necks ]: he likens the obligations imposed upon them to ArbAq . (TA.) One says also, ↓ Hal~a riboqatahu , meaning (tropical:) He removed from him his anxiety: (K, TA:) and so ↓ qaTaEa riboqatahu . (TA.)

AirotijaAjN , (K,) It was, or became, in a state of commotion or agitation; (S, A, Msb, * K;) or of convulsion, or violent motion; or it shook, quaked, or quivered; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ tarajoraja ; (A, K;) and ↓ rajoraja inf. n. rajorajapN ; (S, K; but they mention only the inf. n. of this verb;) and so ↓ raj~a , inf. n. raj~N : (K, * TA; but of this verb, also, only the inf. n. is mentioned:) Artj~ is quasi-pass. of raj~ahu ; (T, A, Msb;) and is said of the sea, as meaning it was, or became, in a state of commotion or agitation (S, Msb) with its waves; and in like manner of other things: (S:) and ↓ tarajoraja signifies it (a thing) went to and fro; and is said of a woman's flesh; (S;) or [particularly] of her hinder part; (A;) or of both. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the blowing of the horn [on the day of resurrection], fatarotaj~u AlA^aroDu biA^aholihaA And the earth shall be in a state of commotion or agitation, with its inhabitants. (TA.) See also 4. ― -b2- [Hence,] Artj~ AlZ~alaAmu (assumed tropical:) The darkness became confused. (Msb.) ― -b3- And Artj~ AlkalaAmu (assumed tropical:) The speech, or language, became confused; mentioned by ISd in this art: (TA:) or Airotaj~a Ealayohi AlkalaAmu (tropical:) the speech, or language, became conflicting and confused to him. (A.) [See also Aurotuj~a Ealayohi in the first paragraph of art. rtj .]

definition: Lean, or emaciated, sheep or goats, (S, K,) and camels: (TA:) and naEojapN rajaAjapN a lean, or an emaciated, ewe;
sourceDefinition: Lean, or emaciated, sheep or goats, (S, K,) and camels: (TA:) and naEojapN rajaAjapN a lean, or an emaciated, ewe; (S, K;) or a weak ewe, that has no marrow in her bones. (As, TA.) And Weak men, and camels; (S, K;) and so ↓ rajoraAjN applied to the latter, and to men as meaning weak, without understanding, intellect, or intelligence. (TA.) Hence, it is said of men who have become weak by reason of travel, and whose camels upon which they are riding have also become weak, fahumo rajaAjN waEalaY rajaAji [ And they are weak men, and upon weak beasts]. (S.)

definition: He made it, or rendered it, soft, yielding, flaccid, flabby, lax, slack, uncompact, crummy, fragile, frangible, brittle, friable, easily or quickly broken;
sourceDefinition: He made it, or rendered it, soft, yielding, flaccid, flabby, lax, slack, uncompact, crummy, fragile, frangible, brittle, friable, easily or quickly broken; i. q. jaEalahu rixowFA ; as also ↓ rAxAhu . (K.) You say, ArxY Alr~ibaATa [ He relaxed, or slackened, the tie, or bond ]; (M, TA;) and ↓ rAxAhu , inf. n. muraAxaApN . (JK, TA.) And lahu mino xinaAqihi ↓ raAxi [lit, Relax thou, or slacken thou, his cord with which he is being strangled ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) make thou his circumstances ample and easy to him; ease him; relieve him; or grant him a delay. (TA. [See a similar phrase in art. rbw , conj. 2.]) And A^aroxi lahu qayodahu Make thou his shackle, or shackles, wide, or ample, not strait, to him. (TA.) And A^aroxi lahu AlHabola [lit. Relax thou, or slacken thou, to him the rope ]; meaning (tropical:) give thou to him ample scope for using his own judgment, or discretion, in the disposal, or management, of his affairs, so that he may go whither he pleases. (TA.) And ArxY Alfarasa and lilofarasi He lengthened the horse's rope. (K.) And ArxY lahu AlT~iwala [lit. He relaxed, or slackened, his tether ]; meaning (tropical:) he left him to his own affair. (A, TA.) And ArxY EimaAmatahu [lit. He slackened, or loosened, his turban ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) he became, or felt, in a state of security or safety, tranquil, or at ease; (K, TA;) because the turbans are not slackened, or loosened, ( laA turoxaY ,) in difficulty, or hardship. (TA.) And ArxY Als~itori (S, Msb, K) wagayorahu (S) He let loose, let down, or lowered, the veil, or curtain, &c. (S, K.) And ArxY viyaAbahu EalaY rijolayohi [ He let, or made, his clothes hang down loosely upon his legs ] in riding and in sitting [&c.]. (TA in art. rsl .) [And ArxY dumuwEFA (assumed tropical:) He shed tears. ] And ArxAhu xaTobuhu (tropical:) His state, or condition, made him to enjoy an easy, ample, or unstraitened, life, or a life of ease and plenty. (T, TA.) ― -b2- Arxt , said of a she-camel, [app. for Arxt SalaAhaA , i. e. She relaxed the part on either side of her tail, virtually] means SalaAhaA ↓ AisotaroxaY , (S, K, TA,) i. e. [ the part on either side of her tail became relaxed; or] her SalawaAni [or parts on the right and left of her tail ] gaped, [or receded from each other, ] on the occasion of bringing forth. (T, TA.) ― -b3- A_iroxaA='N also signifies A sort of running: (S:) or vehement running: (K:) or running exceeding what is termed taqoriybN : (JK, K: [see 2 in art. qrb :]) or running ( HuDorN ) that is not ardent, or not impetuous: (A, TA:) or gentleness in running: (Ham p. 158:) accord. to Az, AlA_iroxaA='u AlA^aEolaY means The most vehement [ running termed ] HuSor ; and AlA_iroxaA='u AlA^adonaY is less than that: and ArxY fiY Eadowihi , said of a horse, signifies A^aHoDara [app. as meaning He rose in his running ]; and is from ruxaA='N as an epithet applied to wind. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, ArxY daAb~atahu , meaning He made his beast to go the pace, or in the manner, termed A_iroxaA=' , explained above: (Lth, K:) [or,] accord. to A 'Obeyd, AlA_iroxaA='u signifies the leaving a horse to follow his own eager desire in running, without fatiguing him. (S.)

definition: He (a horse) remitted, or flagged, in his running;
sourceDefinition: He (a horse) remitted, or flagged, in his running; or was, or became, remiss, or languid, therein. (Az, TA.) And [in like manner] fiY AlA^amori ↓ AstrxY [ He remitted, or flagged, in the affair; or was, or became, remiss, or languid, therein ]. (K in arts. bn$ and fn$ , &c.) And trAxY Eano HaAjatihi He remitted, or flagged, in the accomplishment of his want; or he was, or became, remiss, or languid, therein. (TA.) ― -b2- He drew back, held back, or hung back, (JK, K, TA,) Ean~iY from me, (TA,) or Eani Al$~aYo'a from the thing. (JK.) ― -b3- He was, or became, slow, sluggish, tardy, dilatory, late, or backward. (JK, TA.) You say also, trAxY Als~amaA='u The rain delayed; or was tardy, late, or backward. (S, K.) [And trAxY Alwaqotu The time was, or became, late: and it became protracted. And trAxY Eanohu It was, or became, after, or later than, it: see mutaraAxK , below.] And trAxY AlA^amoru The affair, or case, was, or became, protracted; the time thereof became extended. (Msb.) And fiY AlA^amori taraAxK In the affair, or case, is ample time or scope [ for action &c. ]; syn. fusoHapN ; (Msb, TA;) and extension, or protractedness: (TA:) or remoteness; referring to the case of the resurrection, i. e. the time thereof. (Mgh in art. ntj .)

definition: Firm, stable, strong, solid, compact, or sound;
sourceDefinition: Firm, stable, strong, solid, compact, or sound; (S, M, K;) applied to a thing: (M:) and ↓ muroSanN and ↓ maroSuwnN , made, or rendered, firm, stable, strong, &c. (TA.) You say diroEN raSiynN A coat of mail firmly, strongly, or compactly, made. (TA.) And ↓ binaA='N muroSanN A building made, or rendered, firm, stable, strong, &c. (TA.) And rajulN lahu raA^oYN raSiynN (assumed tropical:) [ A man having firm, or sound, judgment ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, applied to a man, i. q. raziynN (assumed tropical:) [ Grave, staid, steady, sedate, or calm; and forbearing: still, or motionless: or firm, or sound, of judgment: wise, or sensible ]. (M.) ― -b3- fulAnN raSiynN biHaAjatika (assumed tropical:) Such a one is gracious, or knowing and gracious, with respect to thy want; or mindful, regardful, or considerate, thereof; syn. HafiY~N bihaA . (S, K. *) ― -b4- raSiynN also signifies Pained, or suffering pain: (S, K:) so in the saying of a poet, yaquwlu A_in~iY raSiynu Aljuwofi faA@soquwniY [ He says, or he saying, Verily I am suffering pain of the belly, or chest, therefore give ye me to drink ]. (S.) -A2- What are termed Alr~aSiynaAni , (S,) or raSiynaA Alfarasi , (K,) are The [ two ] extremities of the qaSab [or round and hollow bones, meaning here of the arms, (in one of my copies of the S, erroneously, of the EaSab , or sinews, )] that are set in, or upon, the raDofap [n. un. of raDofN , which is evidently the correct reading, meaning the bones that are between the arm and the shank ], in the knee. (S, K.)

definition: A certain weapon, (L, TA,) well known;
sourceDefinition: A certain weapon, (L, TA,) well known; (L, Msb, K;) [i. e. a spear, or lance; one with which one thrusts, not which one casts; accord. to El-Hareeree, (cited by De Sacy in his “ Chrest. Ar, ” sec. ed., ii. 332,) not so called unless having its iron head mounted upon it: ] pl. rimaAHN and A^aromaAHN , (S, L, Msb, K,) the former of mult. and the latter of pauc. (L.) [Hence the saying,] kasaruwA bayonahumo rumoHFA [lit. They broke a spear between them, or among them; meaning] (tropical:) evil, or mischief, [or enmity, or contention, ] happened between them, or among them. (A, TA.) And muniynaA biyawomK kaZil~i Alr~umoHi (tropical:) We were tried with a long and distressing day. (A, TA.) And humo EalaY baniY fulaAnK rumoHN waAHidN (tropical:) [ They are in league against the sons of such a one as one man ]. (A, TA.) And kaA^an~a Eayonayohi fiY rumoHayoni [ As though his two eyes were upon two spears ] is said of one in fear and fright, and looking hardly, or intently; and sometimes of one in anger. (TA.) [The dim. is ↓ rumayoHN . And hence the saying,] A^axa*a rumayoHa A^abiY saEodK (assumed tropical:) He (a man, K, TA, or an old man, TA) stayed himself upon a staff by reason of extreme old age, or decrepitude: by AbwsEd is meant Lukmán the Sage, (K, TA,) who is mentioned in the Kur-án: (TA:) or Marthad Ibn-Saad: or it is a surname applied to old age, and decrepitude. (K, TA.) ― -b2- See also raAmiHN . ― -b3- [As a measure in astronomy, accord. to modern Arabian astronomers, it is Four degrees and a half; the eightieth part of a great circle; and accord. to various works on practical law, it consists of twelve A^a$obaAr (or spans ): but there is reason to believe that ancient usage differed from the modern, with respect to both these measures, and was not precise nor uniform: in an instance mentioned voce zubaAnaY , it appears to be about twice the measure stated above; i. e., about nine degrees; and to consist of five cubits, a measure perhaps equal to twelve spans. ] ― -b4- A^axa*ato rimaAHahaA , said of the [species of barley-grass called] buhomaY , (T, S, A, TA,) and of any similar pasture, (T, TA,) (tropical:) It assumed, or put forth, its prickles, (A, * TA,) or became dry in its prickles, (T, TA,) and thus (T, A, TA) resisted the attempts of animals to pasture upon it. (T, S, A, L, TA.) Also, said of camels, (tropical:) They became fat, (S, K, TA,) or yielded milk plentifully; (S, TA;) as though they prevented one's slaughtering them; (K;) or because their owner is prevented from slaughtering them: (S:) or they became goodly in the eye of their owner so that he was prevented from slaughtering them; (A, * TA;) and so A^axa*ato A^asoliHatahaA . (TA.) One says also naAqapN *aAtu rumoHK (tropical:) A fat she-camel; and A_ibilN *awaAtu rimaAHK (tropical:) fat camels; because their owner, when desiring to slaughter them, looks at their fatness and their goodly appearance, and is prevented from slaughtering them. (A, * TA.) ― -b5- rimaAHu Aljin~i (tropical:) [ The pestilence termed ] AlT~aAEuwnu . (A, K.) [See the following verses.] ― -b6- rimaAHu AlEaqorabi i. q. $awolaAhaA [evidently a mistranscription for $awolaAtuhaA , i. e. (assumed tropical:) The stings of scorpions, with which they strike; AlEqrb being here used, as it seems to be in some other instances, as a coll. gen. n.: that such is the case is shown by the verses here following, quoted in the TA as an ex. of rimaAHu Aljin~i ]. (K.) A poet, cited by Th, says, laEamoruka maA xa$iytu EalaY A^ubaY~K rimaAHa baniY muqay~idapi AlHimaAri wal`kin~iY xa$iytu EalaY A^ubaY~K rimaAHa Aljin~i A^awo A_iy~aAka HaAri [ By thy life, or by thy religion, I feared not, for Ubeí, the stings of the scorpions; but I feared, for Ubeí, the pestilence, or thee, O Harith; HaAri being for HaArivu ]; by bnY mqy~dp AlHmAr he means the scorpions. (TA.) ― -b7- [The dim.] ↓ rumayoHN is a proper name of (assumed tropical:) The penis; (K, * TA;) like as $urayoHN is a proper name for “ the vulva of a woman. ” (TA.) ― -b8- ↓ *uw Alr~umayoHi means (assumed tropical:) A species of jerboa, (K, TA,) long in the hind legs, in the middle [?] of each waZiyf [here meaning metacarpus ] having a nail in excess [ of those of the hind feet; for the fore feet have each five toes of which one only has no nail, and the hind feet have each but three toes, all of which have nails]: or it means any jerboa: and its rmH [evidently a mistranscription for rumayoH ] is its tail. (TA. [It is there added, wrmAHh $wlAthA ; another mistranscription, and an obvious solecism; or probably some words which should have preceded these have been omitted by the copyist.])

definition: , (S, A, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. zax~N , (TA,) He pushed him, or thrust him, (S, A,) or made him to fall, (K,) into a depressed place, or a deep hollow or cavity: (S, A, K:) [or he pushed him, or thrust him, in any manner; for] zax~N signifies, accord. to IDrd, any pushing, or thrusting. (TA.) You say, zux~a fiY Aln~aAri , (A,) or zux~a bihi fiY Aln~aAri , He was pushed, or thrust, and thrown, or cast, into the fire [of Hell]. (TA.) And zux~a fiY qafaAhu (A, TA) He was pushed, or thrust, on the back of his neck: or he was pushed, or thrust, on the back of his neck, and expelled. (TA.) And it is said in a trad. of Aboo-Moosà, mano yat~abiEi AlquroA=na yahobiTo bihi EalaY riyaADi Aljan~api wamano yat~abiEohu AlquroA=nu yazux~a fiY qafaAhu Hat~aY yaqo*ifa bihi fiY naAri jahan~ama [ Whosoever follows the Kur-án as his guide, it will make him to alight upon the gardens, or meadows, of Paradise; and whomsoever the Kur-án follows as a punisher, it will push, or thrust, upon the back of his neck, until it shall cast him into the fire of Hell ]. (S.) One says also of lambs or kids, tuzax~u , meaning They are driven; and impelled from behind them. (TA.) And of a driver, zax~a AlA_ibila He drove the camels quickly, and urged them on. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zax~a bibawolihi , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He cast forth his urine; (K, TA;) and propelled it. (TA.) And zax~ato biAlmaA='i , and zax~ati AlmaA='a , She (a woman) ejected the [ seminal ] fluid. (TA. [See zax~aAxapN .]) ― -b3- Hence also, (TA,) zax~a AlmaroA^apa , (S, * A, * K,) aor. as above, (S, A,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) He compressed the woman; (A, K;) as also ↓ zaxozaxahaA , (K,) inf. n. zixozaAxN . (TA.) ― -b4- And zax~ahu biAlr~umoHi i. q. zaj~ahu [ He pierced him, or thrust him, with the pointed iron foot of the spear ]; like zalaxahu . (TA in art. zlx .) ― -b5- And zax~a , (K,) and zax~a binafosihi , (TA,) [as though meaning “ he propelled himself, ”] He leaped: (K, TA:) thus, sometimes a man leaps a nahor [here meaning a rivulet for irrigation], putting his misoHaAp in the middle of it. (TA.) ― -b6- And zax~a , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He went quickly; [as though propelling himself:] (TA:) he (a driver) went, or journeyed, a violent, or rigorous, pace. (K, TA.) -A2- zax~a , (S, K,) [aor., accord. to analogy, ,] inf. n. as above, (S,) He (a man) was, or became, angered, or enraged. (S, K. [See also zax~apN .]) -A3- zax~a Aljamoru , (S, A, K,) in some copies of the K, erroneously, Alxamoru , (TA,) aor. , (S, K,) with kesr, (S,) and , with damm, [which is anomalous,] (TA,) inf. n. zaxiyxN (S, * A, * K) and zax~N , (K,) The live coals glistened: (K:) or glistened vehemently: (S, A:) and in like manner, AlHariyru [ the silk ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: He disquieted, disturbed, agitated, or flurried, him; (IDrd, S, K;) and removed him from his place: (S, A, Msb, K:) and ↓ zaEajahu signifies the same. (IDrd, K.) And it is said in a trad., raA^ayotu Eumura yuzoEiju A^abaA bakorK , meaning I saw 'Omar rousing Aboo-Bekr, and not suffering him to remain still. (TA.) And in another, AlHalifu yuzoEiju Als~iloEapa wayaHomaqu Albarakapa , meaning, accord. to Az, [ Swearing ] lowers in estimation [ the commodity that one desires to recommend thereby and does away with the blessing thereof]: or, accord. to IAth, causes it to be easy of sale and to go forth from the hand of its owner [ but does away with the blessing thereof]. (TA.) A_izoEaAjN [is the inf. n.; and as inf. n. of the pass. verb,] signifies [The being disquieted, &c.; and hence,] the quitting of home. (Har p. 392.)

(TA.)

definition: A musical reed, or pipe;
sourceDefinition: A musical reed, or pipe; (S, * A, Msb, * K, * TA;) what is called in Persian naAYo [now generally meaning a flute ]; (marginal note in a copy of the KT;) as also ↓ zam~aArapN , (K,) [which latter, by many pronounced zum~aArap , and generally so pronounced in Egypt, is applied to a double reed-pipe, figured and described in my work on the Modern Egyptians,] and ↓ mazomuwrN and ↓ mazomuwrN , (IAth,) the latter like magoluwqN and magoruwdN : (TA:) pl. of the first, (S, A,) and of the last two, mazaAmiyru . (S, * A.) It is related in a trad., that Mohammad, on hearing Aboo-Moosà El-Ash'aree reciting, said to him, laqado A^uEoTiyta mizomaArFA mino mazaAmiyri A=li daAwuwda (tropical:) [ Verily thou hast been gifted with a pipe like that of David himself ]; likening the sweetness of his voice and melody to the sound of the mizomaAr ; (TA;) as though he had musical pipes in his throat: or mzAmyrA=l dAwwd is here the same as mazomuwraAt daAwuwd : (A:) for, ― -b2- mazaAmiyru daAwuwda also signifies [ The Psalms of David; ] what David used to sing, or chant, ( yatagan~aY bihi , in the CK yutagan~aY bh ,) of the Psalms: (K:) and to such is likened the utmost sweetness of voice in reciting: and A=l is said to be here redundant or pleonastic; meaning the person: (TA:) or (so in the TA, but in the K “ and ”) mzAmyr dAwwd signifies kinds of prayer, or supplication: it is pl. of mizomaArN and of ↓ mazomuwrN or muzomuwrN . (So in different copies of the K.)

definition: The twelfth letter of the alphabet;
sourceDefinition: The twelfth letter of the alphabet; called siynN . It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap [or non-vocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice]; and of the letters termed A^asaliy~ap , as also S and z , because proceeding from the tip of the tongue: its place of utterance is between that of S and that of z : and Az says hat it is never conjoined with either of these two letters in any Arabic word: (TA:) it is a sibilant letter; and is distinguished from S by the raising of the tongue to the palate [in the utterance of the latter], and from z by the suppression of the voice [in the utterance of the former]. (K in art. syn .) It is one of the letters of augmentation [occurring in the form AisotafoEala and its derivatives]. (S and L in art. syn .) [See also siynN in art. syn . It is sometimes substituted for S ; as in saqorN , for SaqorN : and for $ , as in siToranojN , for $iToranojN : (see De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., ii. 230-233: and iii. 530-532:)] and AZ says that some of the Arabs substitute for it t , (S and L and K * in art. syn ,) as in the saying (S and L in art. syn ) of 'Alyà Ibn-Arkam, (L ib.,) yaA qabaHa A@ll~`hu baniY Als~iEolaAti Eamoraw bona yarobuwEK $iraAra Aln~aAti layosuwA A^aEf~aA='a walaA A^akoyaAti [ O, may God remove far from good, or from prosperity, the sons of the Sialáh, 'Amr Ibn-Yarbooa, the worst of mankind: they are not chaste, nor sharp in intellect ]: he means Aln~aAsi and biA^akoyaAsi : (S and L ib.:) and in like manner one says TasotN for Tas~N . (TA in art. kyt .) ― -b2- y`s= in the Kur [commencing ch. xxxvi.] is like A=l=m= and H`m= at the commencement of chapters of the same; and is said by 'Ikrimeh to mean yaA A_inosaAnu [ O man ]; because it is followed by the words A_in~aka lamina Almurosaliyna : (S and L in art. syn :) or it means either thus, or yaA say~idu [ O man of dignity ]. (K in art. syn .) -A2- sa is a particle peculiarly prefixed to the aor., rendering it clearly denotative of the future, (Mughnee, and S * and L * in art. syn ,) as in sayafoEalu [ He will do such a thing], (S and L ib.,) and considered as forming a part thereof, for which reason it does not exercise any government upon it: it is not contracted from sawofa , contrary to what the Koofees hold: nor is the extent of the future with it shorter than it is with sawofa , contrary to what the Basrees hold: the analytical grammarians term it Harofu tanofiysK , by which is meant a particle of amplification; because it changes the aor. from the strait time, which is the present, to the ample time, which is the future: but plainer that their expression is the saying of Z and others, [that it is] a particle denoting the future. (Mughnee.) Kh asserts that it corresponds [as an affirmative] to [the negative] lano . (S and L in art. syn .) Some assert that it sometimes denotes continuance, not futurity: this is mentioned in relation to the saying in the Kur [iv. 93], satajiduwna A=xariyna [as though meaning Ye continually find others ]; and they adduce as an evidence thereof the saying in the same [ii. 136], sayaquwlu A@ls~afahaA='u mina A@ln~aAsi maA wal~aAhumo Eano qibolatihimo [as meaning The light-witted of the people continually say, What hath turned them away, or back, from their kibleh? ]; affirming that this was revealed after their saying maA wal~aAhumo : but this the grammarians know not; and that this verse was revealed after their saying mA wl~Ahm is not a fact agreed upon: moreover, if it be conceded, still continuance is inferred from the aor.; like as when you say, fulaAnN yaqoriY AlD~ayofa and yaSonaEu Aljamiyla , you mean that it is his custom to do thus. (Mughnee.) Z asserts that when it is prefixed to a verb signifying what is liked or disliked, it denotes that the event will inevitably happen: i. e., when it is prefixed to a verb signifying a promise or a threat, it corroborates and confirms its meaning. (Mughnee.) -A3- [As a numeral, s denotes Sixty. ]

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tasobiyEN , He made it seven; or called it seven; (S, K;) as also ↓ AsbEhu . (TA.) See also 1. ― -b2- He made it to have seven angles, or corners; to be heptagonal. (K.) ― -b3- He (God) gave him his reward, or recompense, seven times, or seven fold. (K.) An Arab of the desert said to a man who had done a good act to him, (TA,) sab~aEa A@ll~`hu laka May God give thee thy reward, or recompense, seven times, or seven fold. (K, TA.) The Arabs also said, sab~aEa A@ll~`hu laka A^ajorahaA May God multiply to thee the reward, or recompense, for it; meaning, for this good act: (Aboo-Sa'eed:) [for] tasobiyEN is used by them to signify the act of multiplying, though it be more than seven fold. (TA.) And sab~aEa A@ll~`hu lifulaAnK is used as meaning May God make a thing to be followed by another thing to such a one; in relation to good and to evil; as also tab~aEa lahu . (TA.) And sab~aEa A@ll~`hu laka meaning May God bless thee with seven children. (TA.) ― -b4- He washed it (namely, a vessel,) seven times. (K.) Hence the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, kanaEoti A@l~atiY qaAmato tusab~iEu suw^orahaA [ Like her who has arisen to wash out seven times her remains of beverage in the bottom of a vessel, left by a drinker; that drinker, as is said in a marginal note in my copy of the TA, being her dog]: or, accord. to Es-Sukkaree, the meaning is, to give as alms her suw^or [ remains of beverage in the bottom of a vessel after one had drunk, or remains of food &c., ], thereby seeking to have her reward, or recompense, multiplied; suw^orahaA being used by the poet for bisuw^orihaA . (TA.) ― -b5- sb~E AlquroA=na [app. followed by lahu or Ealayohi ] He appointed him the reading, or recitation, of the Kur-án [ in seven portions so that he should complete the whole ] in every seven nights. (O, L, K.) ― -b6- sb~E liA@moraA^atihi , (K, TA,) or EinodahaA and lahaA ↓ A^asobaEa , (TA,) He remained with his wife seven nights. (K, TA.) In like manner one says val~ava ; and thus of every number from one to ten; in relation to any saying or action. (TA.) ― -b7- sb~Et She (a woman) brought forth at seven months. (TA.) ― -b8- sb~E daraAhimahu He made his dirhems to be seventy complete; but this is post-classical; (K;) and in like manner, drAhmh ↓ saboEana , meaning the same, and also post-classical, and not allowable; the proper phrase to express the meaning “ I made it to be seventy ” being kam~alotuhu saboEiyna . (TA.) ― -b9- sab~aEati Alqawomu The people, or company of men, completed the number of seven hundred men: (K, TA:) occurring in a trad, (TA.)

sourceDefinition: fem. of saboEapN , q. v. -A2- See also sabuEN in two places. -A3- Als~aboEu The place to which mankind shall be congregated (K, TA) on the day of resurrection. (TA.) Hence the trad., (K, TA,) which relates that while a pastor was among his sheep, or goats, the wolf rushed upon him, and took from them a sheep, or goat, and the pastor pursued him until he rescued it from him; whereupon the wolf looked aside towards him, and said to him, (TA,) mano lahaA yawoma Als~aboEi , meaning Who will be for it [namely, the sheep, or goat, as aider, or defender, ] on the day of resurrection? (K, TA:) thus expl. by I Aar, and mentioned by Sgh and the author of the L: (TA:) but to this is contradictory, or repugnant, yaEokuru , [in the CK erroneously written yaEokaru ,]) the saying of the wolf, (K, TA,) after the words mentioned above, (TA,) “ the day when it shall have no pastor but me; ” for the wolf will not be a pastor on the day of resurrection: or the meaning is, who shall be for it on the occasion of trials, when it shall be left to itself, without pastor, a spoil to the animals of prey: the animal of prey being thus made to be a pastor to it: (K, TA:) this is in the way of a trope: and accord. to this explanation, it may be [↓ yawoma Als~abuEi ] with damm to the b : (TA:) or yawomu Als~aboEi was a festival of their's in the Time of Ignorance, on which they were diverted from everything by their sport: (AO, K, TA:) and accord. to one relation [of the trad.] it is with damm to the b . (L, K.)

definition: (S, Sgh, Msb, K) and ↓ saboEN , (Sgh, Msb, K,) a dial.
sourceDefinition: (S, Sgh, Msb, K) and ↓ saboEN , (Sgh, Msb, K,) a dial. var., (Sgh, Msb,) and the form in common use with the vulgar, (Msb,) adopted also by several readers of the Kur in v. 4, (Msb, TA,) and often occurring in the poems of the Arabs, (TA,) and ↓ sabaEN , (Sgh, K,) a form adopted by two readers of the Kur in the place above mentioned, and perhaps a dial. var., (Sgh, TA,) The animal of prey; the rapacious animal; (K;) [ whether beast or bird; being sometimes applied to the latter, as, for instance, in the K, voce mixolabN ; but generally to the former:] or whatsoever has a fang, or canine tooth, with which it makes hostile attacks, and seizes its prey; (Msb;) such as the lion, [to which it is particularly applied by most of the Arabs in the present day,] and also (TA) such as the wolf and the lynx and the leopard, (Msb, TA,) and the like of these, that has a fang, and attacks men and beasts and makes them its prey: (TA:) the fox, however, is not thus called, though having a fang, (Msb, TA,) because he does not attack with it nor take prey, (Msb,) or because he does not attack small beasts, nor seize with his fang any animal; (TA;) and in like manner the hyena (Msb, TA) is not reckoned among the hostile animals thus called, wherefore the Sunneh allows that its flesh may be eaten, and requires that a compensation be made for it [by the sacrifice of a ram] if it be smitten [and killed] in the sacred territory or by a person in the state of ihrám: but as to the jackal, it is a noxious sbE , and its flesh is unlawful, because it is of the same kind as wolves, except that it is smaller in size and weaker in body: thus says Az: but some others say that the sbE is any hostile beast having a mixolab [or tearing claw ]: and it is said in the Mufradát to be thus called because of the perfectness of its strength; for Als~aboEu [seven] is one of the perfect numbers: (TA:) the pl. is sibaAEN , (Sb, S, Msb, K,) i. e., of sabuEN , which has no other pl.; (Sb, Msb;) A^asobuEN is also a pl., (Sgh, Msb, K,) but this is pl. of pauc. of ↓ saboEN , (Sgh, Msb,) which, not being a contraction [of sabuEN , but a dial. var. thereof], has also for its pls. [of mult.] subuwEN and subuwEapN , like SuquwrN and SuquwrapN , pls. of SaqorN . (TA.) See also saboEN : [and see sabuEapN .] You say of him who is very injurious, or mischievous, maA huwa A_il~aA sabuEN mina Als~ibaAEi (tropical:) [ He is none other than one of the animals of prey ]. sourceDefinition: A certain number of days; (S, * Msb, K; *) i. e. seven days; a week; (Msb;) also termed ↓ subuwEN , (Lth, Msb, K,) by some of the Arabs; (Lth, Msb;) [and ↓ suboEN , as shown by what follows:] pl. of the first A^asaAbiyEu . sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. sadamN , (S, M, K,) He repented and grieved: (S:) or he was, or became, affected with anxiety: or with anxiety together with repentance: or with wrath, or rage, together with grief. sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. saloqN , (TK,) He prostrated him on the back of his neck; (K;) or threw him down on his back; (S;) as also ↓ saloqaAhu , inf. n. siloqaA='N . (S, K.) You say, TaEanotuhu fasalaqotuhu and ↓ saloqayotuhu , i. e. [ I thrust him, or pierced him, and ] threw him down on his back. (S.) And salaqaniY liHulaAwapi AlqafaA and EalaY qafaAYa ↓ saloqaAniY He threw me down on my back: and so with S ; but more commonly with s . (TA, from a trad.) And salaqahu AlT~abiybu EalaY Zahorihi The physician extended him on his back. (TA.) And salaqahaA , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He threw her down on the back of her neck [or on her back ] for the purpose of compressing her; namely, his wife: (Msb:) or he spread her, and then compressed her; (S, K;) as also ↓ saloqaAhaA ; (S;) namely, a girl, or young woman. (K.) ― -b2- He thrust him, or pierced him, (K, TA,) with a spear; (TK;) and pushed him, or repelled him; and dashed himself, or his body, against him; (TA;) and ↓ saloqaAhu signifies the same; (K, TA;) inf. n. siloqaA='N : (TA:) [and he struck him, or smote him; for the inf. n.] saloqN signifies the act of striking, or smiting. (TA.) [Hence,] salaqahu biAlkalaAmi , (S, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. saloqN , (S, TA,) (tropical:) He hurt him, or displeased him, with speech; (S, K, TA;) spoke strongly, or severely, to him; (S, TA;) made him to hear that which he disliked, or hated, and did so much: (TA:) and salaqahu bilisaAnihi (assumed tropical:) he said to him that which he dislike, or hated. (Msb.) saquwkumo biA^alosinapK HidaAdK , in the Kur xxxiii. 19, means (tropical:) They hurt you, or displease you, (Fr, Jel, TA,) by what they say, or bite you, (Fr, TA,) or are extravagant, or vehement, in speech to you, (AO, S, TA,) or smite you, (Bd, Jel,) with sharp tongues: (Fr, Bd, TA:) saloqN signifying the act of assaulting, and smiting, with force, with the hand, or arm, or (assumed tropical:) with the tongue: (Bd:) and the verb is also with S ; but this is not allowable in the reading [of the Kur]. (TA.) ― -b3- You say also, salaqati AlA^aqodaAmu waAlHawaAfiru AlT~ariyqa , (TK,) inf. n. saloqN , (K,) The feet of men, and the hoofs of horses or the like, marked, or made marks upon, the road. (K, TK.) ― -b4- And salaqahu He flayed him with a whip. (K.) ― -b5- He galled it; namely, the back of his camel. (TA.) ― -b6- He (a beast) abraded the inner side of his (the rider's) thigh. (TA.) ― -b7- He peeled it off; namely, the flesh from the bone ( Eani AlEaZomi ); syn. AilotaHaAhu ; (O, K, TA;) he removed it therefrom. (TA.) ― -b8- He removed its hair, (Msb, K,) and its fur, (K,) with hot water, (Msb, K,) leaving the traces thereof remaining; (K;) aor. , inf. n. saloqN . (Msb.) ― -b9- He boiled it with fire: (K:) or he boiled it slightly: inf. n. as above. (TA.) You say, salaqotu Albaqolu I boiled the herbs, or leguminous plants, with fire, slightly: (S:) or I boiled them with water merely: thus heard by Az from the Arabs: (Msb:) and in like manner, eggs, (S, Msb,) in their shells: so says Az. (Msb.) You say also, salaqotu $ayoy^FA biAlmaA='i AlHaAr~i [ I cooked a thing with hot water ]. (Lth, TA.) And suliqa is said of anything as meaning It was [ boiled, i. e.] cooked with hot water (TA.) ― -b10- salaqa Albarodu Aln~abaAta The cold nipped, shrunk, shrivelled, or blasted, the herbage, or plants; syn. A^aHoraqahu [q. v.]. (K.) ― -b11- salaqa AlmazaAdapa , (inf. n. as above, TA,) He oiled, or greased, the leathern water-bag: (S, K:) and in like manner, AlA^adiyma [ the hide, or tanned hide ]. (TA.) And salaqa AlbaEiyra (K, TA) biAlhinaA='i (TA) He smeared the camel all over with tar: (K, TA:) from Ibn-'Abbád. (TA.) -A2- salaqa AljuwaAliqa , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. saloqN , (S, TA,) He inserted one of the two loops of the [ sack called ] jwAlq into the other: (S, TA:) or salaqa AlEuwda fiY AlEurowapi he inserted the stick into the loop [of the jwAlq ]; as also ↓ Aslqhu : (K:) accord. to AHeyth, saloqN signifies the inserting the [ stick called ] $iZaAZ at once into the two loops of the [ two sacks called ] juwaAliqaAni when they are put and bound upon the camel. (TA. [See also qaTaba AljuwaAliqa .]) -A3- salaqa AlHaAy^iTa : see 5. -A4- suliqato A^afowaAhunaA mino A^akoli waraqi Al$~ajari Our mouths broke out with pimples, or small pustules, from the eating of the leaves of trees. (TA. [See sulaAqN .]) -A5- Alit~aY suliqa EalayohaA ↓ h`*ihi saliyqatuhu and suiqahaA [ This is his nature, to which he was constitutionally adapted or disposed ]: said by Sb. (TA.) -A6- salaqa , [intrans., aor. ,] (S, K,) inf. n. saloqN , (TA,) He called out, cried out, or shouted; or did so vehemently; or with his utmost force: (S, K:) a dial. var. of Salaqa : (S:) he raised the voice: (Ibn-El-Mubárak, TA:) or he raised his voice on the occasion of the death of a man, or on the occasion of a calamity: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) accord. to IDrd, the meaning [of the inf. n.] is a woman's slapping and scratching her face: but the first explanation is more correct. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He ran. (K.) You say salaqa saloqapF He ran a run. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)

definition: [ Bete; and particularly red garden-bete: so called in the present day; and also called $awanodar and sawanodar and banojar :] a certain plant, (S, Msb,) or herb ( baqolapN ), (K,) that is eaten,...
sourceDefinition: [ Bete; and particularly red garden-bete: so called in the present day; and also called $awanodar and sawanodar and banojar :] a certain plant, (S, Msb,) or herb ( baqolapN ), (K,) that is eaten, (S,) well known; (Msb, K;) i. q. jgndr [or Jugunoduro , whence the vulgar name $awanodar , and hence sawanodar ]; so says ISh; i. e. in Pers.; in some of the MSS. jlndr [a mistranscription for JuGunoduro ]; a plant having long leaves, and a root penetrating [ deeply ] into the earth, the leaves of which are tender, and are cooked: (TA:) it clears [ the skin ], acts as a dissolvent, and as a lenitive, and as an aperient, or a deobstruent; exhilarates, and is good for the niqoris [i. e. gout, or podagra, ] and the joints: its expressed juice, when poured upon wine, converts it into vinegar after two hours; and when poured upon vinegar, converts it into wine after four hours; and the expressed juice of its root, used as an errhine, is an antidote to toothache and earache and hemicrania. (K.) [See also Hum~aADN , and kuronubN .] siloqu AlmaA='i and siloqu Albar~i , also, are the names of Two plants. (K.) -A2- Also The he-wolf: (S, Msb, K:) and ↓ siloqapN the she-wolf: (S, K:) or the latter signifies thus; but siloqN is not applied to the he-wolf: (K:) the pl. of siloqapN is suloqaAnN and siloqaAnN : (JM, TA;) or these are pls. of siloqN ; and the pl. of siloqapN is silaqN and siloqN , (K,) or [rather] this last is a coll. gen. n. of which siloqapN is the n. un. (Sb.) Hence the prov., ↓ A^asolaTu mino siloqapK (JK, Meyd) i. e. More clamorous than a she-wolf: or it may mean more overpowering. (Meyd.) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) ↓ siloqapN is applied to a woman as meaning (tropical:) Clamorous; or long-tongued and vehemently clamorous, (S, K, TA,) foul, evil, or lewd; (K, TA;) likened to the she-wolf in respect of her bad qualities: (TA:) pl. suloqaAnN and siloqaAnN . (K.) ― -b3- ↓ siloqapN also signifies A female lizard of the kind called Dab~ , (JK,) or a female locust, (TA,) when she has laid her eggs. (JK, TA.) -A3- Also A water-course, or channel in which water flows, (K, TA,) between two tracts of elevated, or elevated and rugged, ground: or, accord. to As, an even, depressed tract of ground: (TA:) pl. suloqaAnN (K) and A^asolaAqN and A^asaAliqu , which (i. e. the second and third of these pls.) are also said to be pls. of salaqN [q. v.]. (TA.)

definition: [ Natural, or untaught, speech;
sourceDefinition: [ Natural, or untaught, speech; ] speech whereof the desinential syntax is not much attended to, but which is chaste and eloquent in respect of what has been heard, though often tripping, or stumbling, in respect of grammar: (Lth, L, TA:) or the speech which the dweller in the desert utters according to his nature and his proper dialect, though his other speech be nobler and better. (L, TA.) And ↓ saliyqiy~apN [in like manner, the p being affixed to the epithet saliyqiY~N to convert it into a subst.,] signifies The dialect in which the speaker thereof proceeds loosely, or freely, according to his nature, without paying much attention to desinential syntax, and without avoiding incorrectness. (O, TA.) You say, ↓ fulaAnN yatakal~amu biAls~aliyqiy~api , meaning Such a one speaks according to his nature, not from having learned. (S, K.) And ↓ fulaAnN yaqoraA^u biAls~aliyqiy~api Such a one reads, or recites, according to the natural condition in which he has grown up, not as having been taught. (TA.)

definition: of the camel, (S,) of the he-camel and of the she-camel, [The hump;
sourceDefinition: of the camel, (S,) of the he-camel and of the she-camel, [The hump; i. e.] the highest part of the back: (M, TA:) [ in substance, ] it is to the camel like the A^aloyap [here meaning the fat of the tail ] to the sheep: (Msb:) pl. sourceDefinition: [ A whip; ] a certain thing, (S, M,) namely, plaited skin, (Bd in lxxxix. 12,) [or a lash, ] with which one beats, or strikes, (S, M,) well known; (Msb;) i. q. miqoraEapN : (K:) so called because it mixes the flesh with the blood (IDrd, M, K) when a man or a beast is struck with it; (IDrd, TA;) or because its several component parts are mixed together: (Bd, ubi suprà:) pl. [of pauc.] A^asowaATN and [of mult.] siyaATN : (S, M, Msb, K:) the latter originally siwaATN . (TA.) The saying Darabotu zayodFA sawoTFA means Darabotu zayodFA bisawoTK [ I struck Zeyd with a whip ]: (M, Msb: *) or it is one of those rare instances in which a prefixed n. is suppressed; being originally Darabotuhu Darobapa sawoTK [ I struck him a stroke, or lash, of a whip ], meaning DarobapF bisawoTK [ a stroke, or lash, with a whip ]: (M:) or DarobapF waAHidapF bisawoTK [ one stroke, or lash, with a whip ]. (Mgh.) One says also, Darabahu miAy^apa sawoTK [ He struck him a hundred strokes, or lashes, of the whip ]. (S and K in art. sHl .) ― -b2- In the Kur [lxxxix. 12], where it is said, faSab~a Ealayohimo rab~uka sawoTa Ea*aAbK , (S, Msb,) it signifies (tropical:) A portion, or share: (S, K:) or (S, Msb, but in the K, “ and ”) (tropical:) vehemence, or severity; (S, Msb, K;) as being likened to the paining of a whip; (Msb;) because punishment is sometimes with the sawoT ; (S;) and this word is used by the Arabs to denote every kind of punishment when it is extreme, though there be in it no beating: (Fr:) [therefore,] the above-cited saying in the Kur means, (tropical:) [ And thy Lord poured upon them a portion, or a share, or vehemence, or severity, of punishment: or it means,] a mixture; prepared for them, of various punishments: or it is designed to show that what befell them in the present world was, in comparison with what is prepared for them in the final state, like the whip in comparison with the sword: (Bd:) or the meaning is (assumed tropical:) a kind of punishment. (Jel.) [Agreeably with this last explanation, it is said that] the phrase humaA yataEaATayaAni sawoTFA waAHidFA means (tropical:) They two are agreed upon one mode: (A:) or the meaning is (tropical:) [ they two enter, or plunge, into; or venture boldly upon, and do; ] one thing, or affair; (S, and K; but wanting in one copy of the former; and in the latter, in the place of hmA is put mA ;) i. e., one sort [ of thing or affair ]. definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) and bihimo , (S, Msb, K,) and fiyhimo , (TA,) and $agabahumo , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) and bihimo , (S, Msb, K,) and fiyhimo , (TA,) and $agabahumo , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (A, Msb, K,) inf. n. $agobN , (S, * A, * K, * TA,) with which $agabN is syn., (A, K,) a syn. sometimes used, (A,) or this latter is not allowable, (S, K,) as some say, (K,) and is ascribed by IAth to the vulgar, and said by El-Hareeree in the “ Durrat el-Ghowwás ” to be a mistake, but IB says in the commentaries on the “ Durrah ” that it is correct, mentioned by IDrd, and MF says that it is mentioned by IJ, as well as by Z in the A; (TA;) and one says also $agiba Elyhm , [and it seems to be implied that one says likewise $agiba bhm , and $agibahumo ,] aor. as above, (S, K,) inf. n. $agabN ; (S, TA;) but this latter form of the verb, with kesr, is of weak authority; (S, * TA;) [whence it seems that $agabN is correct as inf. n. of $agiba , but disallowed by some who knew not this form of the verb;] He excited, or stirred up, (S, A, Msb, K, TA,) [ against them, or] among them, (Msb,) evil, or mischief, (S, A, Msb, K, TA,) and conflict, faction, sedition, or discord, and contention, or altercation, and opposition: (TA:) and [it is said that] ta$ogiybN is like $agobN signifying the exciting, or stirring up, evil, &c.; (K, TA;) [but] ↓ $g~b , inf. n. ta$ogiybN , signifies he excited, or stirred up, evil, &c., much, or often. (O.) A trad. mentioned in [the first paragraph of] art. $Eb is quoted by IAth thus: maA h`*ihi AlfotoyaA Al~atiY $agabato fiY Aln~aAsi [ What is this judicial decision which has excited evil, &c., among the people? ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [See also $agobN below.] ― -b3- The saying of 'Amr Ibn-Kameeäh, faA_ino ta$ogibiY faAl$~agobu min~iY sajiy~apN means (tropical:) And if thou oppose, or contravene, me, and do that which is not agreeable to me, [know that opposition, &c., is a natural disposition of mine; EalaY~a being understood after t$gbY , as appears from what here follows.] (TA. [See also 3, and 6.]) Accord. to El-Báhilee, *aAtu $agobK [applied to a she-ass] means (tropical:) Having the quality of opposing or contravening [the male]: so in the saying of El-'Ajjáj, kaA^an~a taHotiY *aAta $agobK samoHajaA qawodaA='a laA taHomilu A_il~aA muxodajaA (tropical:) [ As though beneath me were a she-ass] such as opposes or contravenes [the male], long-bodied, long-necked, [ that would not bear in her womb aught save a fœtus imperfectly formed; ] meaning, laA tuw^aAtibhi wata$ogabu Ealayohi [i. e. that she (the beast that he was riding) would not comply with his desire, and was contravening him ]. (TA.) [Accord. to J,] *aAtu $agobK waDigonK , [in the TA wSgb , and so in a copy of the A, an evident mistranscription,] applied to a she-ass that has not conceived during a year or two years or some years, means (tropical:) Refractory, or incompliant, to the strong, or bulky, male. (S: there expl. by the words A_i*aA waHimato waA@sotaSoEabato EalaY AljaA^obi [which have been misunderstood by Golius, and rendered by him, and by Freytag after him, as applied to a woman, and meaning respuens maris congressum, aut picâ laborans ].) ― -b4- And $agaba signifies also (assumed tropical:) He declined, or deviated, from the right way or course: (Sh, TA:) or $agaba Eani AlT~ariyqi , aor. , (K,) inf. n. $agbN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He declined, or deviated, from the road or way. (K.)

AirotaAba ; (Msb;) and ↓ t$k~k signifies the same. (S, K.) ― -b4- $ak~a EalaY~a AlA^amoru means $aq~a [i. e. The case, or affair, was difficult, hard, distressing, &c., to me ]: (O, TA:) or, as some say, [ was such that ] I doubted ( $akakotu ) respecting it. (TA.) -A2- $ak~a said of a camel, (IAar, S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) He limped, or halted; or had a slight lameness, (IAar, S, TA,) of his hind leg: (IAar, TA:) or his arm stuck to his side, (K, TA,) and he had a slight lameness in consequence thereof: (TA:) and ↓ A$tk~ , likewise said of a camel, he had a slight lameness; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA;) like $ak~a . (Ibn-'Abbád, O.) ― -b2- $ak~N also signifies The cleaving or sticking [of a thing to another thing]. (S, O, TA.) So in a verse of Aboo-Dahbal El-Jumahee cited voce yalabN . (S.) And one says, $ak~ati Alr~aHimu The relationship was, or became, closely united. (O, TA. [See raHimN $aAk~apN , voce $aAk~N .]) ― -b3- $ak~a fiY Als~ilaAHi , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He put on [or around him, ] or attired himself with, the arms, or weapons, completely, not leaving any of them; (TA;) [ as though ] he entered amid them. (K, TA.) -A3- $akakotuhu biAlr~umoHi , (S, O, Msb, in the K $ak~ahu ,) and biAls~ahomi , and the like, aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (Msb, TA,) I pierced, or transpierced, him, or it, ( TaEanotuhu , Msb, or xazaqotuhu , O, and in like manner in the TA, but in my copies of the S xaraqotuhu [meaning I made a hole in him, or it ], and thus in one place in the TA, and AinotaZamotuhu , S O, and in like manner in the K,) with the spear, (S, O, Msb, K,) and with the arrow, &c.: (TA:) but IDrd says that, accord. to some, $ak~N is only by the conjoining two things with an arrow or a spear: (O, TA:) [thus,] fa$ak~a rijolahu maEa rikaAbihi means And he clave and transpierced his leg, or foot, together with his stirrup. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] $akakotu A_ilayohi AlbilaAda I traversed, or crossed, or cut through, the countries, or districts, to him. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And $uk~a Ealayih Alv~awobu The garment was put [or drawn ] together upon him, and fastened with a thorn or a wooden pin: or was let down, or made to hang down, upon him. (TA.) ― -b4- $ak~uwA buyuwtahumo They placed their tents in one row, or series, (O, Msb, K,) in one regular order, (T, TA,) near together. (Msb.) ― -b5- Hence; $ak~uwA AlA^aroHaAma They made the relationships to be closely connected. (Msb.) And $uk~a He was made, or asserted, to be connected with the lineage of another. (IAar, O.) ― -b6- And $akakotuhu said of anything means I drew and joined, or adjoined, it [to another thing]. (Msb.) [And I infixed it in, or thrust it into, another thing.] ― -b7- maA $ak~a kafiY xaliyluhaA , [or, more probably, mA $uk~a ,] a phrase in a verse of El-Farezdak,] in which it forms an apodosis,] means maA qaArana [i. e., app., Its friend ( the sword, or the spear, both of which are meanings of Alxaliyl ,) would not be conjoined (or grasped ) with my hand ]. (TA.) ― -b8- $ak~a Alv~awoba He (the sewer) made the stitch-holes far apart [ in sewing the garment, or piece of cloth ]. (O, TA.) [Thus the verb has two contr. meanings.] -A4- $akikotu A_ilayohi , with kesr, and $akikotuhu , (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, and so in the K accord. to the TA, as also in the TK, in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K $akakotuhu and Alyh ,) I inclined to him, or it; or trusted to, or relied upon, him, or it, so as to be, or become, easy, or quiet, in mind; or leaned, rested, or relied, upon him, or it; syn. rakanotu . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)

definition: [used as a subst.
sourceDefinition: [used as a subst.] signifies Doubt; (Msb; [see 1;]) or the contr. of yaqiynN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) by which explanation is meant a wavering or vacillation in opinion between two things, whether they be equal [ in probability ] or such that one of them outweighs [ therein ] the other; or, as the expositors explain its meaning in the Kur x. 94, uncertainty: (Msb:) or a wavering or vacillation in opinion, between two inconsistent things, without making either of them to outweigh the other in the estimation of him who conceives the $ak~ : or, as some say, a pausing, or hesitation, between two extremes that are equal [ in probability ], without the mind's inclining to either of them: when one of them is made to outweigh, without the other's being rejected, it is Zan~N : (KT:) accord. to Er-Rághib, it is the alternation, or confusedness, of two inconsistent things, in the judgment of a man, and their being equal: this is sometimes because of there being two indications, equal in his judgment, of the two inconsistent things; or of there being no indication thereof: and sometimes it relates to the question whether a thing be, or be not; and sometimes, to the question of what kind it is; and sometimes, to some of its qualities; and sometimes, to the accident that is the cause of its being: it is a species of jahol ; but is more special than this; for jhl is sometimes the utter nonexistence of knowledge of the two inconsistent things; so that every $k~ is jhl , but every jhl is not $k~ : (TA:) accord. to some, the primary meaning is a state of commotion, or disturbance, of the heart and mind: (Msb:) pl. $ukuwkN . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence, yawomu Al$~aki The day of which one doubts whether it be the last of one month or the first of the next month: and generally, whether it be the last of Shaabán or the first of Ramadán; and to fast on this day is forbidden.] -A2- Also A small crack in a bone. (K.) ― -b2- And A seam, or line of sewing, of a garment. (L in art. SwH .) ― -b3- [And accord. to Freytag, A coat of mail composed of narrow rings: but he names no authority for this.] -A3- And [ Arsenic; ] a certain medicament, that destroys rats; brought from Khurásán, from the mines of silver; (K, TA;) of two kinds, (TA,) white and yellow; (K, TA;) now known by the name of sam~u AlfaA^ori [ ratsbane ]. (TA.)
