definition: He adorned himself: (K:) or t$w~ft she (a woman, IDrd, O, or a girl, or young woman, S) adorned herself.
sourceDefinition: He adorned himself: (K:) or t$w~ft she (a woman, IDrd, O, or a girl, or young woman, S) adorned herself. (IDrd, S, O.) One says of a woman divorced by a sentence that admits of her returning, tuta$aw~afu lizawojihaA i. e. She adorns herself for her husband, by making her face clear, and polishing her cheeks; from 1 in the first of the senses assigned to it above. (Mgh.) -A2- t$w~ft AlA^awoEaAlu The mountain-goats ascended upon the tops of the mountains, (Lth, O, Msb,) and looked down, (Lth, O,) to see the plain country and its freedom from those whom they feared, in order that they might repair to the water and the pasturage. (Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, t$w~f lika*aA He (a man) raised, or stretched and raised, his eyes, or sight, towards such a thing: and hence the verb became used to denote hope, or expectation, and desire, or seeking. (Msb.) And t$w~f mina Als~aToHi He stretched himself up, and looked, and overlooked, or looked down, from the house-top. (K.) One says, Aln~isaA='u yata$aw~afona mina Als~uTowHi The women look, [or look down, ] stretching themselves up, from the house-tops. (S, O.) [See also 8.] And one says also, t$w~f A_ilaY Al$Yo'i , (S,) or AlY Alxayori , (O, K,) or AlY Alxabari , (CK,) He looked for [ the thing, or good, or the news or tidings ], (S, O, K,) &c. (TA.) ― -b3- And t$w~f Al$~aYo'u The thing rose, or became high or elevated; as also ↓ A$Af . (TA.)

[of pauc.] A^aSoHunN (Msb, * TA) and [of mult.] SiHaAnN (TA) [and app., agreeably with modern usage, SuHuwnN ]. ― -b2- And [hence,] A [ kind of ] cymbal; (PS;) a small brazen basin, ( TusayotN , [dim. of TasotN ,]) one of what are termed SaHonaAni , (S,) this meaning two little brazen basins, ( TusayotaAni SagiyrataAni , K,) which are struck together. (S. K.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) The interior of the solid hoof; (K, TA;) also called skrjp [i. e. sukur~ujap or sukur~ajap ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) The interior of the ear: or the maHaArap [i. e. concha ] thereof. (TA.) And SaHonaA AlA^u*unayoni [thus accord. to the TA and my MS. copy of the K, in the CK SaHonA'u ,] (assumed tropical:) The resting-place ( musotaqar~ ) of the interior of each of the ears; (K;) meaning the place of hearing [or meatus auditorius ] of the resting-place of the interior of each of the two ears of the horse: pl. A^aSoHaAnN . (TA.) ― -b5- Also The middle of a house; (S, K;) meaning the saAHap [i. e. court ] of the middle of a house [and of a mosque &c.]: (TA:) [and also a hall: for] it is thus called whether without, or with, a roof. (Kull, voce bayotN .) And The saAHap [or spacious vacant part ] of the middle of a desert; and of an elevated and plain, or hard and elevated, tract; and of a wide space of low, or depressed, ground: pl. SuHuwnN , the only pl. form. (TA.) A wide part of a desert: so in the saying, sironaA fiY SaHoni AlfalaApi [ We journeyed in the wide part of the desert ]. (Msb.) And A level, or plain, tract of ground. (TA.) And An acclivity ( sanad ) of a valley, in which is some elevation above [ other ] elevated ground, as though supported [ by the latter ]; and in like manner, of a mountain, and of a hill such as is termed A^akamap ; the SuHuwn of the ground being the dufuwf [i. e. banks, or acclivities, ] thereof: it is bare, and such as flows [ with rain ]; and is not thus called unless bare of everything, and even: and it means also an even tract of ground like the area of the place in which dates are put to dry. (TA.) ― -b6- [Hence,] one says, jaraY Ald~amoEu EalaY SaHonaYo wajonatayohi (tropical:) [ The tears ran upon the middle of each of his cheek-balls ]. (TA.) -A2- Also A gift. (TA. (TA.)

definition: A possessor of a Siromap of camels.

sourceDefinition: A she-camel whose [ fore or kind ] pair of teats have been cut off, (S, M, K,) in order that the A_iHoliyl [or orifice through which the milk passes forth from the udder of each teat] may dry up and the milk not issue, for the purpose of giving greater strength to her: and (AA used to say, S) this is sometimes in consequence of the stoppage of the milk, something having happened to the udder, for which it is cauterized, and her milk stops, (S, K,) no milk ever issuing from the udder: (S:) see also SaromaA='u , voce A^aSoramu : or muSar~amapu AlA^aTobaA='i means a she-camel treated ( Euwlijato ) so that her milk has stopped. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. SalafN , The clouds had in them no water: (M:) or Salifati Als~aHaAbapu the cloud had little water. (A, TA. [It is implied in the TA that this is tropical; but I doubt its being so.]) See also its part. n., SalifN . ― -b2- Salifa said of a man's Harov [or seed-produce], It did not increase, or multiply, or become plentiful or abundant. (TA.) ― -b3- SalafN as a quality of TaEaAm [or wheat] signifies Its having little increase ( nuzol , S, or nazal , L, or namaA=' and barakap , K) and little goodness. (L, TA: said in the latter to be tropical.) ― -b4- [Hence, app., or from the verb as used in the sense expl. in the next sentence below,] mano yabogi , fiY Ald~iyni yaSolafo , (S, M, Meyd, &c.,) a prov., (S, Meyd, O, K,) relating to the holding fast to religion, (S,) or used in urging to the mixing in social intercourse with the holding fast to religion, (O, K,) or, accord. to IAth, a trad., (TA,) i. e., accord. to As, He who exceeds the right bounds in religion (Meyd) will not be in favour with men, or beloved by them; (S, Meyd;) or will have little increase therein: (M:) or he who finds fault with men in respect of religion, (O, K,) and regards it as an excellence [ that he possesses ] above them, will have little goodness in their estimation, and (O) will not be in favour with them, or beloved by them: (O, K:) or the meaning is, he who seeks worldly good by means of religion, his share of the former will be little: (Meyd:) or he who seeks, in respect of religion, more than he has had revealed to him, his share will be little. (IAth.) ― -b5- Salifato , (S, M, O,) aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. SalafN , said of a woman, means She was not in favour with, or was not beloved by, (S, M, O, K, *) her husband, (S, O, K,) or him by whom she was supported; (M;) and was hated by him. (S, O.) ― -b6- SalafN , (O, K,) in a man and in a woman, (O,) signifies also The saying that which one's companion dislikes, or hates. (O, K.) ― -b7- And, (O, K,) likewise in a man and in a woman, (O,) (assumed tropical:) The commending, or praising, oneself for, or the boasting of, or glorying in, that which one does not possess: (O, K:) or, (K,) as Kh asserts, (S, O,) the overpassing the due limits in AlZ~arof [here meaning elegance of mind, manners, address, speech, person, attire, and the like ], (S, M, O, K,) and in excellence in knowledge or courage or other qualities, (TA,) and arrogating to oneself more than is due, through pride: (S, O, K:) but some say that this is post-classical: (M, TA:) [see an ex. voce A=fapN , in art. Awf ; mentioned here in the TA as occurring in a trad.:] one says, of a man, Salifa , (M, MA,) inf. n. SalafN , (M,) meaning (assumed tropical:) He commended, or praised, himself [&c.]; (MA;) and ↓ tSl~f , (S, MA, O,) meaning the same; (MA;) or this latter means takal~afa AlS~alafa , (K, TA,) i. e. [ he affected the overpassing of the due limits in AlZ~arof (meaning as expl. above); or he took upon himself as a task ] the arrogating to himself more than was due, through pride: (TA:) [you say, tSl~f bimaA layosa Einodahu (assumed tropical:) He commended, or praised, himself for, or he boasted of, or gloried in, that which he did not possess: ] the epithet from the former verb is ↓ SalifN , (AZ, S, M, O, K,) applied to a man, (AZ, S, M, O,) and SalifapN applied to a woman; (M;) and the pl. of SalifN is SalaAfaY (AZ, M, K) and SulafaA='u and Salifuwna : (AZ, O, K:) it is said to be from SalifN applied to a vessel, accord. to IAar as meaning “ that takes little water; ” but rather, as others say, as meaning “ thick and heavy: ” the vulgar misapply it [app. by using it in the sense assigned to it by IAar]. (TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph.

definition: The side ( EuroD [in one of my copies of the S EaroD , and in the other copy Eirq ,]) of the neck;
sourceDefinition: The side ( EuroD [in one of my copies of the S EaroD , and in the other copy Eirq ,]) of the neck; the two being called SaliyfaAni ; (S, O, K;) [i. e.] AlS~aliyfaAni signifies the two sides of the neck ( jaAnibaA AlEunuqi ): or this signifies what are between the liyt [or part beneath the earring ] and the qaSarap [or base of the neck, on the two sides ]: (M:) or the two heads of the vertebra that is next to the head, in the two sides of the neck. (AZ, O, * K, * TA.) In this last explanation, in the copies of the K, rA^s is put for rA^sA . (TA. [And in some copies of the K, $iq~ayohimaA is there erroneously put for $iq~ayohaA , which, as is said in the TA, refers to the neck.]) A^axa*a biSaliyfihi and ↓ biSaliyfatihi mean, accord. to As, He took hold of the back of his neck: (O, TA:) and one says also, ↓ A^axa*ahu biSaliyfatihi meaning He took him, or it, altogether. (TA. [But I think it not improbable that ↓ biSaliyfatihi in these two instances may be a mistranscription for biSaliyfayohi .]) ― -b2- AlS~aliyfaAni signifies also Two staves, or pieces of wood, which are placed across [ horizontally ] upon the [ camel's saddle called ] gabiyT , by means of which the maHaAmil [pl. of maHomilN , q. v.,] are bound. (S, O, K.) And (TA) SaliyfaA AlA_ikaAfi signifies The two [ similar ] pieces of wood that are bound upon the upper part of the [ saddle called ] A_ikaAf . (M, TA.) -A2- See also SalifN , latter half.

definition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ SamagN , (K,) the latter mentioned by ISd on the authority of AHn, (TA,) [ Gum;
sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ SamagN , (K,) the latter mentioned by ISd on the authority of AHn, (TA,) [ Gum; i. e.] the fluid that exudes from the trees called EiDaAh and the like of these: (Msb:) it is of many sorts: (S, O:) that which is called AlS~amogu AlEarabiY~u is the Samog of the TaloH , (S, O, Msb,) which is said to be the same [tree] that is called A^um~u gayolaAna : (Msb:) or the mucilage ( giraA=' ) of the [ tree called ] qaraZ [and more commonly sanoT , i. e. the mimosa Nilotica, also called acacia Nilotica ]; and this is what is called AlS~amogu AlEarabiY~u ; not the Samog of the TaloH ; J [and others] having erred [in asserting it to be this]: [but] every tree also has Samog : (K: [this last assertion, however, is questionable; for Samog seems to signify properly gum, or juice that exudes from certain trees and concretes: ]) the n. un., (Msb, TA,) or term applied to a portion thereof, (S, O,) is SamogapN (S, O, Msb, TA) and SamagapN : (TA:) and the pl. is SumuwgN : (S, O, Msb, K:) among Sumuwg [i. e. sorts of Samog ], the muqol [q. v.] is said to be included; but this is not known. (AHn, TA.) It is said in a prov., tarakotuhu EalaY mivoli maqorifi AlS~amogapi [ I left him in a condition like that of the place where the piece of gum has been pared off ]: this is when one has left a person nothing; for the Smgp is plucked off from its tree until there remains not upon it what would retain one's life: (S, O:) or, as some relate it, EalaY mivoli maqolaEi AlS~amogapi [ in a condition like that of the place where the piece of gum has been plucked off ]; (O, and so Meyd;) meaning, without anything remaining to him; because, when the gum is plucked off, there remains not any trace of it. (Meyd.) And in a trad. of El-Hajjáj occurs the saying, laA^aqolaEan~aka qaloEa AlS~amogapi [ I will assuredly pluck thee away with the plucking away of the piece of gum ]; meaning I will assuredly extirpate thee. (TA.) [― -b2- Also Resin; see EilokN .]

SiyaAHN and SayoHapN (S, A, * O, Msb, K *) and SayoHN and SuyaAHN and SayaHaAnN , (S, O, K, *) He raised his voice, voiced, called or called out, cried or cried out: (S, A, O, Msb, K:) or did so vehemently, cried aloud, uttered a loud cry or crying, shouted, exclaimed, or vociferated: (T, S, * A, * O, * Msb, * TA:) or did so with his utmost force or power; (K, TA;) as also ↓ Sy~H : (A, * TA:) it is said of a man, and of other things: (TA:) or of anything: (T, TA:) originally, of an animal, and often of a bird of the crow-kind, but rarely of a bird unrestrictedly, and sometimes of a spear as being likened to an animal. (Ham p. 187.) One says, SaAHa SayoHapF $adiydapF [ He called, or cried, &c., with a vehement calling or crying &c., or with a vehement call or cry &c.]. (A.) And SAj bihi He called or cried, or called out or cried out, to it [or to him ]. (Msb.) And SiHo liY bifulaAnK Call thou to me such a one. (A, TA.) And bihi ↓ SaAyaHa and SaAyaHahu , (A, TA,) and ↓ Say~aHa bihi and Say~aHahu , (A,) He called, hailed, or summoned, him; called out, cried out, or shouted, to him. (K.) ― -b3- One says also, laqiytuhu qabola kul~i SayoHK wanaforK I met him before every calling, or crying, and dispersing; meaning (assumed tropical:) I met him before daybreak: (S, TA:) so in the Proverbs of Meyd. (TA.) Or A^atayotuhu qabola SayoHK wanaforK (tropical:) I came to him before everything. (A.) And gaDiba mino gayori SayoHK walaA naforK (tropical:) He was angry for neither little nor much: (ISk, S, K:) or for nothing. (A.) ― -b4- And SaAHati Al$~ajarapu , (A, Msb,) or Aln~axolapu , (K,) (tropical:) The tree, (A, Msb,) or the palm-tree, (K,) became tall. (A, Msb, K.) And SAH AlEunoquwdu (tropical:) The raceme came forth completely from its envelope, and became long, and in a fresh and tender state. (K.) And SAH AlkaAfuwru (tropical:) [app. meaning The spathe of the palm-tree put forth its spadix, or its raceme, to its full length ]. (A.)

definition: The part between the armpit and the ka$oH [or flank ];
sourceDefinition: The part between the armpit and the ka$oH [or flank ]; (S, K, TA;) or the HiDon [which generally means as above]; (A'Obeyd, TA;) [or] the part, of the side, between the armpit and the HiDon [which is here evidently used as syn. with ka$oH ]: (S:) or the armpit [itself]: so says Ibn-El-Faraj: like DiborN : (TA in art Dbr :) or the armpit and the part next to it: or the uppermost part of the side: or the part beneath the ka$oH [or flank ] and beneath the armpit: or the part between the xaASirap [or flank ] and the head [or crest ] of the hip. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) A side of a road: one says, A^axa*a fiY DibonK mina AlT~ariyqi (assumed tropical:) He took a side of the road: pl. A^aDobAnN . (TA.) ― -b3- And huwa fiY Diboni fulaAnK means (assumed tropical:) He is in the quarter, or protection, of such a one; as also ↓ fY Dibonatihi . (TA.) ― -b4- [The pl.] A^aDobaAnN signifies also (tropical:) The narrow places ( maDaAyiq ) of the jamal [an evident mistranscription for jabal i. e. mountain]. (TA.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) Places abounding with beasts of prey: (K, TA:) sing. DibonN . (TA.) ― -b6- And AlD~ibonu signifies (assumed tropical:) That [ place, or ground, ] which renders people impotent, or helpless, to dig it. (K.)

definition: A xubozap , (S, K, TA,) [i.
sourceDefinition: A xubozap , (S, K, TA,) [i. e. a cake of bread, or lump of dough, ] baked in hot ashes in a hollow in the ground; what people [now] call a mal~ap ; but this is the name of the hollow itself: what is baked in this is [properly called] the Tulomap and xubozap and maliyl : (S, TA:) pl. TulamN . (L, TA.) It is said in a prov., A_in~a duwna AlT~alomapi xaroTa qataAdi huwobara (Meyd, TA) [i. e. Before the attainment of the cake of bread baked in hot ashes is the stripping of the leaves, by grasping each branch and drawing the hand down it, of the tragacanth of Howbar ]: the Tulomap is the cake of bread that is put in hot ashes; and Howbar is a place abounding with the tragacanth: the prov. is applied in relation to a thing that is unattainable. (Meyd.)

rawSourceText: A xubozap , (S, K, TA,) [i. e. a cake of bread, or lump of dough, ] baked in hot ashes in a hollow in the ground; what people [now] call a mal~ap ; but this is the name of the hollow itself: what is baked in this is [properly called] the Tulomap and xubozap and maliyl : (S, TA:) pl. TulamN . (L, TA.) It is said in a prov., A_in~a duwna AlT~alomapi xaroTa qataAdi huwobara (Meyd, TA) [i. e. Before the attainment of the cake of bread baked in hot ashes is the stripping of the leaves, by grasping each branch and drawing the hand down it, of the tragacanth of Howbar ]: the Tulomap is the cake of bread that is put in hot ashes; and Howbar is a place abounding with the tragacanth: the prov. is applied in relation to a thing that is unattainable. (Meyd.)

sourceDefinition: A bundle of reeds or canes, (S, M, K,) or (so accord. to the Msb, but in the TA “ and ”) of firewood: (Msb, TA:) thought by IDrd to be not genuine Arabic: and pronounced by the vulgar Tin~ , with kesr: (TA:) n. un. with p ; (K;) [i. e.] ↓ Tun~apN signifies a single reed or cane [or piece of firewood ] of a bundle: (S:) and the pl. is A^aTonaAnN : (Msb:) [or,] accord. to AHn, a Tun~ of reeds or canes, and of fresh branches, is a wryqp [app. meaning a leafy bundle ] put together and bound round, and having flowers, or blossoms, and plucked fruits put in the interior thereof. (TA.) ― -b2- And A thing that is put between the two half-loads that are upon the sides of a beast. (AHeyth, K.) ― -b3- And The stature [of a man]: or, accord. to IAar, (TA,) the body of a man and of any animal: pl. A^aTonaAnN and TinaAnN : (K, TA:) whence, he says, the saying, fulaAnN laA yaquwmu biTun~i nafosihi fakayofa bagayorihi [ Such a one will not rise with his own body: how then with another? ]: but accord. to IDrd, this is a saying of the vulgar; and he does not think it to be genuine Arabic. (TA.) -A2- See also Tan~N .

definition: , (S, Msb, *) or AlS~aHiyfapa , (K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, *) or AlS~aHiyfapa , (K,) aor. yaTowiY , (Msb, K,) inf. n. TaY~N , (S, Msb,) [ He folded, folded up, or folded together, and he rolled up, the thing, such as a garment, or piece of cloth, or the like, or the written piece of paper: ] TawaY AlS~aHiyfapa meaning the contr. of na$arahaA . (TA.) And one says also, TawaY Alv~awoba , inf. n. Tiy~apN , with kesr, and TiyapN , like EidapN , this latter on the authority of Lh, and extr., [meaning He folded, &c., the garment, or piece of cloth: ] and the phrase SaHiyfapN jaAfiyapu AlT~iyapi has been mentioned as meaning AlT~aY~i [i. e. A written piece of paper thick, or rude, in respect of the folding, &c.]. (TA.) [And Tawayotu Als~iqaA='a EalaY bululatihi , and bulalatihi , or balalatihi , I folded the skin while it was moist: whence the phrases Tawayotu fulaAnFA EalaY bululatihi , and bulalatihi , &c., and TawaAhu EalaY bilaAlihi , and buluwlihi , expl. voce balalN ; and a similar phrase in a verse cited voce *ariba , q. v.: see also a similar phrase in art. dml , conj. 3: and see TawiYa .] ― -b2- [Hence, TawaY signifies also (assumed tropical:) He, or it, made a thing compact, as though folded; or round, like a scroll.] One says, TuwiYa jisomuhu Tay~FA Hat~aY A@kotanaza laHomuhu (assumed tropical:) [ His body was, or became, compacted, or rounded, so that his, or its, flesh was firm, or hard ]. (Lh, TA in art. dmlj .) And saAqN Hasanapu AlT~aY~i (assumed tropical:) [ A shank goodly in respect of the compacture, or rounding; well compacted, well rounded, or well turned ]. (K in art. jdl , &c.) And [hence likewise,] TawaAhu means also (assumed tropical:) It rendered him lean, lank, light of flesh, slender, or lank in the belly. (L in art. msd .) One says, TawaAhu Als~ayoru (assumed tropical:) Journeying, or travel, rendered him lean, or emaciated him. (TA.) ― -b3- TawaY Eunuqahu wanaAma A=minFA is said of a gazelle [as meaning He folded, or bent, his neck, and slept free from fear ]. (TA.) ― -b4- TawaY ka$oHahu [lit. He folded, or bent, his flank, ] means (tropical:) he turned away his love, or affection: (S, TA:) or, as in the M, (tropical:) he withdrew his countenance: and the following ex. is cited: waSaAHibK qado TawaY ka$oHFA faqulotu lahu h`*aA Eanoka yaTowiyniY ↓ A_in~a A@noTiwaA='aka (tropical:) [ Many a companion has withdrawn countenance, and I have said to him, Verily this thy withdrawing withdraws me from thee ]: (TA:) or TawaY ka$oHahu Ean~iY means (tropical:) he turned away from me, forsaking, or abandoning. (K, TA. [See also art. k$H .]) ― -b5- And TawaY ka$oHahu EalaY A^amorK (tropical:) He concealed an affair, or a case: (K, TA:) or, as in the M, (assumed tropical:) he determined, or resolved, upon an affair: (TA:) or, as in the L, and other lexicons, (assumed tropical:) he persevered in an affair. (TA in art. k$H .) ― -b6- And TawaY , [for TawaY A^aHo$aA='ahu ,] (S, K,) aor. yaTowiY , inf. n. TaY~N , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He suffered hunger intentionally, or purposely. (S, K. [See also TawiYa .]) ― -b7- And TawaY Ean~iY AlHadiyva , (K, * TA,) and Als~ir~a , (TA,) (tropical:) He concealed from me the story, (K, * TA,) and the secret. (TA.) One says, AiTowi h`*aA AlHadiyva (tropical:) Conceal thou this story. (TA.) ― -b8- And TawaY HadiyvFA A_ilaY HadiyvK (assumed tropical:) He concealed in his mind a story and passed on from it to another story; like as is said of the traveller in the sentence next following: and similar to this is the phrase TaY~u AlS~awomi (assumed tropical:) [ the passing on from the fasting to the next fasting]. (TA.) One says of the traveller, yaTowiY manozilFA A_ilaY manozilK falaA yanozilu (assumed tropical:) [ He passes on from one place of alighting to another so that he does not alight ]. (TA.) And TawaY AlmakaAna A_ilaY AlmakaAni (assumed tropical:) He passed on from the place to the place. (TA.) And TawaY AlbilaAda , (K, Ta,) inf. n. TaY~N , (TA,) (tropical:) He traversed the countries, (K, TA,) country after country. (TA.) ― -b9- TawaY Alqawoma means (assumed tropical:) He came to the people, or party: or he passed by them: (IAar, K, TA:) or he sat by them, or at their place of abode. (K, TA.) ― -b10- TawaY A@ll~`hu AlbuEoda lanaA , accord. to the K, means (tropical:) May God contract (lit. make near ) the distance to us: but accord. to the T, AlbaEiyda [i. e., make near the remote ]. (TA.) ― -b11- AlT~aY~u also denotes the passing away of life: [or rather the making life to pass away:] one says, TawaY A@ll~`hu Eumuraha (assumed tropical:) [ God made, or may God make, his life to pass away ]: and a poet says, Tawatoka xuTuwbu dahorika baEoda na$orK (assumed tropical:) [ Thy misfortunes have exanimated thee after vivifying, or reviving ]: TuwiYa fulaAnN wahuwa mano$uwrN (tropical:) [ Such a one has been exanimated but he is revived ] is said of a person when [he has died and] a good reputation of him remains, or a good memorial. (TA.) [It is also implied in the TA that, in accordance with this usage of the verb, TawaAhu may be rendered (assumed tropical:) He caused it to pass away, or come to nought or to an end; destroyed it; or annihilated it: (see the pass. part. n.:) and, accord. to Bd, yawoma naTowiY A@ls~amaA='a , in the Kur xxi. 104, may mean On the day when we shall efface the heaven: but this phrase is better rendered on the day when we shall fold, or roll up, the heaven. ] ― -b12- One says also, TawaY Algazola EalaY AlmiTowaY [ He wound the spun thread upon the winder ]. (TA.) ― -b13- And TawaY Alr~akiy~apa , (TA,) or Albiy^ora , (Msb,) inf. n. TaY~N , He cased the well with stones, and with baked bricks: and in like manner, TawaY All~abina fiY AlbinaA='i [ He cased the bricks, or crude bricks, in the building ]. (TA.) -A2- TawiYa Als~iqaA='u , [aor. yaTowaY ,] inf. n. TawFY , The skin was folded having in it moisture, or some remains of milk, in consequence of which it became altered, and stinking, and dissundered by putrefaction. (TA. [See also the third sentence of this paragraph.]) ― -b2- And TawiYa , aor. yaTowaY , inf. n. TawFY (S, K) and TiwFY also, on the authority of Sb, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was hungry; (S, K; *) as also ↓ A^aTowaY . (K. [See also TawaY , above.]) ― -b3- And Tawiyato Tiy~atuhu The place to which, or towards which, he would repair, or betake himself, was, or became, remote. (Lh, TA.)

definition: [originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: [originally an inf. n., of TawaY , q. v.,] and ↓ TiY~N and ↓ TiwaY , [said in one place in the TA to be like A_ilaY , but I think that this is only said to show that its first vowel is kesr and the second fet-h, and that it is correctly TiwFY , for there is no reason for its being imperfectly decl.,] accord. to the M, are sings. of A^aTowaA='N , which it explains as signifying The lines, or streaks, and creases, of the folding of a garment, or piece of cloth, and of a written piece of paper, and of the belly, and of fat, and of the guts, and of a serpent, and of other things; and it is said in the T and K that ↓ maTaAwK , of which the sing. is ↓ maTowFY , signifies the A^aTowaA=' of the serpent, and of the guts, and of fat, and of the belly, and of a garment, or piece of cloth: (TA:) one says, A^amaEaAy^ihaA ↓ maA baqiyato fiY maTaAwiY vamiylapN [ There remained not in the creases of her, or their, guts any relic of food ]: (A, TA:) and Ald~iroEi ↓ maTaAwiY signifies the creases of the coat of mail when it is drawn together, or contracted. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, EalaY jabiynihaA A^aTowaA='u Aln~ajomi i. e. TaraAy^iquhu [app. meaning Upon her forehead (for so jabiyn sometimes signifies) are the wrinkles indicative of the time for the payment of the debt of nature ]. (TA.) The A^aTowaA=' in the she-camel are The TaraAy^iq [i. e. lines, or streaks, or perhaps creases, or wrinkles, ] of the fat (S, K, TA) of the hump: (K, TA:) [or the creases, or wrinkles, one above another, of the side and of the hump; for] Lth says, TaraAy^iqu janobihaA wasanaAmhaA TaY~N fawoqa TaY~K [ the creases, or wrinkles, of her side and of her hump are, or consist of, TaY~ above TaY~ ]. (TA.) And AHn says that A^aTowaA='N signifies The bending [or rather he should have said, or perhaps he did say, the places of bending ] in the tail of the locust, [ which are ] like Euqad [or articulations ]: and the pl. [of mult.] is ↓ TiwaY [said to be like A_ilaY , but I think that it is correctly TiwFY , as I have observed above]. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also, wajadotu fiY TaY~i AlkitaAbi ka*aA [lit. I found within the folding of the writing, or letter, such a thing; meaning, infolded, or enclosed, or included, in it; or among the contents, or implications, of it ]: and fiY A^aTowaA='i Alkutubi and ↓ maTaAwiyhaA [lit. within the folds, or places of folding, of the writings, or letters ]. (A, TA.) And Algil~u fiY TaY~i qalobihi (tropical:) [ Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite, is conceived, as though it were infolded, in his heart ]. (TA. [See 7.]) And A^adorajaniY fiY TaY~i Aln~isoyaAni (tropical:) [ He, or it, infolded me within the folding of oblivion ]. (TA.) ― -b3- See also TawFY . ― -b4- And see TawiY~N . ― -b5- [Also A casing of stones or of baked bricks; and particularly such a casing of a well; an inf. n. used as a subst. properly so called; and often occurring in the lexicons &c. in this sense.]

(TA.) One says, A_in~ahu laHasanu AlT~iy~api [ Verily he is good in respect of the mode, or manner, of folding, &c.]. (K, TA.) And TawaAhu Tiy~apF jay~idapF [ He folded it, &c., in a good mode, or manner, of doing so ]. (TA.) And hence the saying of Dhu-rRummeh, kamaA tuna$~aru baEoda AlT~iy~api Alkutubu [ Like as the writings, or letters, are unfolded after the folding in a particular manner ]: (S, TA:) he said Tiy~ap , with kesr, because he did not mean a single time [of folding]. (TA.) ― -b2- [See also 1, second sentence, where it is mentioned as a simple inf. n., and sometimes pronounced TiyapN , without teshdeed.] ― -b3- Also i. q. niy~apN ; (S, K;) and so ↓ Tawiy~apN ; (K;) and [agreeably with this explanation] Kh says that it may mean A place of alighting or abode [ to which one purposes repairing, or betaking himself ], and it may mean an object of aim or purpose or intention [ whatever it be ]: (S:) and in the A it is expl. as meaning the direction towards which countries are traversed: (TA:) one says Tiy~apN baEiydapN i. e. [ A place of alighting or abode &c.] that is distant, or remote: and baEudato Ean~aA Tiy~atuhu i. e. sourceDefinition: is said by some to be like ↓ TiwFY , meaning A thing twice done [as though folded]; and to be thus in the Kur [xx. 12 and lxxix. 16]; meaning twice sanctified [referring to the valley there mentioned]; (S, TA; [and thus expl., and said to be like vinFY , in the Ksh and by Bd;]) or, as El-Hasan says, twice blest and sanctified: (S, TA:) or meaning twice called [referring to the calling of Moses mentioned in the context]. definition: (S, A, O, K) and ↓ miEorajN and ↓ maEorajN , (S, O, K,) the second and third allowable accord.
sourceDefinition: (S, A, O, K) and ↓ miEorajN and ↓ maEorajN , (S, O, K,) the second and third allowable accord. to Akh, like miroqaApN and maroqaApN , (S, O,) A ladder, or series of steps or stairs: (S, A, O, K:) or, with the article Al , [but most commonly the first of these with Al ,] a thing resembling a darajap [i. e. ladder, or series of steps or stairs ], upon which the souls ascend when they are taken [ from their bodies ]: it is said that there is nothing more beautiful than it; so that when the soul sees it, it cannot refrain from making its exit [from the body]: (TA:) hence layolapu AlmiEoraAji [ the Night of the Ladder; in which Mohammad is related to have ascended from Jerusalem to Heaven, after having been conveyed to the former from Mekkeh upon the beast named AlburaAq ]: pl. maEaAriyju and maEaAriju , like mafaAtiyHu and mafaAtiHu . (Msb.)

definition: A thing that is, or that is to be, coveted;
sourceDefinition: A thing that is, or that is to be, coveted; syn. maTomaEN ; (S, TA;) as also ↓ EasamN ; or this latter signifies coveting, or covetousness; and Ea$amN , with $ , is a dial. var. of it. (TA in this art. and in art. E$m .) So the former signifies in the saying maA laka fiY baniY fulaAnK maEosimN [ There is not for thee, in the sons of such a one, anything that is, or is to be, coveted ]. (S.) [Freytag has written this word maEosam , as from the K, in which I do not find it; and has expl. it as signifying desire. ]

(K.) One says, of a she-camel, taEoSifu biraAkibihaA (tropical:) She goes quickly, or swiftly, with her rider; (Sh, S, Z, O, TA;) likening her to the wind in the swiftness of her course. (Z, TA.) (S.) ― -b3- [Hence, also,] EaSafati AlHarobu biAlqawomi , (O, K, * TA,) aor. taEoSifu bihimo , (S, O, TA,) (tropical:) War, or the war, carried off, and destroyed, the people, or party; (S, O, K, TA;) as also bhm ↓ AESft , (O, K,) which is [said to be] the more correct. (TA.)

definition: The herb ( baqol ) of corn, or seed-produce: (Fr, S, O, K:) and (TA) the leaves, or blades, of corn, or seed-produce;
sourceDefinition: The herb ( baqol ) of corn, or seed-produce: (Fr, S, O, K:) and (TA) the leaves, or blades, of corn, or seed-produce; (MA, * Mgh, TA;) as also EuSuwfN ; each a pl. of ↓ EaSofapN : (MA: [or rather EaSofN is a coll. gen. n. of which EuSuwfN is the pl. and ↓ EaSofapN is the n. un.:]) or the leaves, or blades, that are upon the stalk of corn, or seedproduce, and that dry up and crumble; as also ↓ EaSofapN and ↓ EaSiyfapN and ↓ EuSaAfapN : or the leaves, and what is not eaten, thereof: in these three different senses it is expl. as used in the Kur lv. 11: (TA:) or it there means the stalk, or stem, of corn: (Fr, S voce rayoHaAnN :) or straw; (Jel, TA;) and so Alz~aroEi ↓ EaSiyfu ; (M voce tibonN ;) or Alz~aroEi ↓ EaSiyfapu : (so in copies of the K voce tibonN :) and EuSuwfN signifies straws: (IAar, TA:) or EaSofN signifies dry leaves, like straw: (Bd in lv. 11:) or corn, or seed-produce, or barley, cut while green, for fodder; syn. qaSiylN : (En-Nadr, TA:) or leaves of corn, or seed-produce, that are cut, and eaten while fresh: or the leaves of the ears of corn; as also ↓ EaSiyfapN : or what are cut thereof; as also ↓ EaSiyfN : or both signify the leaves, of corn, that incline in its lower part, and which one cuts off, in order that it may become lightened: or the former signifies the ears, themselves, of corn: and the pl. is EuSuwfN . (TA.) kaEaSofK maA^okuwlK , in the Kur [cv. last verse], means Like corn of which the grain has been eaten and the straw thereof remains: (El- Hasan El-Basree, S, O, K:) or like leaves of which the contents have been taken and which remain without any grain therein: (O, K:) or like EaSof , (O,) or leaves, (K,) which the beasts have eaten: (O, K:) or, as Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr is related to have said, like barley growing or growing forth [ that has been eaten ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And IAar says, (O, TA,) [the pl.] EuSuwfN , (O, K, TA,) with damm to the E , (TA,) [in the CK, erroneously, EaSuwf ,] signifies Handfuls of reaped corn; syn. kadarN [a coll. gen. n. of which the n. un. is kadarapN ]: (O, TA:) in the copies of the K, kudorap ; and in the L, kd . (TA.) -A2- And accord. to IAar, (O,) EuSuwfN signifies also Wines; syn. xumuwrN . (O, L, K. [In the CK xamorap ; and in the TA, as from the K, xmr .])

sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K) and EaASifapN (O, Msb, K) and ↓ EaSuwfN [but this app. has a more intensive meaning] (S, O, K) [and ↓ EaSiyfN as used in “ Fákihet el-Khulafà ” p. 196 line 18 but not found by me in this sense in any lexicon] and ↓ muEoSifN (S, O, K) and ↓ muEoSifapN (S, O, Msb, K) Wind blowing violently, or vehemently: (S, O, Msb, K:) pl. of the first EawaASifu , and of the second EaASifaAtN ; (Msb;) and of the last two ↓ maEaASifu and ↓ maEaASiyfu ; and ↓ muEoSifaAtN [pl. of muEoSifapN ] which signifies winds that raise the clouds and the winds. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also yawomN EaASifN , (Fr, S, O, Msb,) because of the violent blowing of the wind therein, (Fr, O, Msb,) EaASifN in this case being an instance of faAEilN in the sense of mafoEuwlN fiyhi , (S, O,) like as one says yawomN baAridN , (Fr, O,) or like layolN naAy^imN ; the meaning being, A day in which the wind blows violently, or vehemently: (S, O:) this is the meaning in the phrase fiY yawomK EaASifK (Fr, O, K) in the Kur [xiv. 21]: or this phrase may mean fiY yawomK EaASifi Alr~iyHi [ in a day violent, or vehement, in respect of the wind ], because the wind is mentioned in the former part of the sentence. (Fr, O.) ― -b3- See also EaSuwfN . ― -b4- EaASifN also signifies (tropical:) An arrow turning aside, or declining, from the butt; (El-Mufaddal, O, K, TA;) pl. EuS~afN ; a tropical meaning: (TA:) and anything inclining, or declining. (El-Mufaddal, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) or EaTanati AlA_ibilu EalaY AlmaA='i , (TA,) aor. and , inf. n. EuTuwnN , (S, Msb, K,) The camels lay down [ at the water ] after having satisfied their thirst; (S, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ EaT~anat : (K:) and AlEuTuwnu , (K, TA,) it is said, (TA,) signifies the resting, or the driving back to the nightly resting-place, a she-camel after her drinking: (K, TA:) or the bringing her back to the EaTan [q. v.], waiting in expectation with her, because she did not drink the first time, (so in the K accord. to the TA, but in the CK, agreeably with the S, this last meaning is made to relate to 4, q. v.,) then offering her the water a second time: (K, TA:) or it signifies [agreeably with the first explanation above] her satisfying her thirst, then lying down: (K, * TA:) in which explanation, in [some of the copies of] the K, vm tnrk is erroneously put for vum~a taboruk . (TA.) qado EaTanuwA mawaA$iyahumo occurs in a trad. as meaning They had rested, or had driven back to the nightly resting-place, their cattle. (TA.) -A2- EaTana Aljiloda , aor. (S, K) and , (K,) inf. n. EaTonN , (S,) He took EaloqaY , which is a certain plant, (S,) so says J, but, as 'Alee Ibn-Hamzeh says, it is the galoqap , a well-known plant, not the EaloqaY , that is used for this purpose, (IB, TA,) [or perhaps EaloqaY is a mistranscription for galoqaY , which is said in the K in art. glq to be a syn. of galoqapN ,] or farov [i. e. the feces thus termed ], or salt, and threw the skin into it, and covered it over, in order that its wool might become dissundered and loose; after which it is thrown into the tan: (S:) or, as also ↓ ET~nhu , he put the skin into the tan, and left it so that it became corrupt and stinking: (K:) or he sprinkled water upon it, (K, TA,) and folded it, (TA,) and buried it (K, TA) for a day and a night, (TA,) so that its hair (K, TA) or its wool, (TA,) became loose; in order that it might be plucked off; (K, TA;) and that it [the skin] might be then thrown into the tan, it being then stinking in the utmost degree: (TA:) or AlEatonu signifies the putting [a skin] into the tan. (Az, TA.) -A3- EaTina , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. EaTanN , (S,) said of a hide, It became stinking, and its wool fell off, in the process termed EaTon [expl. above]: (AZ, S, TA:) or it was put into the tan, and left so that it became corrupt and stinking: (K:) or water was sprinkled upon it, (K, TA,) and it was folded, (TA,) and buried (K, TA) for a day and a night, (TA,) so that its hair (K, TA) or its wool (TA) became loose; in order that it might be plucked off; (K, TA;) and that it [the skin] might be then thrown into the tan, it being then stinking in the utmost degree: (TA:) and ↓ AnETn signifies the same: (S, K:) or this signifies it (a skin) became loose in its wool without becoming corrupt. (AHn, TA.)

definition: means EaTanato A_ibiluhumo [ The people, or party, had their camels lying down at the water after having satisfied their thirst: see 1, first sentence].
sourceDefinition: means EaTanato A_ibiluhumo [ The people, or party, had their camels lying down at the water after having satisfied their thirst: see 1, first sentence]. (S, K.) -A2- AETn AlA_ibila He watered the camels and then made them to lie down [ at the water ]: (S, TA:) or he confined the camels at the water, and they lay down, after having come to it [ and drunk ], (K, TA,) in order that they might drink again: (TA:) this the Arabs do only in the intense heats of summer; not when the season becomes cool: (Msb:) or they do this only when the asterism of the Pleiades ( Alv~uray~aA ) rises [auro- rally, i. e. about the middle of May, O. S.], and men return from the seeking after herbage to the places of waters, or of constant sources of water: they do so only on the day of the camels' coming to the water; and they cease not to do thus [when necessary] until the time of the [auroral] rising of Canopus ( suhayol [i. e. early in August, O. S.]), in the xariyf , [app. here meaning the period of the rain so called, (see the latter of the two tables in page 1254,)] after which they do it not, but the camels come to the water and drink their draught and return from the water: (Az, TA:) or AETn AlA_ibila signifies he brought back the camels to the EaTan [q. v.], waiting in expectation with them, because they did not drink the first time. (So in the CK [agreeably with what here follows; but see 1, first sentence].) And one says, AETn Alr~ajulu baEiyrahu The man brought back his camel to the EaTan , waiting in expectation with him, he not having drunk. (S.)

definition: and ↓ maEoTinN (ISk, S, Mgh, Msb, K) or maEoTanN (TA [but this I find not elsewhere]) The usual abiding-place of camels: (K:) and also, (K, TA,) by predominance of usage, (TA,) or only, (Az, Msb,...
sourceDefinition: and ↓ maEoTinN (ISk, S, Mgh, Msb, K) or maEoTanN (TA [but this I find not elsewhere]) The usual abiding-place of camels: (K:) and also, (K, TA,) by predominance of usage, (TA,) or only, (Az, Msb, TA,) the place of camels, where they lie down, (Az, S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) at the water, (Az, S, TA,) or around the water, (Mgh, Msb,) or around the watering-trough, (K, TA,) in order that they may drink a second time, after the first draught, and then be sent back to the places of pasture to remain there during the intervals between the waterings; (S;) and likewise the places of sheep or goats, where they lie down around the water: (ISk, S, Msb, K, TA:) pl. of the former A^aEoTaAnN ; and of the latter ↓ maEaATinu ; (Az, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) which latter pl. is used by the lawyers as meaning [generally] the places of lying down of camels. (Msb.) The [space called] Hariym [q. v.] of the well of the EaTan is said to be forty cubits. (Mgh.) Prayer in the A^aEoTaAn of camels is forbidden, because the person praying is not secure from being hurt by them, and diverted from his prayer, and defiled by the sprinkling of their urine. (IAth, TA.) Darabati AlA_ibilu biEaTanK [in which AlA^aroDa is understood after AlAbl ] means The camels lay down [ in a place by the water ]: (S:) or satisfied themselves with drinking and then lay down around the water or by the watering-troughs, to be brought again to drink another time. (IAth, TA.) And one says, Darabati Aln~aAqapu biEaTanK The she-camel lay down [&c.]. (TA.) And Daraba Aln~aAsu biEaTanK (assumed tropical:) The people's camels satisfied themselves with drinking until they lay down and remained in their place [ at the water ]; occurring in a trad.: (TA in art. Drb :) or the people satisfied their thirst and then abode at the water. (K and TA in the present art.) ― -b2- [Hence] one says, fulaAnN waAsiEu AlEaTani waAlbaladi , (S,) or raHobu AlEaTani , (K, TA,) (tropical:) Such a one is a person possessing much wealth; having an ample dwelling or place of abode; (K, TA;) endowed with extensive power or strength or might; or liberal, munificent, or generous. (S, K, TA.) -A2- And AlEaTanu signifies AlEiroDu [app. as meaning Odour, from the same word as inf. n. of EaTina said of a hide]: so in the saying of 'Adee Ibn-Zeyd, cited by Sh, TaAhiru AlA^avowaAbi yaHomiY EiroDahu mino HanaA Al*~im~api A^awo Tamovi AlEaTano [ Pure in conduct, or actions; he guards his honour, or reputation, from unseemliness in respect of that which should be held sacred, or inviolable, or filthiness of odour ]. (TA)

sourceDefinition: , (Msb, K, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. Eaq~N , (Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) He clave, split, slit, ripped, or rent; (Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA;) and he cut. (Mgh, O, TA.) You say, Eaq~a vawobahu He slit, ripped, or rent, his garment. (Msb.) And Euq~ato tamiymatuhu fiY baniY fulaAnK [ His amulet was cut off among the sons of such a one ]; said of a boy when he has attained to the prime of manhood, and become strong, with a tribe; originating from the fact that as long as the boy was an infant, his mother hung upon him amulets to preserve him from the evil eye; and when he became full-grown, they were cut off from him: whence the saying of a poet, bilaAdN bihaA Eaq~a Al$~abaAbu tamiymatiY waA^aw~alu A^aroDK mas~a jilodiY turaAbuhaA [ A country in which the attaining to the prime of manhood cut off my amulet, and the first land of which the dust touched my skin ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] Eaq~ati Alr~iyHu Almuzona , aor. and inf. n. as above, The wind drew forth a shower of fine rain from the mzn [or clouds containing water ]; as though it rent them. (TA.) And Euq~ati Als~aHaAbapu The cloud poured forth its water; [as though it were rent;] and ↓ AinoEaq~at [means the same]; (TA;) and ↓ AEtq~t [likewise]. (O.) ― -b3- And Eaq~a Eano waladihi , (S, Msb,) or Eani Almawoluwdi , (K,) aor. (S, Msb, TA) and , (TA,) inf. n. Eaq~N , (S, Msb,) He slaughtered as a sacrifice (S, Msb, K, TA) for his child, (S, Msb,) or for the new-born child, (K,) a sheep or goat, (T, Msb, TA,) [ generally the latter, ] on the seventh day after the birth. (T, S, Msb, TA.) And He shaved the [ hair termed ] Eaqiyqap [q. v.] (S, TA) of his child, (S,) or of the new-born child. (TA.) ― -b4- And Eaq~a biAls~ahomi He shot the arrow towards the sky; and that arrow was called EaqiyqapN ; (S, O, K;) and it was the arrow of self-excuse: they used to do thus in the Time of Ignorance [on the occasion of a demand for blood-revenge]; and if the arrow returned smeared with blood, they were not content save with the retaliation of slaughter; but if it returned clean, they stroked their beards, and made reconciliation on the condition of the bloodwit; the stroking of the beards being a sign of reconciliation: the arrow, however, as IAar says, did not [ever] return otherwise than clean: (S, O:) the origin was this: a man of the tribe was slain, and the slayer was prosecuted for his blood; whereupon a company of the chief men [of the family of the slayer] collected themselves together to the heirs [who claimed satisfaction for the blood] of the slain, and offered the bloodwit, asking forgiveness for the blood; and if the heir [who claimed satisfaction and who acted for himself and his coheirs] was a strong man, impatient of injury, he refused to take the bloodwit; but if weak, he consulted the people of his tribe, and then said to the petitioners, “ We have, between us and our Creator, a sign denoting command and prohibition: we take an arrow, and set it on a bow, and shoot it towards the sky; and if it return to us smeared with blood, we are forbidden to take the bloodwit, and are not content save with the retaliation of slaughter; but if it return clean, as it went up, we are commanded to take the bloodwit: ” so they made reconciliation; for this arrow never returned otherwise than clean; and thus they had an excuse in the opinion of the ignorant of them. (L, TA.) A poet (S, O, TA) of the family of the slain, said by some to be of Hudheyl, by IB to be El-As'ar El-Joafee, who was absent from this reconciliation, (TA,) says, Eaq~uwA bisahomK vum~a qaAluwA SaAliHuwA yaA layotaniY fiY Alqawomi A_i*o masaHuwA Alil~uHaY [ They shot an arrow towards the sky; them they said, “ Make ye reconciliation: ” would that I were among the party when they stroked the beards ]: (S, O, TA:) or, as some relate it, the first word is Eaq~awoA , with fet-h to the q ; which belongs to the class of unsound verbs [i. e. to art. EqY ]. (S, O.) ― -b5- One says also, Eaq~a waAlidahu , (S, O, K,) or A^abaAhu , (Msb,) aor. , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. EuquwqN (S, O, Msb, K) and maEaq~apN (S, O, K) and Eaq~N , (TA,) He was undutiful, disobedient, refractory, or ill-mannered, to his parent, or father; contr. of bar~ahu ; (K;) he broke his compact of obedience to his parent, or father; (TA;) he disobeyed his father; and failed, or neglected, to behave to him in a good, or comely, manner. (Msb.) And Eaq~a Alr~aHima , (TA, and Ham p. 93,) like qaTaEahaA [i. e. He severed the tie, or ties, of relationship, by unkind behaviour to his kindred ]. (Ham ib.) And Eaq~a [alone], aor. , inf. n. EuquwqN , [ He was undutiful, &c.; or he acted undutifully, &c.; or] he contravened, or opposed, him whom he was under an obligation to obey. (Har p. 158.) Euquwqu AlwaAlidayoni [ Undutiful treatment, &c., of the two parents ] is said in a trad. to be one of the great sins. (O.) And it is said in a prov., AlEuquwqu A^aHadu Alv~ukolayoni [ Undutiful treatment of a parent is one of the two sorts of being bereft of a child ]: or, as some relate it, AlEuquwqu vukolu mano lamo yavokalo [ Undutiful treatment of a parent is (like) the bereavement of him who is not (really) bereft of his child ]: i. e. he whom his children have treated undutifully ( mino Eaq~ahu waladuhu ) is as though he were bereft of his children although they are living. (O.) [See also 3: and 4.] ― -b6- Hence, from Euquwqu AlwaAlidayoni , the verb is metaphorically used in the saying, in a trad., mavalukumo wamavalu EaAy^i$apa mavalu AlEayoni fiY Alr~aA^osi tuw^o*iY SaAHibahaA walaA yasotaTiyEu A^ano yaEuq~ahaA A_il~aA biA@l~a*iY huwa xayorN lahaA (tropical:) [ The similitude of you and of 'Áïsheh is that of the eye in the head, when it hurts its owner, and he cannot treat it severely save with that which is good for it: app. meaning that her severity was for the good of the objects thereof]. (TA.) -A2- Eaq~a , intrans., said of lightning: see 7. -A3- Eaq~ato said of a mare, and of an ass: see 4. -A4- Eaq~ati Ald~alowu , inf. n. Eaq~u , means The bucket came up full from the well; and some of the Arabs say Eaq~at as having taEoqiyapN for its inf. n.; but it is [said to be] originally ↓ Eaq~aqat , the third q being changed into Y , [which is then in this case suppressed,] like as they said taZan~ayotu from AlZ~an~u : [it is, however, mentioned in the TA in art. Eqw also, and there expl. as meaning it rose in the well turning round: and from what here follows, it appears to mean it rose swiftly, cleaving the air: ] a poet, cited by IAar, says, of a bucket, Eaq~ato kamaA Eaq~ato daluwfu AlEiqobaAnN meaning It clave [the air of] the well, rising swiftly, like the hastening of the swift eagle in its flight towards the prey. (TA in the present art.)

definition: It became cloven, split, slit, ripped, or rent;
sourceDefinition: It became cloven, split, slit, ripped, or rent; or it clave, split, &c.; said of anything; (S, O, K, TA;) mentioned by Th as said of a garment. (TA.) ― -b2- AnEq~t Als~aHaAbahu The cloud became rent with the water. (S, O, K.) See also 1, first quarter. [And see 8.] ― -b3- AnEq~ Albaroqu and ↓ Eaq~a [of which latter the aor. is probably yaEaq~u , and the inf. n. EaqaqN , said in the K to mean Aino$iqaAqN ,] signify ta$aq~aqa and Aino$aq~a [as though meaning The lightning became cloven ]; (TA;) [but] the former is expl. as signifying the lightning was, or became, in a state of commotion ( taDar~aba ) in the clouds. (S, O.) [Another meaning is suggested by an explanation of EaqiyqapN (q. v.) in relation to lightning.] ― -b4- AnEq~ AlgubaAru i. q. saTaEa [app. as meaning The dust spread, or diffused itself ]: (IF, O, K:) or Aino$aq~a wasaTaEa [ became cleft, and diffused itself ]. (TA.) ― -b5- AnEq~ AlwaAdiY The valley was, or became, deep. (TA.) -A2- AnEq~t AlEuqodapu The knot became strongly, or firmly, tied. (O, * K, * TA.)

definition: , applied to a mare, (S, O, K, TA,) and to an ass, (TA,) Pregnant: (S, O, K:) or not pregnant after having been covered by the stallion, or during a year or two years or some years;
sourceDefinition: , applied to a mare, (S, O, K, TA,) and to an ass, (TA,) Pregnant: (S, O, K:) or not pregnant after having been covered by the stallion, or during a year or two years or some years; (K;) or it signifies thus also; (O;) having two contr. meanings; (K;) or it is applied to one in the latter state as implying a presage of good; (O, K;) so says AHát; (O, TA;) i. e., as though they meant that she would become pregnant: (TA:) it is extr.; [as being from A^aEaq~ato ;] and one should not say ↓ muEiq~N ; or this is a bad dial. var.; (S, O, K;) or, accord. to AA, it is from AEq~t , and EaquwqN is from Eaq~ato : (TA:) the pl. is EuquqN , and EiqaAqN is a pl. pl., (S, O, K,) i. e. pl. of EuquqN . (S, O.) It is said in a prov., Talaba AlA^abolaqa AlEaquwqa , meaning He sought an impossible thing; because Ablq is applied to a male, and Eqwq means pregnant: (S, O, and K in art. blq ) or AlAblq AlEqwq means the dawn, because it breaks, lit, cleaves. (O, and K in art. blq .) ― -b2- nawaY AlEaquwqi means Date-stones that are easily broken, (Lth, S, O, K,) soft to be chewed; (Lth, O, K;) which are given as provender to camels, (S,) or to the pregnant thereof, in consideration of her state, wherefore they are thus called; and which are eaten, or chewed, by the old woman; but this is of the speech of the people of El Basrah, and not known by the Arabs in their desert: (Lth, O:) and sometimes they called a single date-stone of this sort ↓ EaqiyqapN . (S.) -A2- See also EaAq~N .

sourceDefinition: [a subst. from EaqiyqN , made so by the affix p . Hence, because cleft, or furrowed, in the earth,] A river, or rivulet. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- And A fillet, or bandage, ( EiSaAbapN ,) at the time of its being rent from a garment, or piece of cloth. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b3- And The prepuce of a boy (AO, IAar, O, K) when he is circumcised. (TA.) ― -b4- And [app. because made of cut pieces of skin,] A [ leathern water-bag such as is commonly called ] mazaAdap . (IAar, O, K.) ― -b5- Also The wool of a ja*aE [or sheep in or before its second year ]: (S, O, K, TA:) that of a vaniY~ [or sheep in its third year] is called janiybapN : (TA:) and the hair of a young one recently born, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) that comes forth upon his head in his mother's belly, (TA,) of human beings, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) because it is cut off on his seventh day, (Mgh,) and of others, (Msb,) [i. e.] of beasts likewise; (S, O, K, TA;) as also ↓ EaqiyqN and ↓ Eiq~apN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) but A 'Obeyd says that he had not heard this last except in relation to human beings and asses: (S, O, K: *) its pl. (i. e. the pl. of Eiq~apN ) is EiqaqN : (O, K:) [the pl. of EaqiyqapN and EaqiyqN is EaqaAy^iqu : a law of the Sunneh requires that the Eaqiyqap of an infant should be weighed, and its weight in silver be given to the poor: (and Herodotus, in ii. 65, mentions a similar custom as obtaining among the Ancient Egyptians:)] when the hair has once fallen from the young [by its being cut], the term EaqiyqapN ceases to be applied to it: so says Lth: (O, TA:) but it occurs in a trad. applied to hair as being likened to the hair of a recently-born infant. (TA.) ― -b6- Hence, (S, O,) it is applied also to The sheep, or goat, [ generally the latter, ] that is slaughtered (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) as a sacrifice for the recentlyborn infant (S, Mgh, Msb) on the occasion of the shaving of the infant's hair (O, K) on the seventh day after his birth, (S, Msb,) and of which the limbs are divided, and cooked with water and salt, and given as food to the poor: (Lth, TA:) Z holds it to be thus called from the same word as applied to the hair: but it is said [by some] to be so called because it is slaughtered by cutting the windpipe and gullet and the two external jugular veins: (TA:) the Prophet disallowed this appellation, (Mgh, Msb,) as being of evil omen, (Mgh,) or as though he saw them to regard it as of evil omen, (Msb,) and desired them to use nasiykapN in its stead; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) saying I like not AlEuquwq . (TA.) ― -b7- Eaqiyqapu Albaroqi signifies What remains [ for an instant ] in the clouds, of the rays, or beams, of lightning; (Lth, O, K;) as also ↓ AlEuqaqu ; (K;) which, as well as AlEaqiyqapu , is also expl. as meaning lightning which one sees in the midst of the clouds, resembling a drawn sword: (TA:) or Eaqiyqapu Albaroqi signifies lightning in a state of commotion in the clouds: (S, O:) or lightning extending in an elongated form in the side, or breadth, of the clouds: (TA:) or lightning that cleaves the clouds, and extends high, into the midst of the sky, without going to the right and left: (S in art. xfw :) or, as expl. by Aboo-Sa'eed, a flash of lightning that has spread in the horizon: (O, voce $aqiyqapN :) a sword is likened thereto: (S, O, K:) and [the pl.] EaqaAy^iqu is a name for swords: (O, K:) ↓ EaqiyqN , also, signifies lightning. (TA.) ― -b8- And EaqiyqapN signifies also An arrow shot towards the sky; (S, O, K;) the arrow of self-excuse; which was used in the manner described in the explanation of the phrase Eaq~a biAls~ahomi [q. v.]. (S, O.) ― -b9- See also EaquwqN , last signification.

definition: [The magpie, corvus pica;
sourceDefinition: [The magpie, corvus pica; so called in the present day;] a certain bird, (S, O, Msb, K,) well known, (S, O,) of the size of the pigeon, (Msb,) party-coloured, black and white, (O, Msb, K,) having a long tail, (O, Msb,) said by Is-hák El-Mowsilee to be the same that is called $ajajaY , (Th, IB, TA,) a species of crow, (IAth, Msb, TA,) wherefore it is said in a trad. that the man in the state of A_iHoraAm may kill it; (IAth, TA;) its cry resembles the sound of E and q [or the repeated sound of Eaqo ]; (O, K;) and the Arabs regard it as an evil omen. (Msb.) [See also SuradN .]

definition: Undutiful, disobedient, refractory, or illmannered, to his parent, or father;
sourceDefinition: Undutiful, disobedient, refractory, or illmannered, to his parent, or father; (S, * O, * K;) breaking, or one who breaks, his compact of obedience to his parent, or father; (TA;) disobeying, or disobedient to, his father; and failing, or neglecting, to behave to him in a good, or comely, manner; (Msb;) [and severing, or one who severs, the tie, or ties, of relationship, by unkind behaviour to his kindred; (see its verb;)] and ↓ Eaq~N signifies the same; (O, K;) as also ↓ EuqaqN , (S, O, TA,) but in an intensive sense, altered from EaAq~N , like gudar and fusaq from gaAdir and faAsiq , in the K erroneously said to be EaqaqN ; (TA;) and ↓ EuquqN ; (L, and TA as from the K, but not in my MS. copy of the K nor in the CK;) which last signifies also [as a pl.] men severing, or who sever, the ties of relationship, by unkind behaviour to their kindred; and also remote, or distant, enemies: (TA:) [and ↓ EaquwqN is app. used (as Freytag asserts it to be) in the sense of EaAq~N in the Fákihet el-Khulatà, p. 55, 1. 7 from the bottom:] the pl. of EaAq~N is EaqaqapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) like kafarapN , (S,) and Euq~aqN , like ruk~aEN , a form used by Ru-beh, (O,) and A^aEiq~apN , which is an extr. [meaning anomalous] pl. (Ham p. 93.) ↓ *uqN Euqaqu , (S, O,) in a trad., (S,) said by Aboo-Sufyán to Hamzeh on the day of Ohod, when he passed by him slain, (S, * O,) means *uqN jazaA='a fiEolika [ Taste thou the recompense of thy deed ], (S,) or *uqi Alqatola [ taste thou slaughter ], (O,) yaA EaAq~u [ O undutiful, &c.; or, accord. to the explanation in the TA mentioned above, Euqaqu , for yaA Euqaqu , means O very undutiful, &c.]. (S, O.)

sourceDefinition: , [aor. yaEomaY ,] inf. n. EamFY , He was, or became, blind, (S, Msb, K,) of both eyes; (Msb, K, * TA;) as also ↓ AiEomaAYa , aor. yaEomaAyu , inf. n. AiEomiyaA='N ; (K;) [said by SM to be like AiroEawaY , aor. yaroEawiY , inf. n. AiroEiwaA='N ; as though AiEomaAYa were originally AiEomaY~a , like as AiroEawaY is originally AiroEaw~a , both being of the measure AifoEl~a ; but he adds, correctly, that,] accord. to Sgh, AiEomaAYa is originally like AidohaAmama , which becomes AidohaAm~a , [i. e. it is originally AiEomaAyaYa ,] but the latter Y is changed into A because of the fet-hah of the former, so that it becomes AiEomaAyaA , and the two, thus differing, do not easily admit of idghám (TA;) and sometimes the Y of AiEomaAYa is musheddedeh, (Sgh, K, TA,) so that it becomes [↓ AiEomaAY~a , aor. yaEomaAY~u , inf. n. AiEmiy~aA='N ,] like AidohaAm~a , aor. yadohaAm~u , inf. n. AidohiymaAmN ; but this is by a straining of a point, and not in use: (Sgh, TA:) and ↓ tEm~Y , likewise, signifies the same, (K, TA,) i. e., the same as EamiYa . (TA.) And you say also, Eamiyato EayonaAhu His two eyes were, or became, blind. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence EamFY is metaphorically used in relation to the mind, as meaning (tropical:) An erring; the connection between the two meanings being the not finding, or not taking, the right way: (Msb:) or the being blind in respect of the mind: and in this sense, the verb is as above, with the exception of the measure AifEaAl~a [and the abbreviated form of this]. (K, * TA. [ AafoEaAlK in the CK in this passage is a mistranscription, for A@foEaAl~a .]) You say, EamiYa Eano ru$odihi , and Huj~atihi , meaning lamo yahotadi (assumed tropical:) [ He did not, or could not, become guided to his right course, and his plea or the like; i. e. he was, or became, blind thereto ]. (TA.) And EamiYa Eano Haq~ihi (assumed tropical:) [ He was, or became, blind to his right, or due ], like Ea$iYa Eanohu . (TA in art. E$w .) ― -b3- One says also EamiYa Ealayohi Alxabaru (tropical:) The information was, or became, unapparent, obscure, or covert, to him. (Mgh, Msb. *) And EamiYa Ealayohi Tariyquhu , (TA,) and AlA^amoru , (S, TA,) and Al$~iEoru , and AlkalaAmu , (Har p. 190,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ His way, or road, and the affair, and the poetry, or verse, and the speech, or saying, ] was, or became, obscure, or dubious, to him; (S, TA, and Har ubi suprá) and so ↓ Eum~iYa ; (TA;) and ↓ tEm~Y . (Har ubi suprá.) Hence, accord. to different readings, in the Kur [xxviii. 66], faEamiyato Ealayohimu A@loA^anobaA='u and ↓ faEum~iyato (assumed tropical:) [ And the pleas shall be obscure, or dubious, to them ]. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And Eamiytu A_ilaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) I betook myself to such a thing, not desiring any other; as also EaTi$otu . (TA. [Accord. to the TA, the inf. ns. of these two verbs, thus used, are EmyAn and ET$An : but they are correctly EamFY and EaTa$N .]) -A2- EamaY Almawoju , aor. yaEomiY , (S, K,) inf. n. EamoYN , (S,) The waves cast the particles of rubbish, or the like, (S, K, TA,) driving them to their upper, or uppermost, parts, (TA,) and the foam. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And EamaY bilugaAmihi , (K, TA,) aor. yaEomiY , (TA,) He (a camel) brayed, and cast the foam of his mouth upon his head, or the upper part of his head, or anywhere: (K, TA:) mentioned by ISd. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence] EamaAniY bika*aA (assumed tropical:) He cast upon me a suspicion of such a thing. (TA.) ― -b4- EamaY , aor. yaEomiY , said of water, (K, TA,) and of other things, (TA,) also signifies It flowed; (K, TA;) and so hamaY . (TA.) ― -b5- And EmY Aln~abotu [app. EamaY ] and ↓ AEtmY and AiEotam~a are three syn. dial. vars., (TA in this art.,) meaning (assumed tropical:) The plant, or herbage, became of its full height, and blossomed; (S, K, TA, in explanation of the last, in art. Em ;) and became luxuriant, or abundant and dense. (TA in that art.)

sourceDefinition: , (S,) or laqiythu Sak~apa EumaY~K , and ↓ EumoYK , which occurs in poetry, (K, TA,) in a case in which the metre requires it, a verse of Ru-beh, who uses it for EamaY~K , (TA, [which shows, by citing that verse, that EamFY , the reading in the CK, is wrong,]) and ↓ A^aEomaY , (K,) i. e. [ I came to him, or I met him, ] in the time of midday when the heat was vehement, (S,) or in the most vehement heat of midday in summer (K, and Lh and O and TA in art. Sk ) when the heat almost blinded by its vehemence; (Lh and O and TA in that art.;) a time in which the divinelyappointed prayer [of midday] is forbidden: it is said only in the hot season; because when a man goes forth at that time, he cannot fill his eyes with the light of the sun; or, as ISd says, because the gazelle seeks the covert when the heat is vehement, and his eye becomes weak by reason of the whiteness of the sun, and the bright shining thereof, and he is dazzled, so that he knocks against his covert, not seeing it: (TA:) EumaY~ being an abbreviated dim. of A^aEomaY : (S:) or it is a name for the heat, (K, TA,) itself: (TA:) or the name of a certain man, (K, TA,) of [the tribe of] 'Adwán, who used to press forward with the pilgrims when the heat was vehement, as is related in the Nh, or (TA) who used to decide cases judicially in, or concerning, the pilgrimage, and he came among a company journeying upon their camels, (K, TA,) performing the religious visit called Eumorap , (TA,) and they alighted at a station in a hot day, whereupon he said, “ Upon whomsoever shall come this hour, or time, of tomorrow while he is HaraAm [i. e. in the condition of one performing the acts of the Haj~ or of the Eumorap ], (K, TA,) not having accomplished his Eumorap , (TA,) he shall remain HaraAm until [this time] next year: ” and they immediately sprang up, (K, TA,) hastening, (TA,) so that they arrived at the House [of God, at Mekkeh, in the time required,] from a distance of a journey of two nights, using exertion; (K, TA;) and this saying became a prov., as is related in the M: (TA:) or it was the name of a certain man, (S, K, TA,) of the Amalekites, (S, TA,) who made a sudden attack upon a people, and exterminated them; (S, K, TA;) and the time became called in relation to him. (S, TA.) [See also art. Sk .]

definition: Tracts of land in which is no sign of the way, (S, K,) nor any habitation or cultivation, (K,) or nor any trace of habitation or cultivation;
sourceDefinition: Tracts of land in which is no sign of the way, (S, K,) nor any habitation or cultivation, (K,) or nor any trace of habitation or cultivation; (S;) and ↓ maEaAmK signifies the same; (S, K;) this latter being a pl. of which the sing., said by ISd to be unknown to him, should by rule be mEmyp [app. muEomiyapN ], but it is ↓ Eum~aY , deviating from rule; (TA;) or it means majaAhilu , and its sing. is mEmAp [i. e. ↓ maEomaApN ] signifying a place of erring, or wandering from the right way: (Har p. 85:) in the K, A^aEomaA='N is also expl. as signifying juh~aAlN [pl. of jaAhilN ], and is said to be [in this sense] pl. of A^aEomaY : but this is a double mistake, for it signifies majaAhilu , [like as maEaAmK is said to do above,] and its sing. is EmY [app. ↓ EamFY ]. (TA.) In the phrase ↓ A^aEomaA='u EaAmiyapN , [in the CK, erroneously, EAmiy~apN ,] the latter word is added to give intensiveness to the meaning; i. e., it signifies [ Tracts in which is no sign of the way, &c.,] in the utmost degree obscure or dubious: thus it is in the following verse: (TA:) Ru-beh says, A^aEomaAw^uhu ↓ wabaladK EaAmiyapK kaA^an~a lawona A^aroDihi samaAw^uhu [ And many a desert, or waterless desert, whereof the tracts in which is no sign of the way are in the utmost degree obscure or dubious, as though the colour of its ground were like that of its sky ]: (S, TA:) he means warub~a baladK . (S.) ― -b2- Also Tall; applied to men: (IAar, K:) pl. of ↓ EaAmK , like as A^anoSaArN is of naASirN . (IAar, TA.)

definition: He sought, desired, demanded, or begged, of him, aid, help, or assistance.
sourceDefinition: He sought, desired, demanded, or begged, of him, aid, help, or assistance. (MA.) You say, AisotaEanotuhu , (Mgh,) or AisotaEanotu bihi , (S, Msb,) or both, (K,) ↓ faA^aEaAnaniY (S, Mgh, Msb, * K) and ↓ EaAwananiY , (S, TA,) for which last, ↓ Eaw~ananiY is erroneously put in the copies of the K; (TA;) [i. e. I sought, &c., of him, aid, &c., and he aided me. ] The alteration of the infirm letter [ w into A ] is made in AstEAn and ↓ AEAn in imitation of a general rule [which requires it when that alteration is made in the unaugmented triliteral verb], though EaAna , aor. yaEuwnu , [as their source of derivation,] is not used. rawSourceText: (S, K) and ↓ guronuwqN and ↓ gironawoqN (O, K) A certain aquatic bird, (S, O, K, TA,) long in the neck (S, O, TA) and in the legs, (TA,) white, (O, K, TA,) or black: (K, TA:) [app. the white stork, ardea ciconia; or, accord. to some, the black stork, ardea nigra: ] or, accord. to IAmb, the males [or male ] thereof: (TA:) or the first, (O, K,) as also the second, (K,) signifies the kurokiY~ [or Numidean crane, ardea virgo ]: (As, O, K, TA:) or a certain bird resembling this: (ISk, O, K, TA:) pl. garaAniyqu . (O, TA.) It is related of the Prophet that [when he was reciting the words of the Kur (liii. 19 and 20), “ Have ye considered El-Lát, and El-'Ozzà, and Menáh, the other third? ”] the Devil put into his mouth the saying tiloka AlgaraAniyqu AlEulaY [ Those are the most high grAnyq , as though meaning cranes, for the Numidian crane is remarkable in the East for its superlatively-high flight]; referring, as IAar says, to the idols, which were asserted to be intercessors with God, wherefore they are likened to the birds that rise high into the sky: (O, TA: *) or grAnyq may in this case be a pl. of one of the sings. expl. in what here follows [but applied to females]. (O.) ― -b2- guronayoqN (O, K, TA, and so in copies of the S) and ↓ gironayoqN (IJ, TA, and so in some copies of the S in the place of the former) and ↓ guronuwqN and ↓ gironawoqN (S, O, K, TA) and ↓ gironiyqN (K) and ↓ gironaAqN and ↓ garawonaqN (O, K) and ↓ guraAniqN (S, K) signify (assumed tropical:) A tender youth; (S;) or a white, or fair, and comely, or beautiful, youth; (O, K;) or a youth white, or fair, tender, having beautiful hair, and comely: (TA:) pl. garaAniyqu and garaAniqapN (S, O, K) and garaAniqu , (S, K,) which last may be pl. of guraAniqN , agreeably with analogy, (IAmb, TA,) or it may be a contraction of garaAniyqu , as such used by a poet. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yago$aY , inf. n. ga$aAwapN , It covered, or concealed, him, or it; (TA;) as also ↓ tg$~Ahu . (MA.) And one says, ga$aAniY All~ayolu , i. e. ga$iyaniY [ The night covered me, or concealed me: or the meaning may be that which next follows]. (JK.) ― -b2- ga$iyahu , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) is said of an event ( A^amorN ), [and of heat, (S and K in art. dgm ,) and of cold, (K in that art.,) and of an affection of the mind or body, and of various things, sometimes in like manner of a man, and of a company of men,] in a similar sense; and so ↓ tg$~Ahu ; (K, TA;) both signifying It came upon, [or invaded, so as to surprise, and so as to over-whelm, properly meaning] as a thing that covered, him, or it. (K, * TA.) Hence, in the Kur [liii. 16], A_i*o yago$aY A@lsi~dorapa maA yago$aY [ When there was coming upon the lote-tree so as to cover it, or overspread it, what was so coming ]. (TA.) And in the same [xx. 81], faga$iyahumo mina A@loyam~i maA ga$iyahumo [ And there came upon them so as to overwhelm them, of the sea, what so came upon them ]. (TA.) And in the same [viii. 11], A_i*o yago$aAkumu [followed by A@Aln~uEaAsu , i. e. When it (drowsiness) was coming upon you, or overcoming you ]; accord. to one reading; other readings being yugo$iykumu and yuga$~iykumu [followed by A@ln~uEaAsa ]. (TA.) See also gaA$iyapN , in three places. ― -b3- [A somewhat similar signification of ga$iyahu will be found below.] ― -b4- One says of the night, yago$aY biZulomatihi kul~a maA bayona Als~amaA='i waAlA^aroDi [ It covers, or conceals, with its darkness, everything that is between the heaven and the earth ]. (Jel in xcii. 1.) And [hence it is said that] ga$iYa All~ayolu means The night was, or became, dark; as also ↓ Ag$Y . (Msb, TA.) ― -b5- [And ga$iyahu , and ga$iYa baSarahu and ↓ g$~Ahu , signify It, i. e. light ( Dawo'N ), came upon him, and upon his eye, with an overpowering effect, so as to obscure, or dazzle, his sight. ] ― -b6- ga$iyahu also signifies jaA='ahu (S) or A^ataAhu (Mgh, Msb, K) [which have two meanings, i. e. He came to him, and he did it; both, perhaps, here meant, for both are well-known meanings of ga$iyahu ]; and, thus used, the aor. is as above, (TA,) and the inf. n. is ga$ayaAnN , (S, TA,) or gi$oyaAnN , (so in one of my copies of the S,) or the subst. is ↓ gi$oyaAnN , (Msb,) with kesr, (Mgh, Msb,) syn. with A_itoyaAnN . (Mgh.) You say, ga$iYa fulaAnFA He came to such a one; syn. A^ataAhu ; as also ga$aAhu , aor. yago$uwhu . (K.) ― -b7- [Hence,] ga$iyahaA , (S, MA, Msb, K,) inf. n. ga$ayaAnN or gi$oyaAnN , (accord. to different copies of the S,) or the latter and ga$oYN , (MA,) or ↓ gi$oyaAnN is the subst. in this case also, (Msb,) and syn. with A_itoyaAnN , metonymically used in the sense of jimaAEN , (Mgh, Msb,) (tropical:) He compressed her; (S, MA, Msb, K;) namely, a woman; (MA, K;) as also ↓ tg$~AhA . (MA, Msb, TA.) ― -b8- And ga$iYa A_ilayohi maHojarFA He did to him ( A^ataY A_ilayohi ) a forbidden action. (TA in art. Hjr .) [Hence,] ↓ gi$oyaAnu AlmaHaArimi [ The doing of forbidden things ]. (Mgh and Msb and K in art. rhq .) And ga$iYa Al$~aYo'a He occupied himself with the thing, engaged in it, or personally managed or conducted it; syn. laAbasahu and baA$arahu . (JM.) [And ↓ tg$~Y has a similar meaning; for it is said that] Alt~aga$~iY and Alga$oYu primarily signify AlA_itoyaAnu and AlmulaAbasapu : and they took an extended range in using the former, so that one said, biAlEadoli ↓ taga$~aAhumo or biAlojawori [app. meaning He ruled them with equity or with injustice ]. (Ham p. 27.) [And one says, yago$aY AlHuruwba (see Ham p. 27), meaning He plunges into wars, or battles: see mugaAmisN , and its verb.] ― -b9- One says also, ga$iyahu biAls~awoTi , (K, in which it is said to be like raDiyahu , and so accord. to some copies of the S, the phrase in these being ga$iyatu Alr~ajula biAls~awoTi ,) or bihi ↓ ga$~aAhu , (accord. to other copies of the S, the verb in these being written ga$~ayotu , and thus accord. to an explanation of qan~aEa raA^osahu biAls~awoTi in art. qnE in the K,) He struck him (i. e. a man, S) with the whip; he flogged him. (S, K.) -A2- gu$iYa Ealayohi , (S, MA, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. ga$oYN , (S, Mgh, * K,) or gu$oYN , (MA,) or both, (Msb,) and ga$ayaAnN , (K, TA, and so in some copies of the S,) or gi$oyaAnN , (so in other copies of the S,) and ↓ ga$oyapN , (S, Mgh,) or this last is an inf. n. of un., (Msb,) or it is the subst., (K,) He swooned, i. e. became senseless: (MA, PS:) or i. q. A^ugomiYa Ealayohi [q. v.]: (K, TA:) or Alga$oYu , or Algu$oYu , is a state of inertness ( taEaT~ul , Mgh, Msb) of the motive and sensitive faculties, (Mgh,) or of the motive faculties and of the sensitive will, (Msb,) on account of the weakness of the heart, (Mgh, Msb,) and the soul's becoming drawn together thereto by a cause that suppresses it ( yuxofiyhi ) within so that it finds not a place of passage, and of the causes thereof is a strangling [or stifling ], or hurtful, cold repletion, or vehement hunger, (Mgh,) or vehement pain, (Mgh, Msb,) or cold, or excessive hunger, (Msb,) or an evil affection in some associate, or participating, organ, such as the heart and the stomach: (Mgh:) some say that it is the same as AlA_igomaA='u [for which see its proper art.]; (Mgh, Msb;) thus say the scholastic theologians: (Mgh:) others (the physicians and the lawyers, Mgh) make a difference between these two terms. (Mgh, Msb.)

definition: , (S, Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb,) inf. n. tago$iyapN , (S,) I covered the thing; put a cover, or covering, upon it, or over it. (S, Msb.) One says, ga$~aY A@ll~`hu EalaY baSarihi , inf. n. as above; and ↓ Ag$Y ; (K, TA;) i. e. God put a covering upon, or over, his eyes. (TA.) And hence, (TA,) it is said in the Kur [xxxvi. 8], fahumo laA yuboSiruwna ↓ faA^ago$ayonaAhumo And we have put a covering over them [ so that they shall not see ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- [See a usage of the inf. n. voce $iynN .] ― -b3- g$~Ahu said of light; see 1, former half. ― -b4- See also 4. ― -b5- g$~Ahu biAls~awoTi : see 1, latter half. ― -b6- One says also, ga$~ayotuhu sayofFA , or sawoTFA , [in my original g$yth , without any syll. sign, but app. as I have written, for I do not find any instance of ga$iYa as doubly trans., meaning I equipped him with a sword, or a whip, ] like the saying kasawotuhu sayofFA , or Eam~amotuhu . (TA.)

definition: and ↓ g$~Ahu He made it to cover it;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ g$~Ahu He made it to cover it; or to be a cover, or covering, upon it, or over it. (MA, * TK, and Bd * and Jel * in vii. 52, &c.) ― -b2- And [hence,] both signify He made it, i. e. an event ( A^amor ), to come upon, [or invade, so as to surprise, or so as to overwhelm, properly meaning] as a thing that covered, him, or it. (K, * TA,) Both of these verbs are used in this sense in the Kur-án accord. to different readings in vii. 52 and xiii. 3, and likewise (as mentioned in the first paragraph of this art., q. v.,) in viii. 11. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, the former, He made him, or it, to come to him. (S, MA, TA.) ― -b4- See also 2, in two places. ― -b5- [Hence,] Ag$Y All~ayolu : see 1, former half.

sourceDefinition: : see ganiymapN , in three places. ― -b2- It signifies also [The regaining (as is shown by an explanation of A 'Obeyd cited in the first paragraph of art. glq ), and] the increase, and growth, and excess in value, of a pledge. (O in art. glq , and TA in the present art.) Thus in a trad., in which it is said, Alr~ahonu limano rahanahu lahu gunomuhu waEalayohi guromuhu [ The pledge pertains to him who pledged it; to him pertains the regaining of it, and its increase, and growth, and excess in value, if such there be, and upon him lies the obligation to pay the debt for it, without requiring any abatement thereof if the pledge have unavoidably suffered damage or total loss: see the explanation of A 'Obeyd mentioned above]. (TA.) Algunomu biAlguromi means The gunom is compensated ( muqaAbalN ) by the gurom [i. e. the regaining of the pledge, with the increase and the growth and the excess in value thereof if such there be, is compensated by the payment of the debt for it]; for like as the owner [of the pledge] is exclusively entitled to the gunom , no one sharing it with him, so he bears the gurom , no one bearing it with him: and this is the meaning of their saying, Alguromu majobuwrN biAlgunomi [which may therefore be rendered The loss suffered by the payment of the debt is repaired by the regaining of the pledge; app. a phrase of the lawyers, implying that such is to be considered as the case whatever be the state of the pledge at the time of its being restored unless it have suffered damage through the fault of the pledgee]. (Msb.) [See more in the first paragraph of art. glq .] ― -b3- See also gunaAmaAka . -A2- gnm [app. gunomN ] is mentioned by Suh as the name of A certain idol. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. $aA='N , (T, Msb, K,) meaning Sheep and goats; (Msb;) [and both together; ] a gen. n., (S, Msb, K,) of the fem. gender, (S, K,) applied to the males and the females, and to both together: (S, Msb, K:) it has no sing. from which it is derived, the sing. being $Ap : the dual ganamaAni is used as meaning two flocks or herds [ of sheep or of goats or of both together ]; (Msb, K;) each flock or herd having its distinct place of pasture and its pastor: (Msb, TA: *) and hence it is said in a trad. that the poor-rate [meaning a portion thereof] is to be given to him to whom the year of drought has left a ganam , but not to him to whom it has left ganamayoni : (TA:) the pl. is A^agonaAmN , (Msb, K,) [properly a pl. of pauc.,] sometimes used, (Msb,) meaning flocks or herds of ganam , (Msb and TA in art. Abl ,) and also gunuwmN and A^agaAnimu , (K,) the last used in an ode of Aboo-Jundab El-Hudhalee: (TA:) the dim. is ↓ gunayomapN , with p , because quasi-pl. ns. of the class having no sing. from which they are derived, when applied to what are not human beings, are constantly fem.; so one says xamosN mina Alganami *ukuwrN [ five of sheep, males ], making the n. of number fem., though one means rams, when it is followed by mina Alganami , for the n. of number is masc. and fem. accord. to the word, not accord. to the meaning. (S.) ― -b2- In the saying laA A=tiyka ganama Alfizori i. e. Hat~aY tajotamiEa ganamu Alfizori [ I will not come to thee until the sheep, or goats, of El-Fizr congregate ], gnm [with its complement] is made to stand in the place of Ald~ahor , [the meaning being, I will not come to thee ever, ] and is [therefore] put in the accus. case as though it were an adv. n. [of time]. (TA. [This saying with miEozaY in the place of ganama is mentioned by El-Meydánee in his “ Proverbs, ” and thus in the S and K in art. fzr . For an explanation of its origin see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 484.]) ― -b3- AlA^agonaAmu is the name of (assumed tropical:) Certain small stars between the legs of Cepheus and the star AljadoYu . (Kzw, in his descr. of Cepheus.) [See $aApN (in art. $wh ), last sentence.]
